MOVED BY: GUIRY
     SECONDED: HARDER

     THAT the Committee of the Whole extend public participation until 8:30 pm.

                                                                                               Motion CARRIED.

     Public Participation opened at 7:08 pm.

     First Time Speakers

     S. Rossander, Langford Resident - re: Item 5.1 - The speaker expressed concerns regarding the
     budget survey. The speaker expressed concern regarding potential tariffs.

     M. Wignall, Langford Resident - re: Item 5.1 - The speaker expressed appreciation for the action
     taken regarding bullying in Council Chambers. The speaker expressed concern regarding the final
     property tax amount. The speaker expressed concern regarding the Capital Regional District tax
     amount for water infrastructure added to the cost of property taxes.

     M. Morton, Langford Resident - re: Item 5.1 - The speaker expressed concerns regarding road
     lines, garbage and sidewalk projects being funded by Development Cost Charges.

     L.Foxall, Langford Resident - re: Item 5.1 - The speaker expressed concern regarding the
     property tax amount. The speaker urged that cost saving measures be explored. The speaker
     expressed concern regarding renovation funds for the flood restoration at City Hall not being
     used for the RCMP building expansion. The speaker expressed concern about Council managing
     large projects. The speaker expressed concern regarding the increase of property taxes in
     previous years.

     Second Time Speakers

     M. Morton, Langford Resident - re: Item 5.1 - The speaker expressed concern regarding the lack
     of sports facilities available. The speaker urged Council to take ownership of the budget.

     S. Rossander, Langford Resident - re: Item 5.1 - The speaker inquired if emails are going to be
     responded to. The speaker expressed appreciation of the frequently asked questions section of

the City's website that was available in years prior and inquired if the City would be willing to
make this tool available again on the City's website.

M. Wignall, Langford Resident - re: Item 5.1 - The speaker inquired about the discrepancy of the
2025 budget line-item amount reflected for the Woodlands Park purchase compared to what the
amount that was publicly stated.

M. Dillabaugh, Director of Finance, responded to the inquiry - The amount stated on the line
item in the budget is the actual BC Assessment value of the property and must be accounted for.
The amount paid was 9.8 million dollars and a tax receipt for 8 million dollars will be issued to
the sellers. 1 million will be put aside for purchases.

S. Perry, Langford Resident - re: Item 5.1 - The speaker expressed concern regarding the cost of
the sidewalk infill projects. The speaker inquired about future sports fields. The speaker
expressed concern regarding the lack of sports facilities.

A. Allen, Langford Resident - re: Item 5.1- The speaker inquired about the cost of the [-comm
911 fee being proposed by the Federal Government and why it was not accounted for in
previous budgets.

M. Dillabaugh, Director of Finance, responded to the inquiry - The [-comm 911 fee was not
accounted for as the City of Langford, in conjunction with nine other municipalities, have
continued to work with the Province of British Columbia to deter that charge.

L.Foxall, Langford Resident - re: Item 5.1 - The speaker inquired about future sidewalk infill
projects and the possible alignment to future development projects. The speaker suggested cost
cutting at the senior administration level.

Third Time Speakers

M. Wignall, Langford Resident - re: Item 5.1 - The speaker inquired about compacted gravel
being used as an interim measure for the sidewalk on Latoria.

L.Foxall, Langford Resident - re: Item 5.1 - The speaker inquired about the line item in the
budget for 2027 election costs.

M. Dillabaugh, Director of Finance, responded to the inquiry - There was a typo on the budget
line for elections on January 20, 2025, that was corrected January 27, 2025. The line item is for
the cost of an election in 2026.

D, Ferguson, Langford Resident - re: Item 5.1 - The speaker expressed concern regarding the
potential increase of property taxes. The speaker expressed concern regarding the survey. The
speaker expressed concern regarding the [-Comm 911 fee.

P. Hamilton, Langford Resident - re: Item 5.1 - The speaker expressed support for the proposed
budget. The speaker expressed support for the sidewalk infill projects.

M. Morton, Langford Resident - re: Item 5.1 - The speaker inquired about the sidewalk projects
being funded by Development Cost Charges.

K. Balzer, Director of Engineering and Public Works, responded to the inquiry - The sidewalk infill
program is funded by amenities, which are paid for by developers.

     J. Ralph, Langford Resident - re: Item 5.1 - The speaker requested that Council focuses on the
     needs, and not the wants regarding the budget. The speaker expressed concern regarding the
     lack of preparation of the potential E-Comm 911 fee. The speaker expressed concern regarding
     the survey. The speaker expressed concern regarding car and bike lane infrastructure.

     M. Wignall, Langford Resident - re: Item 5.1 - The speaker expressed support for amenities in
     Langford. The speaker expressed concern with how amenities will be paid for.

     Public Participation closed at 7:47 pm

     Staff provided clarification to the Committee regarding issues that were raised throughout the
     Public Participation period.

7.   ADJOURNMENT

5.   PUBLIC HEARINGS

     5.1   BYLAW NO. 2098

           "Langford Zoning Bylaw, Amendment No. 692, (2833, 2835, 2837, and 2839 Knotty Pine
           Road) Bylaw No. 2098, 2022."

           The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 2098 at 8:08 p.m.

           Director of Planning Matthew Baldwin adyised that Alex Gannochka of ADEPT
           Engineering Ltd. has applied on behalf of 829 Development Group Ltd. to rezone 2822,
           2835, 2837, and 2839 Knotty Pine Road from the One- and Two-Family Residential (R2)
           Zone to the City Centre 2 (CC2) Zone.

           This is being proposed in order to allow for the development of a townhouse project
           with approximately 26 units.

           Prior to Public Hearing, Council required the following items:

                   1. A technical memo from an engineer that verifies stormwater can be
                   adequately managed on-site for the proposed developments, to the satisfaction
                   of the Director of Engineering;

                   2. A memo prepared by a Landscape Architect that examines existing trees on
                   site and in the frontage and provides comment on the potential for tree
                   retention as part of the development plan, to the satisfaction of the Director of
                   Planning;

                   3.   A revised site plan to the satisfaction of the Director of Planning;

           The above items have all been completed and were considered and accepted by Council
           during their meeting held on February 6th, 2023. The revised site plan allows for three
           existing trees to be maintained and includes a dedication of 5% of the lot to the City.

In further support of this application, the applicant has agifeed to provide the following:

    1. That the applicant will provide the following contributions per unit, prior to the
        issuance of a building permit:

        1.   $1,000 towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund; and

        2. $3,800 towards the General Amenity Reserve|Fund.
    2. That the applicant provides, prior to Bylaw Adoption, a Section 219 covenant,
       registered in priority of all other charges on that title, that agrees:

        a. That the following be implemented to Bylaw No. 1000 standards to the
        satisfaction of the Director of Engineering prior to; the issuance of a building
        permit:

             1. Full frontage improvements, inclusive of sidewalks, bike lanes, road
             edge parking, streetlighting, and boulevard upgrades; and
             2.     A storm water management plan.

        b. That a Construction Park and Traffic Managennent Plan be provided to the
        satisfaction of the Director of Engineering prior to any alteration of land;

        c. That the four subject properties be consolidated prior to the issuance of a
        Development Permit for Form and Character;

        d. That a separate covenant be registered agreeing that the garages and
        carports are to be used for the parking of vehicles and not the storage of items
        preventing the parking of vehicles therein.

        e. That all concrete used on-site will be produced using post-industrial C02
        mineralization technology, or equivalent which offers concrete with lower
        embodied C02 than all other competing bids, and that prior to the issuance of a
        Building Permit the applicant shall provide a prodgct-specific Type III
        Environmental Product Declaration that is 3rd party verified specifying the total
        embodied carbon content of concrete.

        f. That 5% of the lot area be dedicated to the City at the southwest corner of
        the lot, inclusive of the Garry Oak and Bigleaf Maple trees, prior to the issuance
         of a building permit;

         g. That the tree protection measures outlined in the arborist report be
         implemented throughout construction to protectjthe Garry Oak, BigleafMaple,
         and Cypress trees that have retention potential, inclusive of tree protection
         fencing.

This proposal is consistent with the Official Community Plan City Centre designation.

Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by the Local
Government Act.

6.   PUBLIC HEARINGS

     6.1   BYLAW NO. 2009

           The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 2009 at 6:13 pm.

           Director of Planning Matthew Baldwin advised that Matthew Moradian has applied on
           behalf of Langford Central Developments Inc. to amend the zoning of 2739 to 2751
           Scafe Road and 2746 Peatt Road from the 'One-and Two-Family Residential' Zone to the
           'City Centre Pedestrian' Zone.

This is being proposed in order to allow for the development of 2 mixed-used buildings
that would be 18 and 24 storeys in height.

As part of this application, a public hearing is required in accordance with the
regulations of the Local Government Act.

In support of this application, the applicant has agreed to the following:

That as a bonus for increased density, the applicant will provide the following
contributions prior to issuance of a building permit:
1.   $750 towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund; and
2.   $2,850 toward the General Amenity Reserve Fund.
subject to reductions depending on use and height in accordance with the Affordable
Housing and Amenity Contribution Policy

The applicant will also provide $10.75 per square metre of commercial space towards
the General Amenity Reserve Fund prior to issuance of a building permit.

That prior to bylaw adoption, the applicant will register a section 219 covenant that
agrees to the following:

1. That full frontage improvements, a storm water management plan, and a
construction parking plan be provided and implemented to Bylaw 1000 standards to the
satisfaction of the Director of Engineering prior to issuance of building permit.
2. That all 6 properties associated with this rezoning be consolidated prior to issuance
of a Development Permit.
3. That onsite parking is allocated to each unit in accordance with the zoning bylaw.
4. That a strata plan is registered for each building prior to issuance of an occupancy
permit.
5. That 100% of the residential parking stalls are capable of providing Level 2 charging
for electric vehicles.

This proposal is consistent with the Official Community Plan 'City Centre' designation.

Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by the Local
Government Act.

The Mayor called a first time for presentations.

•   Matthew Moradian and Rachel Sansom provided a presentation on the proposed
    development on behalf of the applicant. The project would provide housing for 271
    families and commercial space in the centre of Langford, and is not requesting any
    variances. The project will be using carbon reduction technology in its concrete.
    Prices for homes will start under $400K.

•   Liisa Stewart - 2723 Peatt Road - Do not feel this development is reasonable for the
    neighbourhood. Have been negatively impacted by a four-storey development
    nearby and this would be worse. Support development of 4-6 stories.

•   Ryan Craycroft - 738 Walfred Road - Have 100+ employees, many of whom will not
    be able to get into the market without developments like this. Support this
    development, will house young families.

    Michael Biscoe - 2958 Sea Point Drive - Support this project.

    Resident - Willshire Drive - Some people are not able to find housing in Langford
    and have to commute.

    Matthew McKay- 780 Hockley Avenue - Support this development, support the job
    development and economic development created by this development. Many
    rental properties have a zero vacancy. We need more developments like this.
    People who live in dense areas are often able to walk to work and don't negatively
    impact traffic.

    Jacqueline Gintaut -1331 Ravensview Drive - Request that Council vote no to tall
    towers, which will set a negative precedent and compound existing traffic, parking,
    services, and infrastructure issues. There was not sufficient community consultation
    on this development or on the zoning bylaw that allowed developments of this
    height. Prefer a staged approach to development.

    Mary Wagner - 103-2669 Deville Road - Clarified that the carbon sequestering
    technology will be used in the concrete for this development. Do not support zones
    with no height limit, feel that the OCP needs more community input. Request more
    green space, would like the neighbourhood to be walkable.

•   David Fulko, 3035 Dorado Court - In favour of this development. Housing is needed
    right now, and it is better to go up than out, environmentally speaking. It is better
    to have more housing than prioritize traffic. It is appropriate to densify the city core,
    this will add energy, vibrancy, and support arts venues and local businesses. Taller
    buildings often have bigger setbacks and allow more space in the neighbourhood.

•   Anil Karim- Working with the developers to include quality child care within this
    development. The developers strongly support the effort to maximize equitable
    childcare spaces, which serve families who might not have access to quality
    childcare otherwise. Childcare is especially challenging for fast-growing cities, and
    this development is especially appropriate for childcare since it and Langford attract
    young families.

•   Robert Friend, 3024 Glen Lake Road - Employ 50 employees who live and work in
    Langford. Employees are getting pushed out of the city. Taller, dense projects are
    needed to support the growth in the city and families who want to stay in Langford.

•   Resident on 3207 Willshire Drive - Langford is a very fast-growing community. We
    need to house people and labour. People are sharing bedrooms and houses.
    Support this development.

•   Dana Elizabeth - 2850 Aldwynd Road - Support this project and density in the core.
    More homes will help facilitate growth, infrastructure, housing, and walkability.

•   Michael Sikich - 849 Homer Street - Will be marketing this development if it comes
    on the market. Langford is very desirable, which affects affordability. These tall,
    dense developments help address affordability and allow more people to achieve
    home ownership and a sense of pride and community. Taller developments reduce
    urban sprawl and allow more green space around the development.

•   Thai Tran - 2853 Crystal View Drive - Support this project for the affordability that it
    brings. Will set a positive precedent and make the downtown core more livable,
    walkable for young families.

•   Rosemary Turnowski - 837 Brock Avenue - This development would have a huge
    impact. Have worked hard for years to build a sense of community and get to know
    neighbours. Those in favour do not live near the proposed development, and it will
    affect the community. Will affect ability to garden, parking. Feel that this will blow
    up the community.

•   Bryce Wade - 19721 64th Avenue, Langley - Housing crisis requires projects like this.
    Thought he would never be able to afford housing in Vancouver, but working
    remotely will allow this. The only way to provide housing and avoid urban sprawl is
    to build up like this. This project is important for our community and economy.

•   Morgan Petrovic - 309-2717 Peatt Road - Will be impacted by the project since it is
    nearby, but fully support it. Despite potential annoyances, don't think the
    difficulties will be as bad as many believe. Think this will bring jobs for construction,
    local businesses. The centre of communities should grow, and Langford will become
    a bigger city.

•   Jackie Sheridan -1005 Golden Spire Crescent - Concerned about the height of the
    proposal and believe there may be issues with infrastructure for buildings over 6
    stories

              Mayor Young left the meeting at 7:17 pm.

•   Jackie Sheridan -1005 Golden Spire Crescent - believe that these will not allow
    young families to enter the housing market since all housing is unaffordable now.
    These buildings are not eco-friendly.

•   Layne Britton - 3022 Shoreview Drive - Support this project, it is vital for the
    downtown Langford core.

              Mayor Young returned to the meeting at 7:19 pm.

•   Layne Britton continued - Langford has become one of the most desirable places to
    live, and do not think this will negatively impact traffic and parking.

•   Mike, 953 Glen Willow Place - Support this project, this is more environmentally-
    friendly than urban sprawl. High-rise buildings are more energy-efficient than other
    developments. Love the plans.

•   Nicole Simpson - 4111 Mariposa Heights - Support this development. There is a
    housing crisis, and we need the hundreds of homes that would be provided by this
    development. Grew up in Langford and have watched it grow. Support Mayor and
    Council's vision.

•   Yazmin Hernandez - 2634 Sunderland Road - Sunderland Road - Feel the
    conversation about this development should not be about ''projects like these" but
    about this specific development, how it works in the context of the neighbourhood,
    and the merits of the proposal itself. There are not enough amenities like rapid

    transit and bike lanes. The ground floor should be active and dynannic instead of
    multiple levels of parking. Appreciate what Langford is doing to provide housing but
    feel that it is enough without this development.

•   Glen Kakoske -1715 Coronation Avenue - Joined out of interest and have no
    comments tonight.

    Isaac Mann - 2747 Scafe Road - A recent graduate and hoping to enter the market in
    a few years. In full support of this project. These units will be more affordable than
    other markets. Support the sustainable aspects of this development, like building
    vertically. Feel that concerns about traffic, fronting, shading have all been
    addressed by the proponents. Need to bring in and keep younger generations to
    communities in order to develop community amenities.

    Chris Newstead - 2732 Scafe Road - Request that Council not approve this
    development. 271 new units is six times the residences currently on the whole
    street. Traffic and parking are already bad and this will make it far worse. Less traffic
    per residence doesn't matter when overall the traffic will be far worse. Not enough
    parking for the number of units built. There will likely be overflow parking on the
    street. Neighbourhood is currently 1-2 storey homes. A 20+ story building will be
    incredibly out of place. Concerned about negative impacts to lifestyle, noise and
    privacy. Feel Council should prioritize existing residents over development.

•   Susie Hicks -2345 Lake End - Agree with previous callers who have voiced concerns
    with parking and traffic. Traffic to downtown Victoria is terrible. Feel there is not
    enough infrastructure, such as doctors, police, fire and ambulance to support
    current residents. Construction jobs will go away and Langford will be left with low-
    paying jobs. People will continue to have to commute to Victoria.

•   Laurie Plomp - 3592 Whimfield Terrace - Oppose development. This neighbourhood
    is not a good fit for tall towers. Parking ratio is insufficient and will contribute to
    conflict in neighbourhood. Traffic Impact Assessment should be provided to
    residents. More consultation with residents should be required, especially in
    developing greenspace. Request that the public hearing be adjourned until the
    greenspace is better developed.

•   Jordan Goldsmith - 3030 Washington Avenue - Grew up in Langford and have a lot
    of peers who are struggling to find housing. Fully support an opportunity for more
    young people to get into homes.

    Elizabeth Markus - 3262 Zapata Place - Ask Council to vote against this
    development. Council must do more community engagement to understand the
    vision of residents. Residents may not want Langford to become a more urban city.
    Residents have been left out of the process. This will forever change the character
    of Langford. Do not believe this development is environmentally-friendly. Feel high
    density and more environmentally-friendly developments can be achieved in 10-12
    storey buildings.

    Kim Robinson - 960B Paige Avenue - Agree with everyone who opposes this project.
    Do not agree 24 stories is appropriate for this neighbourhood. 10 stories would be
    more appropriate. Feel that residents will have no say once it is built.

      Mayor Young called a second time for presentations.

      None.

      the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 2009 closed at 7:51 p.m.

6.2   BYLAW NO. 2008


      The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 2008 at 7:51 pm.

      Director of Planning Matthew Baldwin advised that Matthew Moradian has applied on
      behalf of Langford Gateway Developments to amend the zoning of 2633 to 2647
      Sunderland Road, 808 to 820 Arncote Road, and 2630 to 2646 Peatt Road from the
      'One-and Two-Family Residential' Zone to the 'City Centre Pedestrian' Zone.

      This is being proposed in order to allow for the development of 4 mixed-used buildings
      that would range in height from 13 to 22 storeys.

      As part of this application, a public hearing is required in accordance with the
      regulations of the Local Government Act.

      In support of this application, the applicant has agreed to the following:

      That as a bonus for increased density, the applicant will provide the following
      contributions prior to issuance of a building permit:
      1. $750 towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund; and
      2. $2,850 toward the General Amenity Reserve Fund.
      subject to reductions depending on use and height in accordance with the Affordable
      Housing and Amenity Contribution Policy

      The applicant will also provide $10.75 per square metre of commercial space towards
      the General Amenity Reserve Fund prior to issuance of a building permit.

      That prior to bylaw adoption, the applicant will register a section 219 covenant that
      agrees to the following:

      1. That full frontage improvements, recommendations from the associated Traffic
      Impact Assessment, a storm water management plan, and a construction parking plan
      be provided and implemented to Bylaw 1000 standards to the satisfaction of the
      Director of Engineering prior to issuance of building permit.
      2. That all 11 properties associated with this rezoning be consolidated prior to
      issuance of a Development Permit.
      3. That onsite parking is allocated to each unit in accordance with the zoning bylaw.
      4. That a strata plan is registered for each building prior to issuance of an occupancy
      permit.
      5. That 100% of the residential parking stalls are capable of providing Level 2 charging
      for electric vehicles.

      This proposal is consistent with the Official Community Plan 'City Centre' designation.

      Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by the Local
      Government Act.

The Mayor called a first time for presentations.

•   Matthew Moradian and Rachel Sansom on behalf of Langford Gateway
    Developments.

           Councillor Blackwell left the meeting at 7:54 pm.

    Matthew Moradian and Rachel Sansom continued - This project will provide housing
    for 444 families on just over 2 acres of land and will provide 11 500 square feet of
    commercial and daycare space. Will provide approximately $2.6 million in park and
    amenity contributions and is requesting no variances. Housing 444 families in single
    family homes would require 111 acres of land.

           Councillor Blackwell returned to the meeting at 7:58 pm.

    Anais Holdaway -101-827 Arncote Avenue - Oppose this development. There was
    no meaningful engagement with area residents; don't feel residents were heard.
    Planning for people to behave differently (e.g. cycle or use transit) is not
    reasonable. Majority of people who live in this area work in Victoria and traffic is
    already bad. Appreciate that there will be daycare spots but would like to hear how
    many spaces will be available. This number of units may make the childcare
    situation worse. Would like Council to represent its residents.

    Yazmin Hernandez - 2634 Sunderland Road - Traffic Impact Assessments will never
    indicate a development is not appropriate, but this development will increase traffic
    and is inappropriate. 2.5 metre setbacks are minimal for a development of this size.
    Walkability only increases when amenities are provided and pedestrians are
    prioritized over vehicles. Most units will be 1-2 bedrooms, so this will not build the
    neighbourhood.

           Councillor Wade left the meeting at 8:16 pm.

    Tim Revino -101-1663 MacKenzie Ave - Have planning and density, and know
    people who are currently sharing small units with 5+ roommates and bunkbeds in
    each room. We need more density and housing right now. Fully support this project.

           Councillor Wade returned to the meeting at 8:19 pm

•   Matthew McKay - 784 Hockley Avenue - This is an exciting development, could be
    improved by a public plaza and public art. An art walk would be a great addition to
    Langford.

•   Jacqueline Gintaut -1331 Ravensview Drive - Agree with first two callers.

           Councillor Seaton left the meeting at 8:21 pm.

•   Jacqueline Gintaut continued - Request that Council vote no to tall towers, which
    will set a negative precedent and compound existing traffic, parking, services, and
    infrastructure issues. There was not sufficient community consultation on this
    development or on the zoning bylaw that allowed developments of this height.
    Prefer a staged approach to development.

             Councillor Seaton returned to the meeting at 8:24 pm. Mayor Young left the
                 meeting at 8:24 pm.

             Mayor Young returned to the meeting at 8:26 pm.

•   Mary Wagner -103-2669 Deville Road - Suggest having a significant plaza or corner
    greenspace area. Think that we can build greener and better. Current infrastructure
    such as medical services are not sufficient. Agree that childcare spaces may not be
    sufficient for the new residents in the development. Storm water is an issue.
    Requested shadow study but this was not requested by the City or supplied by the
    developer. Believe this is too much change too fast for this neighbourhood.

•   Michael Biscoe - 2958 Seapoint Drive - Support this development. First time
    homeowner with older parents, and this development would meet all the family's
    needs.

•   Warren Grey -15195 36th Ave Surrey, BC - Would like to move to Langford, support
    this project.

•   Dana Elizabeth - 2850 Aldwynd Road - Would like to thank Council for supporting
    high density housing. We desperately need more housing options since we are in a
    housing crisis. Support the height and density. Know people who have had to buy in
    Mill Bay, Sooke and Duncan; this will help people stay in Langford.

•   Darlene Oudot - 105-827 Arncote Avenue - Invite Council to come to the
    neighbourhood to see how traffic is in the neighbourhood. When a detour was in
    place recently, it was nearly impossible to get out of the neighbourhood by car.
    There are already traffic issues and this will make it worse. Question the quality of
    this housing.

•   Andy Kading - 3257 Doncaster Drive - Represent Watt Consulting Group, which
    completed the traffic impact assessment. The TIA used the gold standard of
    methodologies, which includes 40 years of study and best practice

•   Wendy Hobbs - 3442 Luxton Road - Support the callers who are saying that there
    are not enough services and infrastructure. Municipalities of the future need to
    develop a community, not just apartments. There are not enough schools, fire
    services, or police. Langford should put a hold on development until further
    planning is done for fire services. Mutual aid is not enough.

•   Andrew Fox - 2634 Sunderland Road - Question the rosy picture that developers are
    painting. Concerns about number of childcare spots and traffic. The amenities and
    infrastructure aren't present for this development. This will download the burden of
    responsible planning to residents. It's offensive that you're considering this.

•   Acting Director of Corporate Services Marie Watmough - there will be
    approximately 85 childcare spots

•   Laurie Plomp - 3592 Whimfield Terrace - The density will strongly impact the
    neighbourhood. Council should listen to neighbourhood residents. Although the
    project was initiated in 2019, it was not discussed with local residents until recently
    this year. Residents should be involved from the beginning of such a project.

      •   Isaac Mann - 2747 Scafe Road - Support this project. A lot of the issues brought up
          have been resolved. Some speakers are arguing in favour of stagnicity. We can't get
          the amenities we want without growing the city. Amenities come with density and
          growing the local economy.

      •   Ryan Craycroft - 738 Walfred Road - This development will help address
          infrastructure issues by providing more tax dollars. Support this development.

      Mayor Young called a second time for presentations.

      •   Jason Mackenzie - 996 Cavalcade Terrace - Council should listen to current residents
          and build appropriate density, not necessarily high density. Request that Council
          reject the application.

      •   Acting Director of Corporate Services Marie Watmough - Correction, there is the
          possibility of 300-400 daycare spots.

      Mayor Young called a third and final time for speakers. There being none, he declared
      the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 2008 closed at 8:52 p.m.

6.3   BYLAW NO. 1992

      The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1992 at 8:52 pm.

      Director of Planning Matthew Baldwin advised that City of Langford staff have applied
      on behalf of City of Langford to amend the Zoning Bylaw No. 300 by updating the
      definitions for ''suites'' and "kitchens", adding a new definition for "public assembly and
      entertainment use", and refining Part 2 for enforceability purposes. These changes were
      initially left out of the spring omnibus (Bylaw 1944) while City Staff collaborated to
      ensure that Council and Departmental desires were incorporated.

      Bylaw 1992 proposes changes to Zoning Bylaw No. 300 Part 1 Definitions and Part 2
      General Provisions to allow for increased usability, education and enforcement of the
      Zoning Bylaw No. 300 for City Staff and the general public.

      As part of this application, a public hearing is required in accordance with the
      regulations of the Local Government Act.

      This proposal is consistent with the Official Community Plan

      Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by the Local
      Government Act.

      None.

      Mayor Young called a second time for presentations.

      None.

      Mayor Young called a third and final time for speakers. There being none, he declared
      the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1992 closed at 8:52 p.m.

6.4   BYLAW NO. 1931


The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1931 at 8:53 pm.

Director of Planning Matthew Baldwin advised that The City of Langford has applied to
annend the zoning of 1365 Goldstreann Avenue from the AM (Amenity) Zone to Area 5 -
Multi-Family of the CDl (Comprehensive Development 1 - Goldstream Meadows) Zone.

This is being proposed in order to allow for the development of a 6-storey multi-family
building.

As part of this application, a public hearing is required in accordance with the
regulations of the Local Government Act.

In support of these/this application, the applicant has agreed to provide the following:

1. That the applicant provides, as a bonus for increased density, the following
contributions per residential unit, prior to the issuance of a building permit:
a) $610 towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund; and
b) $3,660 towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund.
Subject to reductions depending on the use and height in accordance with the
Affordable Housing and Amenity Contribution Policy.

2. That the applicant provides, prior to bylaw adoption, a Section 219 covenant,
registered in priority of all other charges on title, that agrees to the following:
a) That parking stalls are allocated to individual units and visitors as required by the
Zoning Bylaw;
b) That a strata plan of the building is registered prior to occupancy;
c) That residential parking stalls are provided with Level 2 charging capabilities;
d) That the following are provided to Bylaw No. 1000 standards to the satisfaction of
the Director of Engineering prior to the issuance of a Building Permit:
i. Frontage improvements;
ii. A storm water management plan; and
iii. A construction parking and traffic management plan;

The applicant has provided a stormwater management memo, to the satisfaction of the
Director of Engineering, as required by Council.

The applicant has furthermore committed to providing 30% of the units in the proposed
development for sale through the City's new Attainable Home Ownership Program.

This proposal is consistent with the Official Community Plan Mixed Use Employment
Centre designation.

Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by the Local
Government Act

The Mayor called a first time for presentations.

•   Mary Wagner -104-2669 Deville Road - This will negatively impact the nearby trails.
    Any time the City gives up land, it has lost an opportunity to provide an amenity
    that benefits the entire community. This development will affect drainage and
    cause soil erosion. Even dead trees help absorb water. Request that Council make
    2885 area a dedicated park.


    Laurie Plomp - 3592 Whimfieid Terrace - There is a discrepancy in the provided
    information. Advertisements say that there is one building, but the staff report says

    develop this property, so it is disappointing that there was no public engagement.
    The transit for this area is not sufficient for the number of units. There is not
    enough information about the proposed design.

    Director of Planning and Subdivision Matthew Baldwin - Clarified that the public
    hearing is for a rezoning and details about the proposed building are not required at
    this time.

    Jacqueline Gintaut -1331 Ravensview Drive - Concerned that the number of
    buildings is different in the advertisement and the staff report. Concerned about
    traffic, parking and lack of meaningful community consultation. Previous
    correspondence for a previous proposal for this property was not included on the
    agenda. Suggest that the development creates units that are not affordable or
    attainable. The attainable housing program will only be available to a very small
    number of residents with a relatively high income. This development will not
    benefit Langford residents.

    Suzanne Goudge - 2807 Lakeshore Place - Support green developments and density,

    development will threaten the natural environment. The location has low
    walkability and has limited bus service, and will require people to drive. Location is
    on a dead-end road. With density, more density and greenspace is needed.

    Cindy Hickson - Lake End Road - Request that Council not approve this rezoning.
    Biggest concern is more traffic on a dead-end road. Already too much traffic and not
    enough parking. Concerned that new multi-use path is not safe. There is run-off
    from roads into the lake. This will cause more run-off and pollute the wetlands and

    Teresa Ackroyd, 325 Renart Place - Agree with previous speakers that this property

    unpleasant place to live.

Mayor Young called a second time for presentations.

•   Karnal Cheema -102-792 Revilo Place - Moved to Langford to be closer to

    Brian Beltcher -1231 Goldstream Ave - Oppose this development. Feel that the

           and enhanced rather than sold. Residents would like more inclusion in the

           Jacqueline Gintaut -1331 Ravensview Drive - Agree with previous caller, and feel
           that the petition should be considered as part of this development process. More
           greenspace is needed.

           Suzanne Goudge - 2807 Lakeshore Place - It is inappropriate to put a 6-storey
           building next to greenspace. Residents are concerned and ask for Council to listen

           Sienna Geary - 1375 Bear Mountain Parkway - Request that Council listen to the

           Mayor Young stated that the property was intended as either a highway

           Jacqueline Gintaut -1331 Ravensview Drive - Feel that Council is not listening to

      •    Dana Elizabeth - 2850 Aldwynd Road - Support the rezoning of this property. This

6.5   BYLAW NO. 2004

      The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 2004 at 9:35 pm.

      Director of Planning Matthew Baldwin advised that Ron Coutre has applied on behalf of
      0797731 BC Ltd., Ryan Craycroft, and Brian & Charlene Semple to amend the zoning of
      3429, 3431, and 3433 Luxton Road, and 3436 Hazelwood Road from the 'Rural
      Residential T, 'Rural Residential 2', and 'Rural Residential 5' Zones to the 'One- and
      Two-Family Residential' and the 'Residential Townhouse T Zones.

      This is being proposed in order to allow for the development of 11 single-family
      dwellings and 60 townhouse dwellings.

      As part of this application, a public hearing is required in accordance with the
      regulations of the Local Government Act.

      In support of this application, the applicant has agreed to the following:
      That as a bonus for increased density, the applicant will provide the following
      contributions per single-family dwelling prior to subdivision:
      1.   $1,000 towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund; and
      2.   $6,000 toward the General Amenity Reserve Fund.
      That as a bonus for increased density, the applicant will provide the following
      contributions per townhouse dwelling prior to building permit:


1. $610 towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund; and
2. $3,660 toward the General Amenity Reserve Fund.

That prior to bylaw adoption, the applicant will register a section 219 covenant that
agrees to the following:
1. That full frontage improvements, a storm water management plan, and a
construction parking plan be provided and implemented to Bylaw 1000 standards to the
satisfaction of the Director of Engineering prior to subdivision approval for the single-
family dwellings, or prior to building permit for the townhouse dwellings.
2. That 0.387 hectares of land immediately west of the single-family lots be dedicated
as Park at the time of subdivision.
3.   That a Statutory Right of Way be registered on the townhouse site to allow the City
access to the future Park.
4. That an easement for a sewer force main be registered over the single-family side of
development, in favour of the townhouse side.
5. That the townhomes abutting the rear property lines of 3413-3425 Luxton Road be
limited in height to 2-storeys.
6. That a playground area, approximately 320m^ in size be provided within the
townhouse side of development.
7. That the full amount of General Amenity Contribution from the townhouse side be
secured prior to issuance of the first building permit and used to complete the sidewalk
along the eastern side of Luxton Road north of this site.
8. That future home owners are notified of the potential nuisances that may arise
from surround land uses, specially those uses related to agriculture and from that South
Vancouver Island Rangers gun range.
9. That future home owners are notified that garages are to be used for off-street
parking and not storage that prevents parking.
This proposal is consistent with the Official Community Plan 'Neighbourhood'
designation.
Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by the Local
Government Act.



The Mayor called a first time for presentations.

•    Ron Coutre - 205-847 Goldstream Avenue - There is a housing crisis. This is a family-
     oriented townhome project that will include a full environmental assessment. While
     residents may prefer no development at all, most seemed amenable to the type of
     development proposed, and at least one resident supports it.

•    Matthew McKay - 784 Hockley Avenue - Support this development, appreciate the
     greenery and separation between units.

•    George Weatherall - 925 Latoria Road - Fully support this project, think it would be a
     nice addition to the area.

•    Morgan Petrovic - 309-2717 Peatt Road - Fully support this rezoning. The developer
     has found a good balance between good homes and an affordable development.
     There is decent greenspace and all of the issues that have come up have been
     addressed.


           •   Chris Tysol - 2934 Robalee Place - Rent in Langford and would like to purchase.
               Developments like this are a good opportunity to get into the market.

           •   Wendy Hobbs - 3442 Luxton Road - Not speaking against the development, but have
               concerns that it is in a 200-year floodplain. Hope that the City will ensure this will be
               built to withstand flooding. Do not support density on a floodplain. Traffic on Luxton
               Road is already busy with pedestrian traffic. Request that the sidewalk will be
               extended. Concerned that there will be a covenant that residents cannot complain
               about existing uses, and that there is not adequate fire service on that side of
               Langford.

           •   Brody Coulter -1121 Lipincott Road - Support this project, happy to have more
               family-friendly housing.

                      Mayor Young left the meeting at 9:52 pm.

           •   Michael Harris - 953 Glen Willow Place - Fully support this development.

           •   Steve Webber - 3437 Luxton Road - Concerned about flooding. Luxton Road was
               closed on Monday due to flooding from Firehall Creek.

                      Mayor Young returned to the meeting at 9:54 pm.

           •   Steve Webber continued - Request that there be a plan to address flooding. Would
               like there to be one less townhouse, and more parking added.

           •   Colby Messer - 2149 Triangle Trail - Support this development, appreciate the
               greenspace in the plan. Feel it would improve what's there now.

           Mayor Young called a second time for presentations.

           Mayor Young called a third and final time for speakers. There being none, he declared
           the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 2004 closed at 9:56 p.m.

motions.source_motion_text:
WHEREAS municipal governments, often on the front lines, bear the brunt of
        addressing shared crises such as climate issues, housing affordability, inequality,
        public health, and infrastructure challenges;

        WHEREAS the burden on municipalities has intensified due to Provincial
        shortcomings in fulfilling their responsibilities, leaving many municipalities
        grappling with insufficient revenue sources, resulting in an overreliance on
        regressive property taxation;

        THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT the Association of Vancouver Island and
        Coastal Communities (AVICC) urges the Province to promptly fulfill its
        responsibilities in providing health care, including mental health care, as well as

        social services and the management of criminal rehabilitation through
        correctional facilities.

        FURTHER BE IT RESOLVED THAT, in the absence of immediate Provincial action,
        the AVICC advocates for a comprehensive and immediate review of municipal
        taxation and revenue sources. This recognizes the pivotal role of municipalities,
        which, despite these being Provincial responsibilities, are left to deal with the
        repercussions without adequate support from the Province.

5.   PUBLIC HEARINGS

     5.1   BYLAW NO. 2126

           "Omnibus No. 61 - Part 3: Unlicensed Vehicles and Institutional Fencing), Bylaw No.
           2126, 2023".

           The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 2126 at 7:46 p.m.

           Director of Planning Matthew Baldwin advised that staff are bringing forward Bylaw No.
           2126 which proposes the following amendments to Zoning Bylaw No. 300:
           • Amend the wording within Zoning Bylaw 300 by adding ''unlicensed vehicle" to the list
           of definitions; and
           • Exclude institutional developments from the maximum fence height requirements of
           Zoning Bylaw 300.
           These are proposed to reflect a change in ICBC licensing practices and to give
           institutional uses more flexibility in their specific fencing needs.
           The proposed amendments would be consistent with the City's Official Community Plan.
           Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by the Local
           Government Act.

           Mayor Goodmanson called a first time for presentations.

           None presented.

11.   NOTICE OF MOTION

      Councillor Harder introduced the following Notice of Motion:

      WHEREAS the City of Langford is developing a comprehensive Economic Strategy and has earned
      a reputation as a forward-thinking and innovative City, known for its ability to efficiently navigate
      bureaucratic processes to attract business investment;
      AND WHEREAS the City of Langford currently does not permit existing business and commercial
      uses such as, "Pet Grooming" and "Bakery", as permitted uses in Business Park/Wholesale Zones
      and Commercial Zones;
      THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT Council direct staff to:
      1) review the permitted uses of all Business Park and Commercial Zones for clarity and
      consistency to support opportunities to attract and retain a diverse base of local businesses and
      to encourage broader Economic Development; and
      2) prepare a bylaw to amend Zoning Bylaw No. 300 as needed to ensure that "Pet Grooming"
      and "Bakery" business uses are permitted in all Business Park/Wholesale Zones and Commercial
      Zones.

WHEREAS the City of Langford recognizes the importance of safety and
                     compliance to the Motor Vehicle Act for all road users and;

                     WHEREAS the discontinuation of vehicle licence plate validation decals in British
                     Columbia has negatively impacted law enforcement officers in their ability to
                     detect and enforce uninsured motor vehicle violations:

                     THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that the AVICC and UBCM petition to the Province
                     and ICBC to provide municipalities and police agencies with the required funds
                     to procure Automated Licence Plate Recognition (ALPR) hardware for all law
                     enforcement vehicles in British Columbia.

                     SECONDED: SZPAK

                     Columbia has negatively impacted law enforcement officers in their ability to
                     detect and enforce uninsured motor vehicle violations:

                     THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that the AVICC and UBCM petition to the Province
                     and ICBC to provide municipalities and police agencies with the required funds
                     to procure Automated Licence Plate Recognition (ALPR) hardware for all law

MOVED BY: GUIRY
       SECONDED: HARDER

       THAT the Committee approve the agenda as presented.

5.   PRESENTATIONS

     5.1     Presentation of Proposed 2024-2028 Five Year Financial Plan and Related Matters

             M. Dillabaugh, Director of Finance; presented a short update. B. Hutchins, Director of
             Corporate Services, presented information regarding the YMCA and Pacific Football Club.

6.   PUBLIC PARTICIPATION

     T.L. Renken-Sebastian Jacklin/Orono - The speaker inquired about Fire Rescue initiatives. The
     speaker inquired about RCMP expenditures. The speaker inquired about the relationship
     between community resources and the Bylaw department regarding the unhoused people
     health and wellness. The speaker inquired about the consequences of not having new hires.

     Chief C. Aubrey responded - That at this time the Fire Department does not have budget
     requirements for new apparatus or vehicles. The Fire Department does explore grants or
     repurposing vehicles before purchasing new.

     Insp. S. Rose, West Shore RCMP responded - That the RCMP collaborates with other agencies,
     not for profits and other provincial agencies to deliver services they provide.

     L.Fletcher, Manager Community Safety and Municipal Enforcement responded - That the Bylaw
     Enforcement Department is engaging in specific training for officers with respect to unhoused,
     mental health issues. That they work with the RCMP to do wellness checks. Housing is a
     provincial mandated position, and the City has limited scope and ability to be involved.

     M. Morton, Phelps Ave -The speaker expressed concern about a tax increase. The speaker
     inquired about the travel budget increasing. The speaker expressed concern about the lack of
     information regarding the need to support the YMCA. The speaker expressed concern regarding
     the cost of consultants. The speaker expressed concern regarding the increase of the cost of the
     event line item. The speaker expressed concern regarding the cost of using the Trolley for a
     library.

     M. Dillabaugh, Director of Finance responded - Clarified that the travel budget from the Covid
     years was minimal travel. The addition of inflation has increased cost. They encouraged the
     resident to look through years 2019 and prior for better clarification. The events budget increase
     does not affect property tax increases. The use of consultants was for clarification of required
     departmental plans for the Council's strategic plan. The City is probably the only municipality
     that doesn't have a transportation plan, parks master plan, updated Official Community Plan. All
     of these cost money, more efficient to contract versus hiring permanent employees when its not
     a yearly process. They stated again that these costs do not affect taxation.

     M. Wignall, Selwyn Rd - The speaker expressed concern regarding the cost of stadium seating.
     The speaker inquired if design build proposals would be an option. The speaker inquired about
     travel expenses; would virtual attendance be an option. The speaker inquired whether the cost
     for proposed upcoming plans could be spread out over time.

     M. Dillabaugh, Director of Finance responded - They clarified that proposed department plans
     are being funded by surplus, not property taxation. Spreading it out would likely not make a
     difference. They also stated that the travel budget is being reduced in 2024 compared to 2023.

S. Rossander, Langford Resident - The speaker expressed gratitude that there is a plan of the
possibility of the purchase of YMCA. The speaker inquired when the public could access the
actuals for revenues and expenditures for the City. The speaker inquired about having some
details regarding the line item FA08 admin property purchase for the 2024 capital budget. The
speaker inquired having the 2023 operating reports for YMCA public.

M. Dillabaugh, Director of Finance responded - That the budget is earlier this year, 2023 actuals
are not ready yet. They will meet the deadline of May 15, 2024. The current 5-year plan includes
purchase of YMCA. They cannot disclose anything further on land acquisition as it is in camera.
He also encouraged residents to go through the FOI process for further records.

S. Sifert, Langford Resident - The speaker inquired for clarification on when year end is. The
speaker inquired about a tax decrease with the RCMP building removal. The speaker expressed
concern regarding the travel budget. The speaker expressed concern regarding consultant fees.

M. Dillabaugh, Director Of Finance responded - They clarified the City is on a fiscal calendar year.
That the RCMP expansion, the potential purchase of YMCA and asset management, was in last
years 2023 budget plan. The tax increase was over a few years. Each year has a reduction of
1.75% with the removal of the RCMP building expansion.

L. Foxall, Langford Resident - The speaker expressed concern about a tax increase. The speaker
suggested travel budget cost cuts by attending conferences electronically. The speaker expressed
concern about the new proposed projects and the lack of information about them. The speaker
expressed concern regarding the tax increase and the effect on renters. The speaker expressed
concern about saving the Pacific Football Club without a referendum.

Councillor C. Harder - point of order - all speakers should speak through the chair.

R. Louie, Langford Resident - The speaker would like to see a property tax decrease. The speaker
expressed concern about the tax increase effecting renters. The speaker inquired about the
trolley being used for a library, The speaker inquired if it could be a grant program. The speaker
inquired about the removal of either the proposed ebike program or compost program.

C. Legacy, Artesian Crt- The speaker was in favour of increasing the function general amenity
fund. The speaker expressed gratitude regarding the resurfacing of the Centennial Park tennis
courts and would like to see more added in future.

N. Johal, Langford Resident - The speakers inquired about having enough RCMP officers. The
speaker expressed concern regarding the proposed ebike program. The speaker expressed
concern regarding the increase of property taxes.

M. Dillabaugh, Director of Finance responded - That the 2024 budget will include the addition of •
3 officers to maintain cop to pop ratio. 5 officers were originally requested, which may be a part
of Councils deliberation.

L. Plomp, Whimfield Terr - The speaker expressed concern about the details of the new budget
items. The speaker offered support for community gardens. The speaker noted that property
taxes are still one of the lowest in region, along with inclusion of hiring Firefighters, RCMP
Officers, and City staff. The speaker expressed gratitude for using the amenity funds for
amenities, instead of lowering taxes.

M. Brooke, Langford Resident - The speaker expressed concern about tax increase and the effect
on renters. The speaker expressed concern about playing catch-up from previous years of low
increases.

Greg, Florence Lake Rd - The speaker expressed concern about tax increase and the effect on
rental increases.

Mayor Goodmanson called for second time speakers:

T.L. Renken-Sebastian, Jacklin/Orono - The speaker spoke in favour of the funding of the HR
consultants in regard to inclusion, diversity, equity and accessibility at City Hall.

L.Foxall, Langford Resident - The speaker expressed concern about consultant fees. The speaker
expressed concern about a tax increase. The speaker expressed concern regarding where the16
million from province will go, why it's not in the financial plan. The speaker also expressed
concern about suing the provincial government.

M. Dillabaugh, Director of Finance responded - Master plans costs are included in budget but
through grant funding or surplus. If we removed or deferred any of the projects, it would not
decrease taxes.

M. Morton, Langford Resident - The speaker inquired where does surplus come from.

M. Dillabaugh, Director of Finance responded - Generated by municipalities, retained earnings
when revenues exceed expenses. Municipality has over 600 million dollars of assets. Noted the
organization must have some surplus. Using some of that surplus to pay for some projects and
plans, for example the Catholic church at Royal Roads University. No surplus = raised taxes for
those projects. Surplus allows us to offset, and smooth out tax increase from year to year.
Money sits at surplus before spending in a future year.

A. Rossander, Langford Resident - The speaker expressed concern about the tax increase. The
speaker stated that the City should look at all possible ways to lower taxes.

B.Sahlstrom, Walfred Rd - The speaker requested some clarification on the purchase of the
YMCA. The speaker expressed concern regarding the price and whether residents get a vote in
how the money is spent.

M. Dillabaugh, Director of Finance responded - Anything the City buys becomes an asset of the
municipality, all land acquisitions is in camera and kept confidential.

D. James, Dornier Rd - The speaker expressed concern about purchase of YMCA. The speaker
spoke in favour of the ebike grant. The speaker is not in support of free libraries. The speaks
stated there are already enough free libraries. The speaker stated they would like the ebike
program expanded instead. Less cars on road equals less road maintenance.

M. Dillabaugh, Director of Finance responded - They encouraged the caller to watch the meeting
video for earlier clarification on YMCA.

S. Sifert, Langford Resident - The speaker expressed concern about spending emergency funds
on plans. The speaker stated they don't agree the City should be paying for consultants. The
speaker is concerned about having a referendum for the stadium. The speaker stated there
should have been a referendum for purchasing the YMCA. The speaker is concerned about the

budget amount for the Royal Roads University. The speaker expressed concern regarding the
proposed ebike program.

B. Hutchins, Director of Corporate Services responded - That in 2019 the Council made a
commitment to the Province. The funding is to be used to attract businesses and residents to the
downtown core.

Nicholas Johal, Walfred Rd - The speaker inquired whether they are local or travel to assist with
the budget. The speaker expressed concern regarding the cost of not using local consultants.

M. Dillabaugh, Director of Finance responded -There will be a selection process for hiring
consultants, he cannot say whether they are local or not as they are not hired yet and is subject
to budget approval.

R, Louie, Langford Resident - The speaker stated they would like to look at rebates in general
versus ebikes only. The speaker expressed opposition to community garden to decrease taxes.

N.Johal, Langford Resident - The speaker expressed concern regarding ebike safety and fires.
The speaker inquired about the cost of Mayor Goodmanson's desk. The speaker inquired if Chief
Aubrey would support ebikes in the budget due to known fires.

Mayor Goodmanson responded - The item was on sale, does not have exact price.

M. Dillabaugh, Director of Finance responded - That the desk price information can be obtained
from the Freedom of Information process.

Chief Aubrey responded - They cannot comment on the budget, but there have been known fires
due to ebike batteries. They would discuss concerns with resident outside of chambers.

N.Johal, Walfred Rd - The speaker expressed support for libraries, believes the City could go
about it differently to reduce taxes by requesting donations.

M. Wignall, Selwyn Rd - The speaker expressed concern about tax increase and projected
increases. The speaker appreciates allocated funds. The speaker inquired why some of the
projects can't be delayed.

Mayor Goodmanson called for third time speakers.

T.L. Renken-Sebastian Jacklin/Orono - The speaker expressed concern why the City isn't buying
Emergency Support Services a new vehicle. The speaker inquired to department heads regarding
not hiring additional staff, what are the effects on mental and physical wellness of current staff.

Chief Aubrey responded - They applied for a grant to fund trailer renovations. Emergency
Support Services Directors are pleased with what we are able to provide for them.

B. Hutchins, Director of Corporate Services responded - That City Hall is a lean organization, any
new hires are to provide current service levels to a growing community.

M. Morton, Phelps Aver The speaker inquired about who is paying the rent for YMCA right now.

M. Dillabaugh, Director of Finance responded - That the City is currently paying 1.9 million
dollars to the Westhills Land Corporation.

N.Johal, Langford Resident - The speaker inquired if 1.9 million dollars to the YMCA is for rent.

M. Dillabaugh, Director of Finance responded - That it is a lease payment.

N.Johal, Langford Resident - The speaker inquired if three RCMP officers are enough or should
we have the five asked for in the budget.

Mayor Goodmanson responded - That three officers were brought forward from last years
budget, became aware of 5 recently and it has not been deliberated yet.

L, Foxall, Langford Resident - The speaker inquired about what is being done to increase
investments in Langford.

Mayor Goodmanson responded - That the speaker's inquiry is not a budget item.

M. Dillabaugh, Director of Finance responded - Current budget projects are similar or slightly
higher revenues than last year.

L, Foxall, Langford Resident - The speaker inquired if health care initiatives are planned.

M. Dillabaugh, Director of Finance responded - Health care is a provincial jurisdiction, identified
in Council's strategic plan to advocate on behalf of residents.

L, Foxall, Langford Resident - The speaker disagrees that it is Healthcare is provincial jurisdiction,
as Colwood is helping with healthcare.

S. Rossander, Langford Resident - The speaker inquired if taxation is a surplus revenue source.
The speaker inquired if a contract amendment is required to pay Westhills and not the YMCA.
The speaker stated that the City is in violation of contract if paying more than the maximum of
$950,000 to be paid.

M. Dillabaugh, Director of Finance responded - That surplus generated when revenue exceeds
expenditures. The second question it an operational matter and doesn't impact current budget
discussion.

D. James, Langford Resident - The speaker supports a proposed staff increase. The speaker
supports community gardens. The speaker inquired whether Council has considered about other
services, food banks for example.

M. Wignall, Selwyn Rd - The speaker expressed concern about fees decreasing from permits and
development in Langford. The speaker inquired if there is an opportunity to do a "plan b" should
development drop off completely.

M. Dillabaugh, Director of Finance responded - The revenues and expenditures are budgeted
conservatively. Budgets are monitored throughout the year; operational adjustments are made
accordingly.

A. Rossander, Langford Resident - The speaker expressed concern about increase to population
and permits and license fees should be increasing not decreasing yearly.

M. Baldwin, Director of Planning and Subdivision - The increase to population is a target in the
Official Community Plan, a refreshed plan will address how we will accommodate the increase.
We are not sure when the increase will happen, could be 25 years out.

Mayor Goodmanson responded - Population increase could be decades off, we are looking at the
next five years only. The speaker can contact City Hall for further clarification.

     S. Sifert, Langford Resident - The speaker inquired what is CRD budget compared to last year.

     M. Dillabaugh, Director of Finance responded - That information is not available yet.

     S. Rossander, Langford Resident - The speaker expressed concern that the 2023 actuals should
     be made public. The speaker stated how do we know what the surplus is when we don't know
     the actuals. Are we using unrestricted cash on hand.

     M. Dillabaugh, Director of Finance responded - Surplus is accumulated over a number of years.
     Cash and surplus are two different things. We have a large cash balance, a fairly large portion of
     that is restrictive for certain purposes. The City doesn't treat cash as restricted or unrestricted.

     Mayor Goodmanson called for 4th time speakers.

     Councillor Harder inquired - Are we allowing 4th time speakers, is it in the procedure bylaw?

     M. Watmough, Deputy Director of Corporate Services responded - The matter is not specific, it is
     at Council's discretion.

     T.L. Renken-Sebastian Jacklin/Orono - Speaker inquired about the impacts of delaying transfers
     to reserves. Speaker expressed support for co-op students/graduate students working in the
     municipality and developing plans that can be completed by staff. Speaker noted RCMP officers
     are moving to other jurisdictions and wondered if the municipality could get a signing bonus
     payment as we trained these individuals.

     Mayor Goodmanson responded - Langford fire volunteers are the ones being lost to paid
     positions elsewhere.

     Chief Aubrey responded - Reimbursement can be challenging as many people are volunteering
     seeking experience to apply for career positions Challenging to get a reimbursement for
     someone who is volunteering their time.

     B.Hutchins, Director of Corporate Services responded - The climate change position is
     completely funded through a grant program and co-op students are frequently hired.

     M. Dillabaugh, Director of Finance responded - Transfers to reserves are to be used for capital
     purposes. Transfers to reserves help the municipality save for expenses upcoming and help level
     out tax increases.

     C.Carlson, Saanich - Speaker expressed concern about the proposed property tax increase.

     Mayor Goodmanson closed public participation.

     5.1   BYLAW NO. 2019

           "Langford Zoning Bylaw, Amendment No. 706 (982, 984, 986, 988 Bray Avenue), Bylaw
           No. 2019, 2022".

           The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 2019 at 7:05 pm.

           Director of Planning Matthew Baldwin advised Kristian Harvie, of Woodsmere Holdings
           Corp, has applied to rezone 982, 984, 986, and 988 Bray Avenue from the One- and Two-
           Family Residential (R2) Zone to the City Centre (CC1) Zone.

           This is being proposed in order to allow for the development of a six-storey rental
           apartment building with approximately 59 units and 74 parking stalls.

           In support of this application, the applicant has agreed to:

           1. Register a Section 219 covenant, prior to Bylaw Adoption, that is in priority of all
           other charges on title, that agrees to the following:

                   a. That frontage improvements, a stormwater management plan, a
                   construction parking and traffic management plan, and mitigation plan are
                   provided to Bylaw 1000 standards to the satisfaction of the Director of
                   Engineering prior to the issuance of a Building Permit

                   b. That the properties be consolidated prior to issuance of a Development
                   Permit for Form and Character;

                  c. That a separate covenant be registered prior to issuance of a building permit
                  for the proposed development that ensures residential parking is allocated to
                  each unit and visitors as required by the zoning bylaw and is not provided in
                  exchange for compensation separate from that of a residential unit;

                  d. That all concrete used on-site will utilize ready-mix concrete that meets or
                  exceeds the weighted average Global Warming Potential targets based on
                  Concrete BC Baseline (average) mix data, and that prior to the issuance of a
                  Building Permit the applicant shall provide a Type Ill Environmental Product
                  Declaration that is 3rd party verified specifying the total Global Warming
                  Potential value and confirming that the proposed development meets the
                  requirements of Low Carbon Concrete Policy POL-0167-PLAN;

                  e. That the developer submit the Fire Underwriters Survey (FUS) calculations
                  prior to the issuance of a development permit to develop the property, and
                  acknowledges that these calculations may determiner different setbacks than
                  what is prescribed in the zone or from what has been grated through variances;

                  f. That, prior to the issuance of a Building Permit, the developer enters into a
                  Housing Agreement with the City that requires a minimum 10% of units
                  constructed be rented at a rate no higher than 30% of the median renter income
                  as calculated by the Canadian Mortgage and Housing Corporation for Langford
                  for a term not less than 10 years or that a minimum of 5% of the units
                  constructed be directed to and sold in accordance with the terms of the

          Attainable Home Ownership Program Policy (POL-0166-PLAN). The developer
          shall identify the Attainable Units on the plans submitted for the required
          Development Permit application.

          g. That at least 10% of the units be designed as adaptable units and that at
          least 70% of the units have side-by-side washer and dryers, to the satisfaction of
          the Chief Building Inspector;

          h. That the rooftop patio located on the northwestern side be designed with 5-
          foot-tall translucent glass along the western side to increase the privacy to
          existing neighbours, to the satisfaction of the Director of Planning;

          i. That no occupancy permit be issued for the proposed building until a strata
          plan for the building has been registered, to the satisfaction of the Approving
          Officer;

          j. That electric heat pumps be installed, to the satisfaction of the Chief Building
          Inspector; and

          k. That the foyer panel is designed to accommodate visual challenges, to the
          satisfaction of the Chief Building Inspector.

In support of this application, the applicant has agreed to provide the following as a
bonus for increased density:

          1. $750 towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund; and

          2. $2,850 towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund;

Subject to reductions in accordance with the Affordable Housing and Amenity
Contribution Policy and the Attainable Housing Policy depending on use and height.

This proposal is consistent with the Official Community Plan City Centre designation.

Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by the Local Government
Act.

      "Langford Official Community Plan Bylaw, Amendment No. 49, (2207 Millstream Road),
      Bylaw No. 2149, 2024".

      "Langford Zoning Bylaw, Amendment No. 708 (2207 Millstream Road), Bylaw No. 2150,
      2024".

      The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw Nos. 2149 and 2150 at 7:28 pm.

      Director of Planning Matthew Baldwin advised Reid Kaufmann of Langford Heights
      Development LP has applied to amend the Official Community Plan designation of a
      portion of the property at 2207 Millstream Road from "Business or Light Industrial" to
      "Neighbourhood" and to amend a portion of the zoning designation of the same
      property from the "Business Park (BP9) Zone" to the "One- and Two-Family Residential
      (R2) Zone".

      This is being proposed in order to adjust the western boundary lines of the OCP and
      Zoning designations by approximately 10 metres.

      In support of this application, the applicant has agreed to provide the following
      contributions per residential lot created as a bonus for increased density:

              2. $3,960 towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund.

      requirements:

              standards, all to the satisfaction of the Direction of Engineering;

             provided, along with the associated bond for those works, all to the satisfaction

                                                                                         of the

      Development - Westhills (CD3) Zone to allow for a group daycare with 53 children at
      1331 Westhills Drive.

      In support of this application, the applicant has agreed to:

      1. Register a Section 219 covenant, prior to Bylaw Adoption that agrees to the
      following:

              a. That the following Transit Demand Management strategies be implemented
              and maintained for all office users:

                      i. Guaranteed Ride Home program with a minimum of 8 reimbursable
                      trips per employee per year; and

                      ii. Provide employees with at least $1.55 per day for not using a single
                      occupant vehicle as their travel mode.

              b. That no-parking stalls be assigned to specific users with the exception of the
              daycare leaseholder and that all parking be provided on a first-come-first-served
              basis, with the exception of accessible parking stalls and designated pick-up and
              drop-off stalls for the daycare use.

      Council has also directed staff to provide notice that Council will consider issuing a
      Development Variance Permit for the property at 1331 Westhills Drive in accordance
      with the following:

              i. That Section 4.01.01 of Bylaw 300 be varied to reduce the required onsite
              parking from 126 to 118 parking stalls.

      This proposal is consistent with the Official Community Plan Neighbourhood Centre
      designation.

      Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by the Local Government
      Act.

9.   NOTICE OF MOTION

     9.1   Exploring Options to Better Manage Waste Collection in Langford

           Councillor Yacucha read aloud a Notice of Motion as follows:

           WHEREAS the City of Langford does not operate a municipal garbage collection service,
           for residential and commercial pick up; waste collection is currently managed by private
           contractors and is non-mandatory;
           AND WHEREAS overflowing garbage cans in public and shared spaces contribute to
           health risks, unsightliness, and negative environmental impacts;
           AND WHEREAS improperly managed waste can attract wildlife, including bears, posing
           risks to both public safety and animal welfare;
           AND WHEREAS residents and visitors have raised concerns about litter accumulation and
           inadequate waste management in high-traffic areas;
           THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT Council direct staff to prepare a report outlining
           potential options to address and reduce overflowing garbage cans in public areas,
           including but not limited to:
           • A data comparison of overflowing public waste receptacles over the past 5 years'
           • Assessing the current maintenance and servicing of public waste receptacles in parks,
           streetscapes, and transit stops;
           • Reviewing potential partnerships with private waste service providers or
           supplementing with City staff to enhance collection in key locations;
           • Options for an interim increase in level of service for existing public waste
           receptacles;
           • Options for an increase in quantity or capacity/design change for public waste
           receptacles and recycling bins to reduce wildlife attraction and discourage the illegal
           practice of dumping household waste;
           • Considering public awareness or signage initiatives to encourage responsible waste
           disposal and to minimize wildlife encounters;
           • Supporting community-level pride and responsibility through education, volunteer
           programs, or beautification campaigns, in partnership with community organizations;
           and
           • Exploring enhanced enforcement options, such as increased bylaw presence, fines
           for illegal dumping or littering, and signage to support compliance.
           AND THAT Council direct staff to explore options for a municipal waste management
           service, grant funding or regional collaboration opportunities, and report back with
           recommendations for short-term improvements and long-term strategies that support
           greater solid-waste diversion and reduction.
