THAT Council:

                 1. Direct staff to give notice that Council will consider First, Second and Third
                    Reading of Bylaw No. 2217 to amend the text of the BP9 zone to add 'School' as
                    a permitted use for the property located at 691 Kodiak Way subject to the
                    following terms and conditions:

                     a. That the applicant, prior to Bylaw Adoption, registers a Section 219
                        covenant in priority of all other charges on title, that agrees to the
                        following:

                         i.   That the following will be provided and implemented to Bylaw No. 1000
                              standards to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering prior to the
                              issuance of a building permit:

                              1. A storm water management plan; and

                              2. A mitigation plan.

                         ii. That all concrete used on-site will utilize ready-mix concrete that meets
                             or exceeds the weighted average Global Warming Potential targets
                             based on Concrete BC Baseline (average) mix data, and that prior to the
                             issuance of a Building Permit the applicant shall provide a Type III
                             Environmental Product Declaration that is 3rd party verified specifying
                             the total Global Warming Potential value and confirming that the
                             proposed development meets the requirements of Low Carbon
                             Concrete Policy POL-0167-PLAN.

     5.1   BYLAW NO. 2137

           "Langford Zoning Bylaw, Amendment No. 702, (798 Gwendolynn Drive), Bylaw No. 2137,
           2023".

           The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 2137 at 7:29 pm.

           Deputy Director of Planning and Subdivision Leah Stohmann advised that Lee Nilsson of
           OV Partners has applied on behalf of OV Holdings 2022 Inc to amend the zoning of 798
           Gwendolynn Drive from the RR2 (Rural Residential 2) Zone to the R2 (One- and Two-
           Family Residential) Zone.
           This is being proposed in order to allow for the development of approximately 6 single
           family homes and 12 townhomes.
           In support of this application, the applicant has agreed to provide the following:

           1. That the applicant provides, as a bonus for increased density, the following
           contributions per residential unit, prior to issuance of a building permit:

                       I. $610 towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund per townhouse unit;

                       ii. $660 towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund per single family lot
                            under 550 m2;

                       iii. $3,660 towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund per townhouse unit;
                             and

                       iv.$3,960 towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund per single family lot
                           under 550 m2

           2. That prior to Bylaw Adoption, the applicant registers a Section 219 covenant in
           priority of all other charges on title that agrees to the following:

                        i. That the following will be provided and implemented to Bylaw 1000
                             standards to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering prior to the
                             issuance of subdivision approval or the issuance of a building permit,
                             whichever is first:

                                   a) Full frontage improvements, inclusive of a sidewalk or
                                   minimum 3 m multi-use paved trail, boulevard, and streetlights
                                   along Gwendolynn and a multi-use gravel road edge trail behind
                                   a split rail fence along Klahanie;
                                   b) A storm water management plan;
                                   c) An erosion and sediment control plan;
                                   d) A dust mitigation plan;
                                   e) A construction parking and delivery management plan;

                       ii. That the developer will connect and be responsible for any upgrades
                       required to the services and utilities required for the development;

                       iii. Acknowledge that the site is in proximity to agricultural uses the South
                       Vancouver Island gun range, and that these uses may create general noise,

            odour, and other nuisances, and agree that the owner and all future owners
            assume all risk and annoyance of such nuisances;

            iv.That a total of 30% of the lot will be fenced and retained as a natural
            greenspace common property area protected by a non-disturbance
            covenant registered prior to subdivision approval or building permit
            issuance, whichever is first, to the satisfaction of the Director of Planning;

            v.That tree protection measures are implemented and excavation
            monitored to the satisfaction of the project arborist, as per their report
            dated April 25th, 2023;

            vi. That all concrete used on-site will utilize ready-mix concrete that meets
            or exceeds the weighted average Global Warming Potential targets based on
            Concrete BC Baseline (average) mix data, and that prior to the issuance of a
            Building Permit the applicant shall provide a Type III Environmental Product
            Declaration that is 3rd party verified specifying the total Global Warming
            Potential value and confirming that the proposed development meets the
            requirements of Low Carbon Concrete Policy POL-0167-PLAN;

            vii. That a separate covenant be registered prior to the issuance of a
            building permit agreeing that the garages and carports are to be used for
            the parking of vehicles and not the storage of items preventing the parking
            of vehicles therein.

Council has also directed staff to amend Section 6.22.04 of the R2 zone to limit the
number of townhouses permitted at 798 Gwendolynn to 12 units.

This proposal is consistent with the Official Community Plan Neighbourhood
designation.
Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by the Local Government
Act.

 angford Zoning Bylaw, Amendment No, 703, (2703, 2707 and 2711 Claude Rd and 726
Percy Place), Bylaw No. 2139, 2023",

The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No, 2139 at 8:17 pm.

Deputy Director of Planning and Subdivision Leah Stohmann advised that Kyle Stewart of
Empowered Development Ltd has applied on behalf of 1377938 BC Ltd to amend the
zoning of 2703, 2707, and 2711 Claude Road and 726 Percy Place from the R2 (One-and
Two-Family Residential) Zone to the CC1 (City Centre 1) Zone.
This is being proposed in order to allow for the development of a six storey apartment
building with approximately 107 residential units.
 n support of this application, the applicant has agreed to provide the following:

1. That the applicant provides, as a bonus for increased density, the following
contributions per dwelling unit, prior to the issuance of a building permit:

        i. $750 towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund; and
          . $2,850 towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund;

Subject to reductions in accordance with the Affordable Housing and Amenity
Contribution Policy and the Attainable Housing Policy depending on use and height.

2. That the applicant registers, prior to Bylaw Adoption, a road dedication plan for the
connection of Percy Place to Claude Road, to the satisfaction of the Director of
Engineering;

3. That the applicant provides, prior to Bylaw Adoption, a Section 219 covenant,
registered in priority of all other charges on title, that agrees to the following:

        a. That the following will be provided and implemented to Bylaw No. 1000
        standards to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering prior to the issuance
        of a building permit:

                i.Full frontage improvements, inclusive of a 1.8 m wide concrete
                sidewalk, scallop parallel parking, boulevard with grass and street trees,
                streetlights, and a 1.5 m wide bike lane on Claude Road;
                ii. A storm water management plan; and
                iii. A construction parking and delivery management plan.

        b. That the properties be consolidated prior to issuance of a Development
        Permit for
        Form and Character;

        c. That a separate covenant be registered prior to issuance of a building permit
        for the proposed development that ensures residential parking is not provided
        in exchange for compensation separate from that of a residential unit;

        d. That all concrete used on-site will utilize ready-mix concrete that meets or
        exceeds the weighted average Global Warming Potential targets based on
        Concrete BC Baseline (average) mix data, and that prior to the issuance of a
        Building Permit the applicant shall provide a Type Ill Environmental Product
        Declaration that is 3rd party verified specifying the total Global Warming
        Potential value;

        e. That the building will, at a minimum, be designed to and meet the
        performance standards of Step 3 of the BC Energy Step Code;

        f. That, prior to the issuance of a Building Permit, the developer enters into a
        Housing Agreement with the City that requires either a minimum 10% of units
        constructed be rented for at least 10% below the benchmark rent for the unit
        type for a term not less than 25 years or that a minimum of 5% of the units
        constructed be directed to and sold in accordance with the terms of the
        Attainable Home Ownership Program Policy (POL-0166-PLAN). The developer
        shall identify the Attainable Units on the plans submitted for the required
        Development Permit application;

        g. That legal public access be provided to the on-site carshare vehicles, prior to
        the issuance of a building permit, to the satisfaction of the Director of Planning
        and Subdivision.

6.   NOTICE OF MOTION

     6.1     Resolution for the Association of Vancouver Island and Coastal Communities

             Councillor Guiry read aloud the following Notice of Motion:

             Whereas:

             People who are postpartum may experience pelvic floor dysfunction, including
             incontinence, pain, and prolapse, as a direct result of pregnancy and childbirth, which
             significantly impacts quality of life, mental health, long-term physical well-being and
             creates inequitable financial burdens.

             AND Whereas:

             The Canadian Physiotherapy Association recognizes pelvic floor physiotherapy as an
             evidence-based, non-invasive treatment option that improves postpartum recovery;
             however, the lack of both equitable access to pelvic floor physiotherapy and education
             about the benefits contributes to healthcare costs associated with untreated pelvic floor
             dysfunction, including corrective surgeries, chronic conditions and the expense of
             personal hygiene products.

             Therefore be it resolved that:

             The provincial government work with healthcare professionals, including
             physiotherapists, obstetricians, midwives and nurse practitioners to ensure postpartum

                 care involves informing patients about and provides patients equitable access to pelvic
                 floor assessments and physiotherapy services, regardless of income or insurance status.

                Be it further resolved that:

                The Province of British Columbia implement a program to provide free pelvic floor
                physiotherapy treatments as part of the standard postpartum care under the BC Medical
                Services Plan (MSP).

5.   NOTICE OF MOTION

     Councillor Harder read the following Notice of Motion:

     WHEREAS on December 5, 2022, Council considered a recommendation to name the Kettle
     Creek Linear Park and Playground after former Councillor Winnie Sifert in recognition of her long
     service to the City of Langford.

     AND WHEREAS Council determined that any decision regarding the naming of this park should
     be deferred until after the adoption of an amended or new park naming policy.

     AND WHEREAS a more suitable park has been identified to be named given its proximity to
     Winnie Sifert's neighbourhood,

     NOW THEREFORE, I move that Council rename Ernhill Park to "Winnie Sifert Park" once the park
     naming policy has been adopted and direct staff to work with former Councillor Sifert's family on
     a formal naming ceremony to be held prior to December 15, 2025.

5.   PUBLIC HEARINGS

     5.1   BYLAW NO. 2082

           "Langford Zoning Bylaw, Amendment No. 679, (Omnibus No. 60 —Various Housekeeping
           Items), Bylaw No. 2082, 2023"

           The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 2082 at 7:47 p.m.

            Director of Planning Matthew Baldwin advised that The City of Langford is proposing to
           amend Zoning Bylaw No. 300 in the following ways:
           • By introducing regulations with respect to tandem parking in townhouse
           developments;
           • By increasing the width of interior, or in-garage, parking spaces;
           • By introducing "accessory dormitories which may include a kitchenette" as a permitted
           use in the CD2 (Hull's Field) zone;
           • By restricting where apartments may occur at the ground level in the City Centre
           Pedestrian (CCP) zone to exclude Peatt Road, Claude Road, Bryn Maur Avenue, Jacklin
           Road and Veterans Memorial Parkway;
           • By deleting the requirement for a lm wide landscaping strip adjacent to an interior
           side
           lot line in the City Centre 1 (CC1) zone.
           • By consolidating all daycare capacity exemptions from each zone into Part 3 of the
           Zoning

      bylaw.
      • By allowing R2 (One-and Two-family Residential) lots to be less than 600m2 but not
      less
      than 500m2 if the lot width is 17m.
      • By prohibiting landscape retaining walls that are visitable from municipal roads that
      are
      finished as smooth concrete blocks and/or a natural concrete colour.
      AND
      • By introducing requirements for accessible parking in all types of multi-family
      residential
      development.
      Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by the Local Government
      Act.

      Mayor Goodmanson called a first time for presentations.

      B. Armstrong, Rodney Rd - Expressed concern with the deletion of the requirement for a
      lm wide landscaping strip adjacent to an interior side lot line in the City Centre 1 (CC1)
      zone.

      Mayor Goodmanson called a second time for presentations.

      None presented.

      Mayor Goodmanson called a third time for presenters.

      None presented.

      Mayor Goodmanson declared the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 2082 closed at 7:52 pm.

5.2   BYLAW NO. 2099

      "Langford Zoning Bylaw, Amendment No. 693, (971 Walfred Road) Bylaw No. 2099,
      2023".

      The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 2099 at 7:52 p.m.

      Director of Planning Matthew Baldwin advised that Pat Guiney has applied on behalf of
      1157393 BC Ltd. to amend the zoning of 971 Walfred Road from the One- and Two-
      Family Zone to the Residential Townhouse 1 Zone.


      This is being proposed in order to allow for the development of approximately 13
      townhouses.


      Prior to Public Hearing, the applicant has provided a technical memo from an engineer
      that verifies stormwater can be adequately managed on-site for the proposed
      development, which has been approved by the Director of Engineering AND a memo by
      a Landscape Architect that examines existing trees on site and along the frontages to
      provide comment on potential tree retention, which has been approved by the Director
      of Planning.

In support of this application, the applicant has agreed to provide the following:
1. Amenity Contributions as a bonus for increased density as follows:
a. $610 per unit towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund; and
b. $3,660 per unit towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund.


2. Road dedication, full frontage improvements, a stormwater management plan, and a
construction parking plan — all to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering;


3. Onsite paver stones, an arbour with a pedestrian gate, and variable rooflines — all to
the satisfaction of the Director of Planning;


4. That storage within garages does not prevent parking of vehicles, tree protection
measures are carried out throughout the entire construction period, and that concrete
used will comply with Council's Low Carbon Concrete Policy;


5. With respect to the neighbouring property at 3303 Lodmell, the developer will install
drainage improvements, remove the existing retaining wall, install a 6-foot fence along
the shared property line, retain trees along the shared property line, and plant an
additional 8 tree along the shared property line.


This proposal is consistent with the Official Community Plan 'Neighbourhood'
designation.


Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by the Local Government
Act.

Mayor Goodmanson called a first time for presentations.

Pat Guinev, Applicant - expressed support for the proposed development and provided
an overview of some energy efficient features of the build including solar energy, electric
car chargers, heat pumps, electric water heaters and induction cook tops. Speaker also
concerned about parking in the area, noting visitor spots including oversized parking
that will be accessible.

Mayor Goodmanson called a second time for presentations.

D. Knudson, Lodmell Rd - expressed concerns with the proposed development including
changes to the neighbourhood over time, effects of previous developments have had on
the speaker's property, and proposed possible remedies for Council's consideration.

L. Plomp, Whimfield Terr - expressed support for the proposed development including
extensive public engagement undertaken by the applicant, and addressing of close
proximity resident's concerns.

Mendez, Mesa PI - expressed concern with the proposed development including concern
for safety of children and pedestrians in the area, size of the proposed buildings, and
emergency safety considerations.

M. Wignall, Selwyn Rd - expressed support for the proposed development including the
applicants work in the community previously.

J.Patterson, Lodmell Rd - expressed concerns with parking within and nearby the
proposed development and concern for safety of children and pedestrians in the area.

Mayor Goodmanson called a third time for presenters.

Councillor Wagner inquired to the Engineering Department. What is the current parking
situation near the proposed development?

K.Balzer, Director of Engineering and Public Works responded - there is currently no
visitor parking on Lodmell Rd, only on Walfred Rd. Parking issues, should they arise, will
be monitored by the Bylaw Enforcement Department. No parking or limited parking
signage would be erected if necessary.

Councillor Wagner inquired to the Engineering Department. Is the current parking there
scalloped?

K. Balzer, Director of Engineering and Public Works responded confirming the scalloped
parking style on Walfred Rd.

Councillor Szpak inquired to staff and Council. Regarding the neighbour at 3303 Lodmell
Rd who has been experiencing difficulties, what can be done to mitigate these issues?

M. Baldwin, Director of Planning responded - staff included the owners of 3303 Lodmell
Rd's concerns as conditions of zoning.

Councillor Szpak wished to confirm that the conditions of zoning as presented were
amenable to the owner of 3303 Lodmell Rd.

D. Knudson, Lodmell Rd - responded confirming these conditions are satisfactory.

Councillor Harder inquired to the Engineering Department. Based off the traffic safety
comments, it appears that the landscaping plans show a sheltered area with pavers and
a bench for those waiting for the bus. Preferably, this is landscaped like the rest of
Walfred Rd.

K. Balzer, Director of Engineering and Public Works responded confirming the bench and
shelter will be present with a 2.2m sidewalk that connects to the existing ones on
Walfred Rd as well as a stop sign on Lodmell Rd.

Councillor Harder noted appreciation for comments regarding families reducing to one
vehicle.

Mayor Goodmanson inquired to the Engineering and Public Works Department. Is the
parking on Walfred signed for use by this development or is it for anyone?

K. Balzer, Director of Engineering and Public Works responded confirming the parking
spots are for the public.

             Mayor Goodmanson declared the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 2099 closed at 8:18 pm.

6.   PUBLIC PARTICIPATION

     Councillor Harder left the meeting at 8:18 p.m.

     Mayor Goodmanson opened the public participation period.

     Councillor Harder returned to the meeting at 8:19 p.m.

     S. Perry, Glen Lake Rd — re: item 4.1— Speaker expressed opposition to the City joining the CRD
     Arts and Culture Program noting Langford and Victoria do not share a border. Speaker also
     encouraged the City to plan for an arts and culture space within the new university building.
     Speaker expressed a wish for Langford's money to stay within the municipality. Speaker
     expressed concern for safety within the City of Victoria and cautioned Council against providing
     funding. re: item 4.2 —Speaker expressed concern with electric water heating tanks noting costs
     associated with this feature including insurance and replacement. Speaker also noted electric
     water heating tanks occupy a large amount of space.

     J. Withers, Woodhampton Rise — re: item 4.1 — Speaker expressed support for the City joining
     the CRD Arts and Culture Program noting a need to travel into Victoria currently to experience
     live music and a wish to have this form of entertainment locally. Speaker noted that music
     fosters a sense of community and local identity.

     J. Rye, Finney Rd — re: item 13.1 — Speaker attempted to address an item that was the subject of
     a previous Public Hearing. As a result, the speaker was interrupted and their comments
     disallowed.

     S. Sifert, Walfred Rd — re: 9.1.7 Speaker expressed concern with the report noting that
     homelessness and camping in public spaces cause negative impacts to residents and businesses.
     Speaker noted that shelters are appearing in many places throughout the City and consideration
     of residents and business safety is important.

     R. Louie, Bellamy Rd — re: item 4.1 —Speaker expressed opposition to the City joining the
     program as there is no opt out feature. Speaker also noted that Langford organizations are not
     guaranteed to receive funding from the program and if they do, it may not be proportionate.
     Speaker noted that the funding should stay within the community and the funding rates through
     the CRD may increase in the future.

     M. Morton, Phelps Ave — re: item 13.5 —Speaker expressed concern with the Tree Bylaw noting
     that homeowners and residents of Langford are experiencing issues with the Bylaw including
     adverse financial effects and unfair process.

     M. Wignall, 2375 Selwyn Rd — re: item 4.1 —Speaker expressed concern with the costs of the
     CRD Arts and Culture program noting the City may not receive the value for the money invested.
     re: item 13.7 —Speaker expressed concern with sheltering within the City, noting the difficult
     relationship between enforcement and allowing sheltering to occur from a public safety
     perspective.

     W. Bowers, Millstream Rd — re: item 4.1 — Speaker expressed concern with the CRD Arts and
     Culture program noting high costs. Speaker also noted that outreach to directly neighbouring
     municipalities is needed and could result in more programs locally rather than providing money
     to the City of Victoria. Speaker noted many programs locally such as the P.A.C.E program and

     programs available through organizations like the Y.M.C.A. Speaker expressed concern with the
     permanency of the agreement noting there is no opt-out feature.

     B. Armstrong, Rodney Rd — re: item 4.1 — Speaker noted that the CRD Arts and Culture program
     is a CRD initiative and not a City of Victoria one. Speaker expressed support for regional arts and
     culture noting many residents of Langford travel around the CRD. Speaker noted that currently
     there is a need to travel outside of the City to experience arts and culture. Speaker also noted
     interest in seeing a report regarding the program in the future.

     S. Rossander, Ravensview Dr — re: item 4.1— Speaker expressed support for a report being
     written exploring the pros and cons of joining the CRD Arts and Culture program. Speaker
     expressed opposition to joining the CRD Arts and Culture program noting the permanency of the
     agreement as there is no opt-out feature.

     L. Foxall, Players Dr — re: item 9.4 -- Speaker noted the minutes did not mention the
     repercussions of the social media clause, only the policies. re: item 4.1 — Speaker noted that they
     have received feedback from residents wishing not to partner with the City of Victoria. Speaker
     noted that the City partners with many neighbouring municipalities who share borders on
     numerous issues and in order to keep investment and jobs in the City, Langford should not
     partner with the CRD on this program. Speaker expressed concern with the permanency of the
     agreement as there is no opt-out feature. Speaker noted an arts and culture center could be
     built at the new university in partnership with nearby municipalities.

5.   PUBLIC PARTICIPATION

     C. Nevil, Ernhill PI - re: RidgeView PI

     J. Hattie, Penelope PI - re: item 4.2 - Proposed a property for sale in the city located at
     Goldstream Ave. and Vantilburg Cres. for a potential location for the Aboriginal Coalition to end
     Homeless Society's new property.

     T. Wright, Commander Crt - re: item 9.2 - Expressed opposition to the tax increase. Will have an
     effect on young families and those with a fixed income.

     J.C., Claude Rd - re: Ridgeview PI - Expressed a need for more help. Speaker expressed not
     enough is being done to assist residents.

     M. Wignall, Selwyn Rd - re: item 6.2 - Expressed concern that their views at public participation
     were not captured accurately. re: item 9.2- Expressed concern about the numbers of the tax
     increase. Expressed concern regarding line item on page 3 of the budget.

     M. Dillabaugh, Director of Finance responded and clarified the percentages.

     A. Rossander, Ravensview Dr - re: item 9.3 - Expressed concern regarding the tax increase.
     Speaker asked if the Mayor be happy with the increase if they were a resident of Langford.
     Expressed concern that the current Mayor has not enlisted the assistance of the former Mayor.

     S. Sifert, Walfred Rd - re: item 9.3 - Expressed gratitude to the mayor for allowing residents of
     RidgeView Apartments to speak. Expressed opposition to the proposed budget. Expressed
     concern regarding the increase of expenditures to the consults. Expressed concern regarding the
     increase to the training and travel allowance. Expressed concern regarding the increase to
     adverting for planning and parks departments. Expressed concern regarding the increase to
     community events expenditures. Expressed concern regarding the increase to tourism
     expenditures. Expressed total increase is $390,453 or over 64% from the previous year.

Expressed concern why are more consultants are hired. Expressed concern why can't there be
better rates. Expressed concern why do staff travel so much. Expressed concern why is the City
buying the YMCA.

S. Rossander, Ravensview Dr - re: item 10.3 - Speaker asked why this bylaw is necessary.

M. Dillabaugh, Director of Finance responded that there is standard wording in the bylaw. The
City has no plans to borrow the funds, but the City is required to have it as part of the banking
agreements.

M.L. Taylor, Claude Rd - re: RidgeView Apartments - Expressed great concern regarding the
current situation with their home. Expressed concern regarding next steps.

C. Aubrey, Fire Chief responded that the resident reach out to them at the firehall, and they will
assist any way they can.

Nicholas Johal, Walfred PI - re: item 9.3 - Expressed disappointment that the budget didn't
prioritize the turf and light field. Speaker is discouraged by the lack of communication and
partnership with the local school district, and minor sports leagues teams regarding the
decision. The speaker inquired who was consulted regarding the decision. Expressed concern
regarding the tax increase and the financial impact to residents.

W. Hobbs, Luxton Rd - re: item 9.3 - Expressed support regarding the number of increases to
firefighters. Expressed support for the increase of RCMP police officers.

L. Foxall, Players Dr - re: item 9.3 - Expressed opposition to the increase and the five-year
financial plan. Expressed concern that Council did not work to decrease the budget. Expressed
suggestions to decrease the budget. Raise fees in the development community too offset taxes.
Raise the rate of amenity fees to pay for new RCMP building. Expressed concern that public
questions were not answered.

R. Taylor, Claude Rd - re: RidgeView Apartments - Expressed concern regarding not being
notified sooner about the situation in the building. Expressed concern regarding next steps.

S. Costello, Robalee PI - re: item 9.3 - Expressed that they are a 52-year resident of the City.
Expressed support for the budget. Expressed support for the financial director. Expressed that
the taxes should be higher, in order to have all of the available amenities.

S. Perry, Glen Lake Rd - re: item 9.2 and 9.3 - Expressed that an increase in City staff is not
necessary. Expressed that work loads have decreased. Speaker stated that Council and staff
need to work harder. Expressed concern that questions submitted have not been answered.

C. Wright, Commander Crt - re: item 9.3 - Expressed concern that the non-property tax revenues
are not being used to reduce property taxes.

W. Bowers, Millstream Rd - re: item 9.3 - Expressed concern that the public is being ignored.
Expressed concern why didn't the purchase of the YMCA go to referendum. Speaker stated that
if there is not enough funding for the RCMP building, that travel expenses should be cut.

V. Barrow, Happy Valley Rd - re: item 9.3 - Expressed concern about the increase of taxes.
Expressed concern about living on a pension and the future increases of expenses.

J. Patterson, Lodmell Rd - re: item 9.3 - Expressed opposition to the tax increase. Expressed
concern that the young families will lose housing.

C. Legacy, Artesian Crt - re: item 9.3 - Expressed support for the proposed budget. Speaker
stated instead of lending the YMCA money, the City should buy it.

M. Wignall, Selwyn Rd - re: item 9.3 - Speaker discussed the fees of the budget. Speaker
discussed the non-property revenues being used for property taxes. Speaker discussed training
and travel expenses. Expressed concern regarding some previous events not being funded again.
Expressed concern regarding the Latoria Rd. turf field.

M. Dillabaugh, Director of Finance responded that the events on page 23 are budgeted as a
group. Regarding revenues, it is the City's practice to budget conservatively. We look at past
year trends when looking at a budget.

L. Foxall, Players Dr- re: RidgeView apartments. Speaker inquired if there is an ambassador for
residents at Ridgeview. re: item 9.3 - Speaker stated to look to increasing development
community. Expressed concern regarding paying taxes in July.

W. Hobbs, Luxton Rd - re: item 9.3 - Speaker inquired about the following years tax rate.
Speaker stated that the budget is actually an increase of 6% from last year.

M. Dillabaugh, Director of Finance responded the rates were 2.95% last year, 2021 5.84%. Just
over 6% for last 3 years.

C. Lervold, Glen Lake Rd - re: item 9.3 - Expressed opposition to the proposed budget. Expressed
disappointment that their questions have not been answered. Expressed concern that
negotiations were compromised. Expressed concern that the YMCA has become a priority over
the RCMP building.

S. Sifert, Walfred Rd - re: item 9.3 - Expressed concern regarding the Council listening to the
community.

Mayor Goodmanson confirmed events are still running, just a separate line item on budget.

A. Rossander, Ravensview Dr - re: item 9.3 - Speaker wanted clarification of line items of the
budget. Speaker believes the calculation to be misleading.

M. Dillabaugh, Director of Finance responded that the numbers are correct. In 2024, 50 million
compared to 45 million in 2023. Not depicting that as a total.

            B. White, Langford Resident - The speaker stated how impressed they were with the
            scope of the presentation. The speaker inquired about the development of Langford
            Heights and how will the Urban Forest Management Plan protect Millstream Creek.

            G. Willing, Colwood Resident - The speaker stated they are a City of Langford property
            owner. The speaker inquired about hiring an arborist. The speaker inquired about the
            protection of tress under 20 cm in diameter. The speaker inquired if Agricultural Land

5.   PUBLIC HEARINGS

     5.1   BYLAW NO. 1927

           "Langford Zoning Bylaw, Amendment No. 706, (957 Walfred Road), Bylaw No. 1927,
           2023".

           The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1927 at 7:05 pm.

           Director of Planning Matthew Baldwin advised Kyle Velikovsky has applied on behalf of
           White Wolf Homes Ltd. to amend the zoning of 957 Walfred Road from the RS1
           (Residential Small Lot 1) Zone to RT1 (Residential Townhouse 1) Zone.

           This is being proposed in order to allow for the development of approximately 17
           townhome units.

           In support of this application, the applicant has agreed to provide the following:

               a.   That the applicant provides, as a bonus for increased density, the following
                    contributions per dwelling unit:

                    i. $610 towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund; and
                    ii. $3,660 towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund;

               b. That the applicant, prior to Bylaw Adoption, discharge the previous rezoning
                  covenant and register a new Section 219 covenant in priority of all other charges
                  on title, that agrees to the following:
                  i. That the following will be provided and implemented to Bylaw No. 1000
                  standards to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering prior to the issuance
                  of a building permit:

                        1. Full frontage improvements, inclusive of constructing a cul de sac and
                        bowtie parking, connecting the existing sidewalk on Hinks Road to the on-
                        site pathway, boulevard, and streetlighting. It must also include
                        improvements to the frontage of 955 Walfred Road;
                        2. A storm water management plan; and
                        3. A construction parking management plan.

                    ii. That a separate covenant be registered prior to the registration of a strata
                    plan for the proposed development agreeing that the garages are to be used for
                    the parking of vehicles and not the storage of items preventing the parking of
                    vehicles therein, in favour of the strata.

                    iii. That tree protection measures, inclusive of tree protection fencing, are
                    implemented prior to commencement of work to protect the trees identified for
                    retention in the arborist report throughout the construction period;
                    iv. That all concrete used on-site will utilize ready-mix concrete that meets or
                    exceeds the weighted average Global Warming Potential targets based on
                    Concrete BC Baseline (average) mix data, and that prior to the issuance of a
                    Building Permit the applicant shall provide a Type III Environmental Product

                      Declaration that is 3rd party verified specifying the total Global Warming
                      Potential value and confirming that the proposed development meets the
                      requirements of Low Carbon Concrete Policy POL-0167-PLAN;
                      v. That a Statutory Right of Way be registered over the public pathway prior to
                      the issuance of a building permit;
                      vi. That the public pathway shall be demonstrated within the landscape plan
                      and be clearly delineated to the satisfaction of the Director of Parks, Recreation,
                      and Facilities.

              In addition, Council has resolved to amend the text of Schedule AD of the Zoning Bylaw
              No. 300 to remove the amenity contributions related to Bylaw No. 1261;

              Council has also, by resolution, authorized the Director of Planning to issue the following
              variances within the form and character development permit:

                      a. Section 6.28.07(1)(a) to reduce the front lot line setback from 3 m to 1.2m;
                      and
                      b. Section 6.28.07(1)(d) to reduce the rear lot line setback from 5.5 m to 1.5 m

              Subject to the condition that the variances are only granted for the development of the
              townhouse project as shown at Public Hearing

              This proposal is consistent with the Official Community Plan Neighbourhood
              designation.

             Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by the Local Government
             Act.

             Mayor Goodmanson called a first time for presentations.

             Kyle Velikovsky on behalf of White Wolf Homes Ltd, provided an overview of the
             proposed development to Council.

             Mayor Goodmanson called a second time for presentations.

             T. Parkinson, Walfred Rd - The speaker expressed concern regarding blasting, parking
             and water management in the proposed development. The speaker expressed concern
             regarding their loss of privacy. The speaker expressed concern regarding the changes the
             development will bring to their family's lives.

             Mayor Goodmanson called a third time for presentations.

             N. Johal, Walfred PI - The speaker expressed support for the development.

             Mayor Goodmanson called for a final time for presentations.

             None presented.

             Mayor Goodmanson declared the Public Hearing for Bylaw No.1927 closed at 7:26 pm.

     Arnold, Ravensview Drive - Item 11.3 - Speaker asked for clarity regarding approaches presented

     equal vote (1 to 1) or weighted average vote. Speaker wished for clarity regarding this decision.
     Item 11.2 - Speaker inquired about the policy's options noting that option 1 had many parts that
     Council will have to choose from.
     S. Sifert. Langford Resident - Item 11.1 and 12.9 - Speaker expressed support for option 2 of the
     report. Speaker expressed concern regarding consultant findings and funds spent on this
     initiative. 12.6 - Speaker expressed concern regarding Bylaw No. 2167 and 2168.
     L. Foxall, Langford Resident - Item 12.6 - Speaker expressed concern regarding the proposed tax
     rates. Item 12.9 - Speaker expressed concern regarding Bylaw No. 2167 and 2168.
     W. Hobbs. Langford Resident - Item 7 - Speaker clarified points made at the April 2, 2024 Council
     Meeting during public participation. Item 12.6 - Speaker expressed concern with the proposed
     tax increase and financial plan. Speaker wished to see sidewalk infill on Luxton Road moved
     higher on the priority list.
     T. Cadeau Glenwillow Place - Item 12.4 and 12.9 - Speaker expressed concern regarding the
     proposed bylaw. Speaker noted removal of trees in this area has a large impact on the makeup
     of the neighbourhood. Speaker asked Council to consider protecting trees on the front of the lot
     for visuals and benefits that trees provide.


     S. Perry, Glen Lake Road - Item 11.1 - Speaker expressed concern with the information presented
     within the report. Speaker expressed concern with extending the temporary tree bylaw. Speaker
     noted the tree canopy in Langford is 48%.
     S. Rossander, Langford Resident - Item 12.6 - Speaker expressed concern with the item noting
     their understanding was that this bylaw was already approved. Speaker inquired as to why
     money needed to be spent on the YMCA.
     Council passed a resolution to extend public participation for first time speakers.
     L. Plomp. Whimfield Terrace -Item 11.1 -Speaker noted the heat effect in the downtown core as
     presented. Speaker expressed support for the Urban Forest Management Plan's continuation.
     Item 11.2 -Speaker noted there are not many successful applications and wished to see this
     program extended to include first responders. Item 12.6 & 12. 7 -Speaker noted that tax
     increases are difficult but needed.

5.   PUBLIC PARTICIPATION

     N. McNeely, Lakehurst Dr - re: item #9.3: The speaker supports Option 1 of the resolutions
     presented. Expressed concerns regarding Priority Section 6, Quality of Life. Speaker noted the
     plan fails to address end of life options. The plan does not cover cemetery requirements for
     residents of Langford. The speaker expressed concern regarding Priority Section 1, Sustainable
     Development. Commercial spaces being proposed should be curtailed due to the already empty
     available spaces for lease or recycle these empty spaces into usable space.

     D. Seaton, Glen Lake Rd - re: item #9.3: The speaker expressed concern regarding the lack of
     public consultation in the development of the Strategic Plan. Families, businesses, seniors, arts,
     sports groups, neighbouring municipalities, and community groups are missing from the
     consultation process. The speaker expressed concerns regarding the lack of public notifications.
     Speaker also expressed concerns regarding the lack of time given for public input and noted the
     Strategic Plan reflects Council priorities not Langford citizens.

     A motion was made to extend D. Seaton speaking time by 2 minutes. Please see the motion
     below.

     D. Seaton, Glen Lake Rd - re: item #9.3: The speaker inquired to Council; Why are the
     consultations number not noted in the plan? What is the rationale behind making the plan
     public prior to the consultation process? Public safety and compassion for all citizens, what does
     this mean? Why is policing and community safety not reflected in the plan? Speaker noted many
     paragraphs are dedicated to climate change and environment compared to the needs of the
     residents.

     S. Geary, Bear Mountain Pkwy - re: item #9.3: The speaker supports the accessibly of the plan.
     The speaker made note of several sections: Section 1 d: The speaker believes this is long
     overdue. Section 1 i. and j: The speaker would like a multi level parkade built for overflow
     parking. Section 1 m: The speaker wants Council to collaborate with other municipalities and the
     Province in regard to this issue. 2 e: The speaker supports a review of old infrastructure. 3 c: The
     speaker would like the encouragement of more tech companies in Langford as they promote
     remote working conditions for commuting benefits.

     G. Haythornwaite, Peatt Rd - re: item #9.3: The speaker believes the plan has many attributes to
     update administrative practices of running a city. The speaker expressed concern regarding the
     development of the Strategic Plan did not display open governance. The speaker believes that
     Council should discuss all matters that are in the public's interest in an open meeting. The
     speaker would like prior to the next budget, open forums to discuss and debate future
     challenges. The speaker expressed concerns regarding the plan not advancing public service and
     instead supports a private service model.

     M. Wignall, Selwyn Rd - re: item #9.3: The speaker expressed concern regarding the plan not
     being inclusive of the public. The speaker expressed concern about the scope of the plan.

     S. Costello, Roblee PI - re: item #9.3: The speaker would like the Council to follow facts including
     vehicle ownership and insurance statistics in reference to the Transportation Master Plan as
     outlined in the Strategic Plan.

M. Morton, Phelps Ave - re: item 9.3: The speaker believes the plan needs more public
consultation.
C.Wright, Commander Crt - re: item #9,3: The speaker believes that the OCP is the first Strategic
Plan. The speaker does not believe the City of Langford requires a Strategic Plan. The speaker
inquired how much the plan cost taxpayers. The speaker expressed concern regarding the lack of
advertising for public input of the plan. The speaker supports Option 1 of the resolutions.
A motion was made to extend public participation for 30 minutes Please see the motion below.
D.Dingman, Reunion Ave               9,3: The speaker expressed disappointment that renters are
only mentioned 3 times in the Strategic Plan. The speaker expressed concern about the
affordable and attainable housing issues in Langford. Expressed that the City needs to take
action on improving the housing situation. The speaker suggested that 5% of units be donated to
the City for a housing program. The speaker would like more parks in the City Centre. The
speaker supports Option 1 of the resolutions.
D. Stroud, Jeanine Dr - re: item #9.3: The speaker appreciates the work done on the document
and the public engagement. However, would like more public input. The speaker expressed
concern that the plan does not show that climate change affects other aspects of the plan. The
speaker encouraged the use of a climate specialist.
K.Velikovskv, Walfred Rd - re   em #8.2: The speaker is an applicant for 957 Wa f ed Rd and is
available for any questions.
L.Foxall Players Dr - re: item #9.3: The speaker supports Option 1 of the resolutions. The
speaker stated that the City already has a Strategic Plan in the Official Community Plan. The
speaker expressed that the development of the plan was rushed. The speaker expressed concern
regarding the cost of developing the Strategic Plan. The speaker expressed disappointment in
the lack of public input. The speaker expressed disappointment in the lack of joint partnerships
with other local municipalities.
K. Robinson, Paige Ave - re: item #9,3: The speaker would like the plan deferred. The speaker
expressed concerns regarding the lack of public consultation. The speaker believes the Official
Community Plan designated City Centre area needs to be scaled down. The speaker expressed
concern regarding wetland protection. The speaker believes that transportation needs to be
reassessed.
S. Plank, Goldstream Ave - re: item #9.3: The speaker stated they would have preferred public
engagement early on in the process. The speaker appreciates that there is a need to move
forward with the implementation of the plan. The speaker requested more community
involvement. The speaker stated that the Official Community Plan refresh requires public
engagement. The speaker stated that transportation and parking plans requires more public
engagement. The speaker would like more integration and focus on the priorities of the plan.
S. Sifert, Walfred Rd - re: item #9,3: The speaker does not support the plan. The speaker
supports Option 1 of the resolutions. The speaker expressed concern regarding the lack of public
feedback and the number of people taking the self survey for the plan.
R. Louie, Langford resident - re: item #9.3: The speaker stated the plan is too vague. The speaker
expressed concern regarding Section 6 c. The speaker stated that First Nations stakeholders were

not consulted. The speaker stated they would like to see a higher percentage of public input. The
speaker inquired as to what reconciliation looks like for Langford.

W. Hobbs, Luxton Rd - re: item #9.3: The speaker expressed concern regarding the name of the
plan. The speaker stated that there is already a Strategic Plan in the Official Community Plan. The
speaker would like more public input and expressed concern regarding the amount of time given
to certain speakers during the public participation.

M. Brooke, Merlin Rd - re: item #9.3: The speaker would like urban food resilience to be
highlighted. The speaker would like renters to have more acknowledgement in the plan. The
speaker expressed the public input was adequate and that more public input is required.

A motion was made to extend public participation for 15 minutes. Please see the motion below.

L. Plomp, Whimfield Terr - re: item #9.3: The speaker appreciates the development of the plan.
The speaker inquired how the plan would affect the day to day lives of the community. The
speaker stated that this could be accomplished by section 2c. A food security policy, with the
design of community gardens would be beneficial in the plan. Helping people with high fuel
costs could be achieved by sections 4b 4c and 4d. Improving mental and physical health could be
achieved by sections 6a. and 6 I. A storm management plan in section 2 d. could help alleviate
worry of localized flooding. The social issues should be advocated to the Province for assistance
section 5 a. The speaker encouraged the increase of small business owners and encouraging
local assistance with the housing crisis referencing sections 3 a. and 1 m. The speaker stated that
the good neighbour policy section 1 f. needs to be a priority.

R.Coutre, Goldstream Ave - re: item #8.1: The speaker is available for any questions regarding
the application.

C. Burdge, Hoffman Ave - re: item #9.3: The speaker stated they are happy a Strategic Plan is
being developed. The speaker supports Option 1 of the resolutions. The speaker attended the
public forums for the plan. The speaker expressed disappointment in the low turnout for public
input. The speaker inquired how many members of the public have downloaded the plan. The
speaker noted great interest in the transportation plan.

S.Parry, Glen Lake Rd - re: item #9.3: The speaker expressed concern about the lack of public
input. The speaker expressed concern regarding protecting identity of those giving public input.
The speaker would like a mail out for public input. re: item #6: The speaker expressed concern
regarding the accuracy of the minutes of October 10, 2023.

A motion was made to extend public participation for 15 minutes for first time speakers. Please
see the motion below.

B. Armstrong, Rodney Rd - re: item #9.3: The speaker supports Option 1 of the resolutions. The
speaker expressed concern regarding the lack of public input. The speaker stated they would like
a mail out to homes in the Langford. The speaker stated they would like focused information
groups for public input.

G. Glowinski, Brock Ave - re: item #9.2: The speaker is available to answer question regarding the
application.

K. Awram, Finlayson Arm Rd - re: item #9.3: The speaker appreciates the efforts that went into
developing the Strategic Plan. The speaker expressed concern regarding the lack of public input

and stated perhaps a mail out would have bolstered public participation. The speaker stated
they would like more consultation with local First Nations with respect to planning and land use.
The speaker expressed they are pleased the Urban Forest Management Plan is in action. The
speaker expressed concern about the lack of affordable housing in Langford. The speaker
supports the film and art industry and supports the growth of greenspaces available to the
public.

C. Lockland, Winster Rd - re: item #9.3: The speaker stated that land use decisions are
permanent and this permanency should be considered.

5.   PUBLIC PARTICIPATION

     Mayor Goodmanson opened public participation at 7:05 pm.

     W. Hobbs, Langford Resident - The speaker expressed concerns regarding the public input
     collected for purchase of the YMCA. The speaker expressed concern regarding the Woodlands
     Park purchase. The speaker expressed concern regarding the E-Comm expense. The speaker
     expressed concern regarding a proposed tax increase. The speaker expressed support for the
     proposed funding of the West Shore RCMP and the Fire Department.

     B. Armstrong, Langford Resident - The speaker expressed concern regarding the maintenance
     fees of the park located at Finlayson Arm. The speaker requested cost cutting measures to lower
     property taxes. The speaker expressed support regarding the proposed funding for West Shore
     RCMP. The speaker expressed concern for the expense required for the unhoused community in
     Langford. The speaker requested a possible staff hiring freeze.

     M. Morton, Langford Resident - The speaker expressed concern regarding proposed increased
     property taxes. The speaker expressed concern regarding the difficulty in seeing the paint lines
     on roads. The speaker expressed concern regarding the Council travel and training expenses. The
     speaker requested a staff hiring freeze.

     T. Sunshine, Langford Resident - The speaker expressed appreciation for the City of Langford's
     budget process. The speaker requested averaging out the tax increases over the next 5 years.

     P. Hamilton, Langford Resident - The speaker requested a few budget items be scrutinized
     further such as the E-bike rebate program, the Royal Roads Innovation Studio, Wi-fi and Internet
     networks.

     S. Sifert, Langford Resident - The speaker expressed concern regarding the rationale for more
     police officers. The speaker expressed concern regarding the West Shore RCMP detachment
     expansion project. The speaker expressed concern regarding the cost of consultants.

     W. Bowers, Langford Resident - The speaker inquired regarding costs of staffing the RCMP and
     Fire Department. The speaker questioned the increase of the Parks and Recreation budget. The
     speaker expressed concern regarding the cost of consultants.

     S. Rossander, Langford Resident - The speaker expressed concern regarding email response time.
     The speaker requested some items be scrutinized such as Council travel and training expenses,
     staff salaries and consulting fees.

     L. Foxall, Langford Resident - The speaker expressed concern regarding the impact of a proposed
     increased property tax on the community. The speaker expressed concern regarding the budget
     survey.

     J. Relf, Langford Resident - The speaker expressed support for funding the proposed West Shore
     RCMP staffing. The speaker requested a decrease in staff workload to levy the need for more
     staff. The speaker requested planning projects be delayed as a cost saving measure. The speaker
     expressed concern regarding staff preparing for the [-Comm expense.

     Council at 7:35 pm made a motion to extend public participation for 30 minutes. Please see the
     vote below.

     Second time speakers

     W. Hobbs, Langford Resident - The speaker expressed support for the cop to pop ratio. The
     speaker expressed requested cuts to staffing and consultants. The speaker requested cuts to the
     Council travel and training expense. The speaker expressed concern regarding the contract with
     Victoria Contracting for outside work. The speaker expressed concern regarding the renovation
     cost at City Hall. The speaker expressed concern regarding the paint lines on roads.

     L. Foxall, Langford Resident - The speaker expressed concern regarding the City's budget for
     wages, salaries, and benefits. The speaker expressed concern regarding the reserve funds. The
     speaker expressed concern regarding the proposed increase of parking fines. The speaker
     expressed concern regarding the City Hall renovation cost. The speaker suggested City staff
     working remotely for a cost saving measure.

     Mayor Goodmanson closed public participation at 7:40 pm.

6.   PUBLIC HEARINGS

     6.1   BYLAW NO. 2082

           "Langford Zoning Bylaw, Amendment No. 679, (Omnibus No. 60 — Various Housekeeping
           Items), Bylaw No. 2082, 2023".

           The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 2082 at 7:52 pm.

           Director of Planning & Subdivision, Matthew Baldwin advised The City of Langford is
           proposing to amend Zoning Bylaw No. 300 in the following ways:

           • By introducing "accessory dormitories which may include a kitchenette" as a
           permitted use in the CD2 (Hull's Field) zone;

           • By removing restrictions on where apartments may occur in the City Centre
           Pedestrian (CCP) Zone excluding Peatt Road, Claude Road, Bryn Maur Avenue, Jacklin
           Road and Veterans Memorial Parkway;

           • By consolidating all daycare capacity exemptions from each zone into Part 3 of the
           Zoning bylaw.

           • By allowing two-family dwellings within the R2 (One-and Two-family Residential)
           zones on lots less than 600m2 but not less than 500m2 if the lot width is 17m.

           • By introducing requirements for accessible parking in all types of multi-family
           residential development.

           Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by the Local Government
           Act.

           Mayor Goodmanson called a first time for presentations.

             M. Wignall, Selwyn Road - Speaker inquired if the changes to the R2 zone are
             independent of new housing legislation.

             M. Baldwin, Director of Planning and Subdivision responded - amendment is
             independent of the new Provincial legislation.

             Mayor Goodmanson called a second time for presentations.

             None presented.

             Mayor Goodmanson called a third time for presentations.

             None presented.

             Mayor Goodmanson declared the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 2082 closed at 7:56 pm.

7.   PUBLIC PARTICIPATION

     P. Hamilton, Langford Resident - re: item 11.1- Speaker expressed support for Bill C-277. Speaker
     expressed a need for accessibility changes within the City. Speaker expressed a need for the
     Capital West Accessibility Advisory Committee to expand membership to include the public and
     allow public participation at meetings.

     W. Bowers, Langford Resident - re: item 5.2 - Speaker expressed support for the presentation. re:
     item 10.4 and 10.5 - Speakers comments were not on topic.

     C. Foxall, Players Drive re: item 5.1- Speaker expressed support for the Ukraine presentation.
     Speaker expressed a need for support and fundraising from residents and the City of Langford to
     support these initiatives. re: item 5.2 - Speaker expressed support for the Westshore Primary
     Care Society and encouraged Council to review options to support.

     M. Wignall, Selwyn Road - re: item 5.1 - Speaker expressed support for the presentations noting
     the importance of coming together to solve these large issues and assist globally. re: item 5.2 -
     Speaker expressed a need for more doctors and supports the work being undertaken by the
     Society. re: item 10.4 - Speaker expressed support for the Transportation Master Plan noting
     there is still an OCP refresh coming. Speaker wished to see Council finish the OCP refresh before
     completing the Transportation Master Plan.

     L. Foxall, Langford Resident - re: item 10.4 and 10.5 - Speaker expressed concern with the
     consultant costs proposed for the Transportation Master Plan & Active Transportation Plan and
     the Parks Master Plan. re: 12.5 - Speaker expressed support for the alternative taxation scheme.
     re: item 5.1 - Speaker expressed support for the Ukraine delegation. re: item 5.2 - Speaker
     expressed support for the work undertaken by the Westshore Primary Care Society.

     W. Hobbs, Luxton Road - re: item 5.1 - Speaker expressed a need for balance with support locally
     as well as globally. re: item 10.4 - Speaker expressed a need to refresh the OCR Speaker
     expressed concern for the use of consultants wishing to see work undertaken by staff instead. re:
     item 5.2 - Speaker expressed a need for Council to advocate to the Provincial government
     regarding health care in our community and beyond.

     S. Sifert, Langford Resident - re: item 10.4 and 10.5 - Speaker noted that the OCP is a Strategic
     Plan. Speaker wished to see amendments done by staff and not consultants. Speaker expressed

      a need to refresh the OCP and not continue producing plans. re: item 12.5 - Speaker expressed

11.   NOTICE OF MOTION

      11.1   Expression of Preference for CRD Director

             Councillor Wagner submitted the following Notice of Motion for consideration at the
             next Regular meeting of Council:

             WHEREAS the position of CRD Director is one of significant regional governance and
             impact;
             AND WHEREAS having a process for the public to provide input aligns with Priority Five
             of the Strategic Plan: Good Governance, increasing transparency and promoting
             democratic values;
             AND WHEREAS allowing public input on a preference for this position is standard
             practice in other municipalities with more than one CRD Director position;
             THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT Council direct staff to prepare a report on what the
             process would be to include an expression of preference for CRD Director as part of the
             2026 election.

      11.2   Permanent Daylight-Saving Time and the Impacts on Safe Routes to School

             Councillor Guiry submitted the following Notice of Motion for consideration at the next
             Regular meeting of Council:

             WHEREAS the adoption of permanent, year-round daylight-saving time means that many
             school age children, including those in the Victoria area who begin their commute
             around 8:00 a.m., will be travelling to school in darkness from early November until the
             end of February;
             AND WHEREAS many communities have older neighbourhoods with wide roadways
             which may cause unintended speeding, limited or non-existent sidewalks or pathways,
             and limited street lighting. Mitigation of these neighbourhood conditions would require
             significant upgrades to ensure safe travel for children during dark winter mornings;
             AND WHEREAS the BC Active Transportation Infrastructure Grant 2025/2026 intake was
             paused pending a review in the fall of 2026, thus limiting the ability of local governments
             to make meaningful change and prepare for the 2026/2027 school year.
             THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT Council direct staff to prepare a letter to the Minister
             of Education and Childcare, the Minister of Transportation and Transit, and the Premier's
             Office, with a copy to all local governments in British Columbia, outlining Council's
             concerns regarding the impacts of adopting year-round Pacific Daylight Time on children
             who would be required to walk to school in the dark.
             AND THAT the letter from the City of Langford Mayor and Council advocate for:
             • the immediate reopening of BC's Active Transportation Infrastructure Grant Program

             for safe routes to school projects;
             • the establishment of a program ensuring all students have access to visibility
             enhancing resources such as lights and reflective gear; and
             • the expansion of The Society for Children and Youth of BC (SCY)'s Walking School Bus
             program.

motions.source_motion_text:
THAT Council:
        1.   Proceed with consideration of first reading of Bylaw No. 1989 to amend the
        policy designation within Langford's OCP from Hillside or Shoreline Policy
        designation to the Business or Light Industrial Policy designation for the
        property located at 1300,1289,1277,1265 and 1253 Valemount Court.
        2. Proceed with consideration of first reading of Bylaw No. 1990 to rezone the
        property at 1300 Valemount Court from RM2A (Attached Housing) Zone to
        BP2A (Business Park - Sooke Road West) and rezone 1289,1277,1265 and 1253
        Valemount Court from Rural Residential (RR5) to Business Park - Sooke Road
        West (BP2A), subject to the following terms and conditions;

        i. That the applicant provides, prior to Public Hearing, the following:

                   a) A technical memo from an engineer that verifies storm water can be
                   adequately managed on-site for the proposed developments, to the satisfaction
                   of the Director of Engineering;
                   b) A Traffic Impact Assessment (TIA) to determine the traffic volume and
                   frequency difference between the current OCP designation (Hillside or
                   Shoreline) to the proposed OCP designation (Business or Light Industrial), to the
                   satisfaction of the Director of Engineering.

                   ii. That the applicant provides, prior to Bylaw Adoption, a section 219
                   covenant, registered in priority of all other charges on titles, that agrees to the
                   following:

                   a) That the developer will connect and be responsible for any upgrades,
                   connections and installation of services and utilities required to support the
                   proposed development, to the standards of Bylaw No. 1000 and to the
                   satisfaction of the Director of Engineering;
                   b) That a formal storm water management plan is submitted and implemented
                   prior to issuance of a building permit or subdivision approval, whichever is first,
                   and implemented, as per Bylaw 1000, all to the satisfaction of the Director of
                    Engineering;
                   c) That a construction parking and traffic management plan, prepared to the
                   satisfaction of the Director of Engineering, be provided prior to the issuance of a
                   building permit.

5.     PUBLIC PARTICIPATION

       W. Bowers, Millstream Rd - item 9 - Speaker asked questions pertaining to correspondence.

     J. Mackenzie, Kettle Creek Terr - item 8.5 - Speaker expressed concern regarding removal of
     parking at 870 McCallum Road. Speaker wished for the exploration of further ideas for parking in
     this area.

     M. Wignall, Selwyn Rd - item 8.2 - Speaker expressed concerns with proposed usage of grant
     funding. Speaker wished for Council to use the grant money for property taxation. Speaker
     expressed concern with an Active Transportation Plan noting challenges for those who cannot
     mode shift.

     S. Plank, Goldstream Ave - item 8.2 - Speaker expressed support for an Active Transportation
     Plan noting growing population and traffic concerns. Speaker also expressed a wish for Council
     to use the grant funds for Official Community Plan (OCP) public engagement.

     R. Louie, Langford - item 8.6 - Speaker expressed support for Option 1 of the Staff Report. Item
     10.3 - Speaker wished for Council to not adopt the bylaw.

     G. Haythornthwaite, Peatt Rd - items 8.2 and 11- Speaker expressed concern regarding public
     participation and Bill 44 (Provincial). Speaker wished to see public input expanded. Speaker
     expressed a wish for jurisdictions to work together when addressing or advocating for changes
     to public participation.

         5.1      Resolution for the Association of Vancouver Island and Coastal Communities

                  Councillor Wagner read aloud the following Notice of Motion:

                  WHEREAS in July 2024, following extensive consultation with First Nations and
                  stakeholders, the Government of BC released its first-ever Coastal Marine Strategy,
                  providing a 20-year vision of "a diverse, productive and resilient coastal marine
                  environment that is valued in its own right and that supports the prosperity, health and
                  well-being of coastal communities now and into the future" (p.3);

                  AND WHEREAS the Coastal Marine Strategy details nine important goals (diverse marine
                  life; abundant wild Pacific Salmon; a clean coast; climate-ready communities; a
                  sustainable coastal economy; vibrant coastal communities; trusting, respectful
                  relationships; a robust tool kit; and integrated and balanced management), but does not
                  have the force of law, and codifying the Strategy into law will support its success and
                  longevity rather than leaving it dependant on the priorities of the government of the
                  day;

                  THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT UBCM call on the Province of British Columbia to
                  enshrine the B.C. Coastal Marine Strategy into law.

motions.source_motion_text:
WHEREAS, local governments provide recreational services to the public, either directly
               or through a third party;

               WHEREAS the City of Langford entered into a long-term tripartite agreement with
               Westhills Land Corporation and the YW/YMCA to provide public funding in support of
               the operation of the Westhills Langford Aquatic Centre;

               WHEREAS Westhills Land Corp., owner of the Westhills Langford Aquatic Centre, wishes
               to transfer ownership of the Westhills Langford Aquatic Centre and the City wishes to
               ensure the continued public access to this important recreational asset; and

               WHEREAS the City has fully explored the risks, benefits and long-term rewards, and has
               provided significant public input opportunities;

      NOW THEREFORE, it is hereby resolved that Council approve the purchase of the
      Westhills Langford Aquatic Centre and the adjacent parking lands for a purchase price
      not to exceed $35,000,000 and authorize the Mayor and Chief Administrative Officer or
      Corporate Officer to execute all documents necessary to complete the purchase.

      AND

      THAT Council direct staff to include this purchase and corresponding funding sources
      and funding requirements within the 2025-2029 Five Year Financial Plan as outlined in
      the presentation by Colliers and staff.

      AND

      THAT Council of the City of Langford authorizes up to $20,000,000 be borrowed, under
      Section 175 of the Community Charter, from the Municipal Finance Authority, for the
      purpose of the purchase of the Westhills Langford Aquatic Centre and the adjacent
      parking lands;

      AND

      THAT that the loan be repaid within five (5) years, with no rights of renewal.

10.   NOTICE OF MOTION
      Councillor Guiry:
      WHEREAS the 2022 Langford Fire Rescue Fire Master Plan recommends for "LFR to begin the
      process of securing funding with City approval to then enter the design phase for a new Fire
      Station #1 to consolidate resources from Fire Station #1 and Fire Station #3" as a short-term
      recommendation that would improve emergency response service delivery in Langford;

      And WHEREAS in 2023 the Province of BC amended Bill 46 to expand what can be levied by
      Development Cost Charges to include fire protection which would share the cost of new fire
      protection infrastructure equitably between existing users and new development;

      THEREFORE, the City of Langford Council directs staff to start planning for a new Fire Station #1
      as recommended in the Langford Fire Rescue Fire Master Plan and establish a DCC Bylaw to
      support the building and development of the new fire station.
      Councillor Wagner:
      WHEREAS UBCM has a Community Excellence Award to recognize and celebrate UBCM member
      First Nations, regional districts, and local governments that have implemented projects or
      programs that go above and beyond in meeting the purposes of local government in BC;
      And WHEREAS the awards are intended to showcase outstanding initiatives and share them with
      other members to implement in their own communities;
      And WHEREAS the City of Langford's Inaugural Strategic Plan meets the criterion set out above;
      Therefore, I move that Council resolve to support the nomination of Langford's Inaugural
      Strategic Plan in being considered for a 2024 UBCM Community Excellence Award.
      Councillor Harder:
      Free Transit for Young People in BC


      WHEREAS the Get On Board Program allows children aged 12 and under to ride all BC Transit and
      Translink transit services free of charge, and this program saves families money while offering
      youth low-carbon transportation that helps the province and municipalities reach emissions and
      transportation mode share targets;

      WHEREAS encouraging young people to use public transportation early in life can lead to lifelong
      habits of sustainable transportation use, and this in turn can have long-term benefits for cities in
      terms of reduced congestion, lower emissions, and increased social inclusion;

      THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT UBCM lobby the Provincial Government expand the Get On

      Board program to include all youth up to the age of 18.


      Free Transit for Seniors in BC

      WHEREAS transportation costs can serve as significant barrier to mobility for many British
      Columbian seniors, and this barrier can contribute to social isolation and adversely affect mental
      and physical well-being;

      WHEREAS removing barriers to seniors using transit encourages a shift towards more sustainable
      transportation, helping lower emissions and reducing congestion, while simultaneously
      increasing affordability, access to essential services, social inclusion, health, and well-being;

      THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT UBCM lobby the Prnvincial Government to make all public
      transit free for seniors (aged 65 years or older).
