5.   PRESENTATIONS

     5.1     Westhills YW/YMCA Langford Aquatic Centre - Matthew Douglas, Colliers Project
             Leaders

             Matthew Douglas, Colliers, delivered a presentation to Council regarding the potential
             purchase of the Westhills YW/YMCA Langford Aquatic Centre and neighbouring parking
             lot.

6.   PUBLIC PARTICIPATION

     L.Foxall, Langford Resident - re: item 5.1- The speaker spoke in support of the current service
     agreement with the West Hills YMCA and expressed concern in relation to the matter. re: item
     9.1.2 - The speaker requested that the per diem stipend not be raised. re: item 9.1.1 - The
     speaker requested that the Community Gardens project be managed by a local farmer.

     S. Rossander, Langford Resident - re: item 5.1 - The speaker requested a town hall meeting for
     the discussion of the purchase of Westhills YMCA and expressed concern in relation to the
     matter.

     W. Hobbs, Langford Resident - re: item 9.1.2 - The speaker requested more information
     regarding dependent care. re: item 9.1.1 - The speaker expressed concern regarding the security
     of the proposed community gardens and suggested a playground be installed in the gardens.

     M. Wignall, Langford Resident - re: item 5.1 - The speaker expressed disappoint that the
     information regarding the purchase of the Westhills YMCA was not made public sooner. The
     speaker expressed they were grateful for the transparency. The speaker questioned the
     management of the Westhills YMCA. re: item 9.1.1 - The speaker spoke in support of a
     playground at the community gardens. re: item 9.1.2 - The speaker requested that Council limit
     the number of members attending conferences.

     B. Armstrong, Langford Resident - re: item 5.1- The speaker inquired if the proposed increase to
     property taxes is based on a possible population growth and whether the lease to the Greater
     Victoria Public Library is a cost to the City of Langford. The speaker inquired if the cost and
     maintenance fees of the Westhills YMCA facility has been compared to other facilities in the
     Greater Victoria area. The speaker inquired about a cost sharing agreement with other local
     municipalities. re: item 9.1.2 - The speaker requested that Council limit the number of members
     attending conferences.

     N.Johal, Langford Resident - re: item 5.1 - The speaker inquired if the Westhills YMCA pays
     property taxes. The speaker inquired if Colliers has a conflict of interest in relation to the matter.
     The speaker inquired regarding rental costs. re: item 9.1.2 - The speaker questioned the per
     diem amount allowed for meals.

     F. Johnson, Langford Resident - re: item 5.1 - The speaker inquired about the approval of
     electors, either in the form of a referendum or an alternate approval process. The speaker
     questioned the use of a loan from the Municipal Finance Authority. The speaker inquired about

     the market value of the property. The speaker expressed concern regarding the lack of the life
     cycle costs for purchasing the Westhills YMCA. re: item 9.1.2 - The speaker expressed that the
     daily per diem rates have not increased in 18 years. The speaker encouraged Council to consider
     the motion for staff to explore dependent care as a qualifying expense.

     Second time presenters:

     W. Hobbs, Langford Resident - re: item 5.1- The speaker requested that a partnership with the
     Westshore municipalities.

     L. Foxall, Langford Resident - re: item 5.1 - The speaker inquired about a board member of the
     Westhills YMCA who is also employed by Colliers.

       PUBLIC HEARINGS

       4.1     BYLAW NO. 2016

               Acting Mayor Wade opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 2016 at 5:34 pm.

               Director of Planning Matthew Baldwin advised that Ruchir Dhall of Architecture Panel
               has applied on behalf of GurbaxSingh and Baldish AujIa to amend the zoning of 640 and





644 Granderson Road froim the 'One- and Two-Family Residential' Zone to the 'City
Centre 1' Zone.

This is being proposed in order to allow for the development of approximately 67
residential units.

In support of this application, the applicant has agreed to provide the following:

1. $750 per unit to the /Affordable Housing Fund.
2. $2,850 per unit to the General Amenity Reserve Fund.
both subject to reductions in accordance with the Affordable Housing and Amenity
Contribution Policy.

Prior to bylaw adoption, the applicant will register a section 219 covenant that agrees to
the following:

1. That both properties are consolidated prior to issuance of a Development Permit.
2. That the design of the building includes a reduced height along the eastern
boundary.
3. That a separate covenant be registered prior to issuance of a building permit to
ensure parking is allocated to each unit.
4. That a strata plan be registered for the building prior to issuance of an occupancy
permit.
5. That 100% of residential parking stalls are capable of providing Level 2 charging for
electric vehicles.
6. That full frontage improvements, a storm water management plan; and a
construction parking management plan be provided and implemented to Bylaw 1000
standards to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering prior to issuance of a
building permit.

This proposal is consistent with the 'CityCentre' designation of the Official Community
Plan.

Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by the Local
Government Act

Ruchir Dhall, representing the applicant, gave a presentation of the proposed
development, noting the project location and proposed design, and answered questions
on rentals and access to the proposed building

Acting Mayor Wade called a first time for presentations.

B. Milne. 644 Goldstream Avenue, asked whether a traffic plan has been made available.
It was noted that the traffic plan has been received by the City.

L. Plomp, 3592 Whimfield Terr, expressed concerns that the proposed development
does not fit with the neighbourhood and asked for clarifications on the traffic impact
assessment.


D. Martino, #102-643 Granderson Rd. expressed concerns about the impacts to parking
spaces.

Acting Mayor Wade called a second time for presentations.





      Acting Mayor Wade called for a third and final time for presentations. There being none,
      he declared the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 2016 closed at 5:48 pm.

4.2   BYLAW NO. 2034

      Acting Mayor Wade opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 2034 at 5:48 pm.

      Director of Planning Matthew Baldwin advised that Golf BC Holdings Inc. has applied to
      amend the text of the CD4 (Comprehensive Development - Olympic View) zone at 749
      Latoria Road, 781 Gwendolynn Drive, 655 Frederick, and an unaddressed parcel off
      Willing Drive (the Olympic View Lands).

      This is being proposed in order to allow for various zoning changes including increasing
      the total number of allowable residential units from 461 to 1000, increasing the total
      number of allowable hotel units, expanding the allowable commercial uses, removing
      the area delineations, introducing an amenity contribution per residential unit,
      increasing the required amount of open space from 15% to 40%, and adjusting the
      height and minimum lot sizes.

      In support of this application, the applicant has agreed to provide the following:

      1. That prior to bylaw adoption, the updated Master Development Agreement will be
      secured through a Section 219 Covenant registered in priority of all other charges on
      title that includes the following:

                 a) That the developer will construct full frontage improvements in
                    accordance with Bylaw 1000 to the satisfaction of the Director of
                    Engineering which shall include the following:

                             i.   Sidewalk or a minimum 3.0 m wide multi-use paved trail on
                                  one side, boulevard/trees, and streetlights along the
                                  Gwendolynn frontage;
                                   ii. A multi-use gravel road edge trail behind split rail fencing
                                   along the Klahanie Drive frontage;
                                   iii. Bike lanes and a flashing pedestrian crossing lined up with
                                   Desmond Drive to provide access to the multi-use trail on the
                                   north side of the road along Latoria;
                                   iv. Multi-use trail and/or sidewalks per the Olympic View
                                  master plan in addition to boulevards and landscaping on all
                                  new interior roads;

                  b) That the developer provides a stormwater management plan,
                     construction parking management plan, and that any necessary above or
                     underground infrastructure or servicing upgrades, extensions or other
                     required servicing requirements are to be fulfilled to the standards of
                     Bylaw 1000 and the Director of Engineering, and that costs incurred will
                     be the responsibility of the developer;

                  c) That the applicant agrees to implement the recommendations garnered
                      from the submitted Traffic Impact Assessment;





                       d)   Acknowledgment that the proximity to agricultural operations and to the
                            South Vancouver Island Rangers has the potential to create conflict and
                            nuisances for residents;

                       e)   That 40% of the land will be used for open space, in general compliance
                            with the Open Space Plan attached as Appendix A;

           2. That prior to bylaw adoption, the current Section 219 Covenant registered on title
           that contains the existing Master Development Agreement be discharged;

           This proposal is consistent with the Official Community Plan Hillside or Shoreline
           designation.

           Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by the Local
           Government Act.

           The applicant gave a presentation on the proposed project, outlining the project
           benefits.

           Acting Mayor Wade called a first time for presentations.

           L. Plomp. 3592 Whimfield Terr, expressed concerns about the traffic, the lack of public
           access to the area, and inadequate public consultation.

           Acting Mayor Wade called a second time for presentations.

           Acting Mayor Wade called for a third and final time for presentations.

           G. Willing, 739 Willing Drive, expressed support for the project.

           Acting Mayor Wade declared the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 2034 closed at 6:08 pm.

4.2   BYLAW NO. 2066

      Councillor Wade opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 2066 at 5:35pm.

      Director of Planning Matthew Baldwin advised that David McGrath has applied on
      behalf of Paradise Homes Ltd to amend the zoning of 2870 and 2874 Peatt Road from
      the R2 (One- and Two-Family Residential) Zone to the CCP (City Centre Pedestrian) Zone.

      This is being proposed in order to allow for the development of a six-storey mixed-use
      building with approximately 44 residential units and 376 nl2 of commercial space.

      in support of this application, the applicant has agreed to provide the following:

      1.   The following contributions as a bonus for increased density:
      a. $750 per SFE towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund;
      b. $2,850 per SFE towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund; and
      c. $10.75 per m2 of commercial gross floor area.


      2. That frontage improvements, a stormwater management plan, as well as a
      construction parking and traffic management plan are provided to Bylaw 1000
      standards to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering prior to the issuance of a
      Building Permit;

      3. That the developer will connect and be responsible for any upgrades required to the
      services and utilities required for the development;





4. That the building be strata titled into individual residential units prior to the
issuance of an occupancy permit, to the satisfaction of the Approving Officer;


5. That the developer consolidate the parcels in accordance with the CCP zone
regulations, prior to the issuance of a development permit;


6. That a separate covenant be registered prior to issuance of a building permit for the
proposed residential building(s) that ensures parking is allocated to each unit and
visitors as required by the zoning bylaw and is not provided in exchange for
compensation separate from that of a residential unit; and


7. That 100% of residential parking spaces, excluding visitor parking spaces, shall
feature an energized outlet capable of providing Level 2 charging or higher to the
parking space; and
a. Energized outlets shall be labelled for the use of electric vehicle charging;
b. Where an electric vehicle energy management system is implemented (load
sharing), a qualified professional may specify a minimum performance standard to
ensure a sufficient rate of electric vehicle charging; and
c. The owner is required to keep the Electric Vehicle ServicingEquipment (EVSE) in
operation and the Strata Council may not prevent an owner, occupant, or tenant from
installing the EV charging equipment.

Council has also, by resolution, directed staff to prepare a bylaw to amend the CCP Zone
to change the interior side lot line and rear lot line setback requirement of 5 meters to
apply when the adjoining lot is zoned to permit a building of 7 or more storeys in height.
This proposal is consistent with the Official Community Plan CityCentre designation.

Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by the Local
Government Act.

The Mayor returned to the meeting at 5:37pm.

Councillor Wade called a first time for presentations.

The applicant, WAArchitects, gave a presentation on the proposal, providing
information on the project location and design.

W. Hobbs. 3442 Luxton Rd. posed questions about underground parking.

Councillor Wade called a second time for presentations.

None presented.

Councillor Wade called for a third and final time for presentations.

None presented.

Councillor Wade declared the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 2066 closed at 5:51 pm.





4.3   BYLAW NO. 2067

      Councillor Wade opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 2067 at 5:52pm.

      Director of Planning Matthew Baldwin advised that Rachael Sansom of Grayland
      ConsultingLtd. has applied on behalf of Steve and Deineke Boudewyn to amend the
      zoning of 892 Walfred Road from the Rural Residential 5 (RR5) to the One- and Two-
      Family Residential (R2) Zone.

      This is being proposed in order to allow for the development of approximately a five lot
      bare land strata subdivision.

      in support of this application, the applicant has agreed to provide the following:

      1. The following contributions as a bonus for increased density:
      a.   $660 per small Lot to the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund;
      b.   $3,960 per small lot to the General Amenity Reserve Fund; and
      c.   $1,000 per lot 550 m2 or more in area to the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund;
      d.   $6,000 per lot 550 m2or more in area to the General Amenity Reserve Fund.

      2.   That a section 219 covenant be registered, that agrees:

      a. That frontage improvements, a stormwater management plan, as well as a
      construction parking and traffic management plan are provided to Bylaw 1000
      standards to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering prior to the issuance of a
      Building Permit;

      b. That a non-disturbance covenant be registered over 20% of the lands to preserve
      these areas as greenspace prior to subdivision approval, to the satisfaction of the
      Approving Officer; and

      c. That vegetation within the road allowance on Walfred Road should be retained. If
      any vegetation is removed, the applicant is required to replant the area and provide a
      temporary irrigation system from a private irrigation system to the satisfaction of the
      Manager of Park.

      This proposal is consistent with the Official Community Plan Hillside or Shoreline
      designation.

      Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by the Local
      Government Act.

      Councillor Wade called a first time for presentations.

      The applicant, Grayland Consulting Ltd., gave a presentation on the proposal, providing

motions.source_motion_text:
WHEREAS the City of Langford acknowledges the vital role of health care, mental
        health care, and social services in building a resilient and safe community;

        WHEREAS the Province's failure to meet its commitments in these areas has
        unfairly burdened municipalities, straining local resources and compromising
        public safety, thus exacerbating social inequity through heightened property
        taxes;

        THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT the Association of Vancouver Island and
        Coastal Communities (AVICC) strongly urges increased Provincial funding and
        support for health care, mental health care, and comprehensive housing
        initiatives. Immediate action is necessary to alleviate the strain on municipal
        resources and enhance public safety;

        FURTHER BE IT RESOLVED THAT the AVICC calls on the Provincial government to
        demonstrate good faith by covering the heightened share of policing costs. This
        recognizes the Provincial responsibility in shifting these public safety costs to
        municipalities due to inadequate provision of social services and health care.

3.     PUBLIC HEARINGS

       3.1     BYLAW NO. 2000

              The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 2000 at 5:34 pm.

               Director of Planning Matthew Baldwin advised that Ryan McKenzie has applied on
               behalf of Westhills Land Corp. to amend the text and schedule map of the CD3
               (Comprehensive Development — Westhills) Zone to allow for various zoning changes.


Some of the proposed zone changes include the following:
- Consolidating the 6 sub-areas of the Comprehensive Development Zone into four:
Community Core, Single Family and Multi-Family Residential, Amenity Area, and
Business Park.
- Allowing additional uses in the community core and amenity area
- Allowing certain commercial uses in residential areas such as bakeries, day cares,
medical clinics, and restaurants.
- Making minor changes to the subdivision requirements for new single-family lots.
- Making changes to the Business Park regulations to better align with other Business
Park zones in the City of Langford
- Requiring the developer to pay an amenity fee for new residential units
- Restructuring how physical amenities will be constructed and increasing the
minimum construction value
- Reducing the allowable number of residential units outside of the Community Core
by 1000 units
- Increasing the allowable density in the Community Core

Additionally, as part of this application, staff are working with the developer to update
the Master Development Agreement, creating a new Parkland Dedication Agreement,
and updating the Open Space Master Plan. All to reflect what Westhills has contributed,
based on their current zoning, and what remains to be contributed.

As part of this application, a public hearing is required in accordance with the
regulations of the Local Government Act.

In support of these/this application, the applicant has agreed to provide the following:


1. That prior to bylaw adoption, a Section 219 Covenant is registered on title in priority
of all other charges on title that secures the updated Master Development Agreement;

2. That prior to bylaw adoption, the current Section 219 Covenant registered on title
that contains the existing Master Development Agreement be discharged;

3. That prior to bylaw adoption, the applicant enter into a Parkland Dedication
Agreement with the City to the satisfaction of the Chief Administrative Officer which
shall include the following:
I. That 40% of the lands as generally shown on Appendix D shall be dedicated to the
City at the time of adjacent development;
ii. Notwithstanding (i), that 35 acres of land located within the red outlined portion as
shown on Appendix D, inclusive of the rock-climbing area, shall be transferred to the
City within 6 months of the adoption of this bylaw;
iii. That the content within the existing Master Development Agreement in relation to
the timing of parkland dedication be included;

4. That prior to bylaw adoption, the applicant enter into an agreement securing that
Westhills Land Corp. shall construct a railway platform and station should passenger rail
service be re-instated along the E&N corridor, to the satisfaction of the Chief
Administrative Officer.


             This proposal is consistent with the Official Community Plan Hillside or Shoreline, Village
             Centre, and Neighbourhood Centre designations.

             Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by the Local
             Government Act.

             The Mayor called a first time for presentations.

             Ryan McKenzie of Westhills gave a presentation on the history and current proposal for
             zoning at Westhills.

             Mayor Young called a second time for presentations.

             None presented.

             Mayor Young called a third and final time for speakers. There being none, he declared
             the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 2000 closed at 5:52 p.m.

motions.source_motion_text:
THAT Council:

   1. Consider bringing forward Bylaw No. 2235 for 1st, 2nd, and 3rd readings
      at a future Council meeting in order to amend the zoning designation of
      the properties located at 897 Walfred Road from RR5 to R2, and subject
      to the following terms and conditions:

       a.    That the applicant provides, as a bonus for increased density, the
             following contributions per new lot created, prior to subdivision
             approval:

             i.   $1,000 towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund, for lots
                  with lot area of 550m2 or above;

            ii. $660 towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund, for lots
                with lot area under 550 m2;

            iii. $6,000 towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund, for lots with
                 lot area of 550 m2 or above; and

            iv. $3,960 towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund, for lots with
                lot area under 550 m2;

       b. That the applicant, prior to Bylaw Adoption, registers a Section 219
          covenant in priority of all other charges on title, that agrees to the
          following:

            i.    That the following will be provided and implemented to Bylaw
                  No. 1000 standards to the satisfaction of the Director of
                  Engineering prior to subdivision approval or Building Permit
                  issuance, whichever is first:

                  1. Full frontage improvements;

                  2. A comprehensive Geotechnical Plan; and

                  3. A Storm Water Management Plan.

            ii. That the following will be provided and implemented to Bylaw
                No. 1000 standards to the satisfaction of the Director of
                Engineering prior to any land alterations:

                  1. A Mitigation Plan; and

                  2. A Construction Parking and Delivery Management Plan.

            iii. That tree protection measures, inclusive of tree protection
                 fencing, are implemented prior to commencement of work to
                 protect the trees identified for retention in the arborist report,
                 prepared by Capital Tree Service Inc. and dated May 14, 2025,
                 throughout the construction period;

                                 iv. That a separate non-disturbance covenant be registered over
                                     32.6% of the land to be protected as open space, prior to
                                     subdivision approval, to the satisfaction of the Approving
                                     Officer;

                                 v. That vegetation within the road allowance on Walfred Road
                                    should be retained. If any vegetation is removed, the applicant
                                    is required to replant the area and provide a private temporary
                                    irrigation system to the satisfaction of the Director of Parks,
                                    Recreation and Facilities; and

                                 vi. That all concrete used on-site will utilize ready-mix concrete
                                     that meets or exceeds the weighted average Global Warming
                                     Potential targets based on Concrete BC Baseline (average) mix
                                     data, and that prior to the issuance of a Building Permit the
                                     applicant shall provide a Type III Environmental Product
                                     Declaration that is 3rd party verified specifying the total Global
                                     Warming Potential value and confirming that the proposed
                                     development meets the requirements of Low Carbon Concrete
                                     Policy POL-0167-PLAN.

motions.source_motion_text:
WHEREAS on December 5, 2022, Council considered a recommendation to name
        the Kettle Creek Linear Park and Playground after former Councillor Winnie
        Sifert in recognition of her long service to the City of Langford.

        AND WHEREAS Council determined that any decision regarding the naming of
        this park should be deferred until after the adoption of an amended or new park
        naming policy and that adoption has now occurred.

        AND WHEREAS a more suitable park has been identified to be named given its
        proximity to Winnie Sifert's neighbourhood,

        NOW THEREFORE, I move that Council rename Ernhill Park to "Winnie Sifert
        Park" and direct staff to work with former Councillor Sifert's family on a formal
        naming ceremony to be held prior to December 15, 2025.
motions.source_block:
MOVED BY: HARDER
        SECONDED: WAGNER

        WHEREAS on December 5, 2022, Council considered a recommendation to name
        the Kettle Creek Linear Park and Playground after former Councillor Winnie
        Sifert in recognition of her long service to the City of Langford.

        AND WHEREAS Council determined that any decision regarding the naming of
        this park should be deferred until after the adoption of an amended or new park
        naming policy and that adoption has now occurred.

        AND WHEREAS a more suitable park has been identified to be named given its
        proximity to Winnie Sifert's neighbourhood,

        NOW THEREFORE, I move that Council rename Ernhill Park to "Winnie Sifert
        Park" and direct staff to work with former Councillor Sifert's family on a formal
        naming ceremony to be held prior to December 15, 2025.

                                                                                Motion CARRIED.

motions.source_motion_text:
THAT the Main Motion be amended in the following ways with respect to Bylaw No.
2255:

1.Adding a new Section 30(7) to the end of Division 2 - Construction and Commercial
Noise Regulations that reads: "(7) All approved permits must be made available on the
City's website in an easily accessible location before the date(s) of the activities. The
information provided must include the applicant, the applicant's company, contact
information, exact location using the municipal address and PID, the times and date(s) of
the activities, the precise nature of the activity that will create the noise, and the
detailed reasons why the exception of the permitted hours in the Community Standards
Bylaw is warranted."; and

2. Adding "and has committed in writing to follow" after "of" and before "all" in Section
34 titled "Responsibility for Sub-contractors."
motions.source_block:
MOVED BY: PLOMP
      SECONDED: JOHNSON


THAT the Main Motion be amended in the following ways with respect to Bylaw No.
2255:

1.Adding a new Section 30(7) to the end of Division 2 - Construction and Commercial
Noise Regulations that reads: "(7) All approved permits must be made available on the
City's website in an easily accessible location before the date(s) of the activities. The
information provided must include the applicant, the applicant's company, contact
information, exact location using the municipal address and PID, the times and date(s) of
the activities, the precise nature of the activity that will create the noise, and the
detailed reasons why the exception of the permitted hours in the Community Standards
Bylaw is warranted."; and

2. Adding "and has committed in writing to follow" after "of" and before "all" in Section
34 titled "Responsibility for Sub-contractors."

                                                                          Motion CARRIED.

5.   PUBLIC PARTICIPATION

     R. Hobbs. Luxton Rd - re: item 6.1 - The speaker inquired about including a youth drop-in centre.
     Inquired about the the grant money being allocated for a youth centre.
     M. Dillabaugh, Director of Finance - responded that a youth centre could be an option for the
     funding.

     W. Hobbs. Luxton Rd - re: item 6.1 - The speaker inquired about the amenities. Inquired about
     the Road DCCs funding.

     M. Dillabaugh, Director of Finance - responded by explaining the Parks DCC's and the Road DCCs
     M. Wignall. Selwvn Rd - re: item 6.1 - The speaker commented on risk management in hiring fire
     fighters through an extended period of time. The speaker inquired why the City needs more
     staff. The speaker was concerned about the purchase of the YMCA.

     S. Hartlieb. Bombardier Cres - re: item 6.1 - The speaker inquired about a fire truck purchase
     being included in the budget. The speaker inquired about the Juan De Fuca recreation centre,
     and to which municipality is responsible for it. The speaker inquired about other municipalities
     contributing to the YMCA costs. The speaker thanked City staff for their presentation.

     S. Sifert. Waifred Rd - re: item 6.1 - The speaker is concern about the increase in tax rate. The
     speaker discussed amenity fees. The speaker would like the sewer connection fees to be
     lowered and amenity fees increased. The speaker is very concerned about a 12% tax increase.

     R. Barrea. Goldstream Ave - re: item 6.1 - The speaker is very concerned about the tax increase,
     and how it will affect the housing market.

     L. Foxall. Plavers Dr - re: item 6.1 - The speaker would like the tax increase 3-5%. The speaker
     would like the hiring of new Citystaff should be done over five years. The speaker believes the
     decrease in investments in the City, has affected the increase to property taxes. The speaker
     inquired about a contract being signed sooner with the YMCA. The speaker agrees with previous
     speakers regarding the fire budget. The speaker is very concerned about the tax increase and
     how it will affect those most vulnerable in the community.

     L. Plomp. Whimfield Terr - re: item 6.1 - The speaker thanked the Mayor, Council and City staff
     for including the public in the budget discussions. The speaker supports the increase in number
     of firefighters hired. The speaker had suggestions regarding budget savings. The speaker made
     suggestions for specific removal of line items being removed from the budget.

     M. Dillabaugh, Director of Finance - responded by explaining that the removal of the items
     would not affect the property tax rate.

     Nicholas Johal. Waifred PI - re: item 6.1 - The speaker inquired about the tax increase. The
     speaker inquired about the increase to City staff. The speaker supports the hiring of 4 new
     firefighters. The speaker is very concerned about the amount of the tax increase.

     M. Dillabaugh, Director of Finance - responded by explaining the budget for building permit
     revenue is the same as 2022.



B. Hutchins, Director of Corporate Services - responded by explaining that the increase staff
does not affect planning, engineering, or building. The added staff are for population growth to
the City.

B. Armstrong. Rodney Rd - re: item 6.1 - The speaker inquired about the road DCC's costs. The
speaker inquired about parks being funded.

M. Dillabaugh, Director of Finance - responded by explaining the borrowing of funds from Parks
DCC's does not mean they won't be paid back. That the money is used upfront then collected
when projects are completed. They explained that Parks DCC's has plenty of funding for it's own
projects.

S. Rossander. Ravensview Dr - re: item 6.1 - The speaker inquired about the revenues. The
speaker inquired about how confident the City is about the amount of non property revenues.
The speaker inquired if the City is on track with the expected revenues. The speaker compared
the revenues to expenditures and inquired where the money is.

M. Dillabaugh, Director of Finance - responded by that the City is confident based on trends.
That the City doesn't overstate revenues. They also responded that the City is on track with
expected revenues. The Director of Finance responded that that the funds are unaudited. If the
numbers are correct, the funds will then get added to the surplus at the end of the year.
W. Hobbs. Luxton Rd - re: item 6.1 - The speaker inquired about legal options of the contract
with YMCA. The speaker inquired about a referendum regarding funding the YMCA. The speaker
inquired about having other municipalities assist with funding the YMCA.

M. Dillabaugh, Director of Finance - responded by explaining the City is legally responsible for
the funding of the YMCA. Purchasing the YMCA is an option.

Nicholas Johal. Walfred PI - The speaker inquired about the proposed staff positions in the
budget.

Darren Kiedyk, CAO - responded that the staff positions descriptions will be made available in
the budget section of the City's website.

Braden Hutchins, Director of Corporate Services - responded by directing the speaker to a staff
report from the Committee of the Whole meeting, February 27, 2023.

M. Wignall. Selwvn Rd - re: item 6.1 - The speaker noted a discrepancy of line items of the
published budget report.

M. Dillabaugh, Director of Finance - responded that the total column does not impact anything.
They assured the speaker they would look into the error.

S. Sifert. Walfred Rd - re: item 6.1 - The speaker spoke to the amount of the increase of
firefighters. The speaker supports increasing the amount of police. The speaker inquired about
the proposed staff positions.

S. Rossander. Ravensview Dr - re item 6.1 - The speaker suggested that maybe there is a middle
ground solution for funding the YMCA.

N. Johal. Walfred PI - re: item 6.1 - The speaker concerned about the tax increase. The speaker
inquired about the YMCA, what is the cost of maintenance of the building. The speaker inquired



        how any developments have been approved since October 2022. The speaker inquired about a
        youth centre supporting the Guides and Scouts.

        Braden Hutchins, Director of Corporate Services - responded that the City is in preliminary
        stages of any decision regarding the YMCA.

              Recreation Facilities Master Plan project.

13.   NOTICE OF MOTION

      Notice of Motion from Councillor Guiry

      Whereas Rick Hansen Foundation Accessibility CertificationTM (RHFAC) is a national rating system
      that measures and certifies the level of meaningful access of buildings and sites and the Rick
      Hansen Foundation found that 64% of Canadians have a disability or take care of a person with a
      disability.

      And whereas, one of the key findings of a 2020 Cost Comparison Feasibility Study issued by
      HCMA Architecture + Design was that when meeting the National Building Code there was a cost

      increase of 1% to achieve Rick Hansen Foundation Certified Gold which reinforces that
      "accessibility can be achieved with minimal cost impact through commitment to
      thoughtful/universal design".

      Therefore, Langford Council directs staff to consider Rick Hansen Foundation Accessibility
      CertificationTM (RHFAC) when completing the upcoming review of Langford's Design Guidelines
      and through this process consider a possible timeline for adopting RHFAC as a standard for all
      new buildings in Langford.

4.2   BYLAW NO. 1999


      The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1999 at 5:44 pm.

Director of Planning Matthew Baldwin advised that Ben Gulbrandsen has applied on
behalf of Jill Moores, Barry Moores, Janis Bayley, Lamar Grube, Patricia Van Buskirk,
Peter Van Buskirk, and Peter Lasell to amend the zoning of 2762, 2768, and 2774
Winster Road from the R2 (One- and Two-Family Residential) Zone to the CCl (City
Centre) Zone.

This is being proposed to allow for the development of a six-storey apartment building.

In support of this application, the applicant has agreed to provide the following as a
bonus for increased density:

a. $750 per unit to the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund; and
b. $2,850 per unit to the General Amenity Reserve Fund.

Subject to reductions depending on the use and height in accordance with the
Affordable Housing and Amenity Contribution Policy.

2. That the applicant also agrees to provide, prior to bylaw adoption, a Section 219
covenant, registered in priority of all other charges on title, that agrees to the following:

a. That frontage improvements, a stormwater management plan and a construction
parking and traffic management plan are provided to Bylaw 1000 standards to the
satisfaction of the Director of Engineering prior to the issuance of a Building Permit:

b. That the developer registers a strata plan, prior to the issuance of an occupancy
permit, that creates individual strata titles for each residential unit;

c. That a separate covenant be registered prior to issuance of a building permit for the
proposed residential building that ensures parking is allocated to each unit and visitors
as required by the zoning bylaw and is not provided in exchange for compensation
separate from that of a residential unit;

d. That 100% of residential parking spaces, excluding visitor parking spaces, shall
feature an energized outlet capable of providing Level 2 charging or higher to the
parking space; and

i. Energized outlets shall be labelled for the use of electric vehicle charging;
ii. Where an electric vehicle energy management system is implemented (load
sharing), a qualified professional may specify a minimum performance standard to
ensure a sufficient rate of electric vehicle charging; and
iii. The owner is required to keep the Electric Vehicle Servicing Equipment (EVSE) in
operation and the Strata Council may not prevent an owner, occupant, or tenant from
installing the EV charging equipment.

Council has also, by resolution, authorized the Director of Planning to issue a variance to
reduce the northern interior side lot line setback from the required 3m to 1.5m for a
stairwell within the Form and Character Development Permit.
This proposal is consistent with the Official Community Plan City Centre designation.

Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by the Local
Government Act.

Mayor Young called a first time for presentations.

B. Gulbrandsen, on behalf of the applicant - Pacific Viking Group has been a family
business since 2003. Projects are based on the OCP. Realizes that Council must weigh
the concerns of the community. An increase of inventory is what's needed in the City of
Langford. Architect Alan Lowe has designed the building.

A. Lowe; Architect, on behalf of the applicant - presented a Power Point summary of the
proposed development.

Councillor Szpak inquired about bicycle storage.

M. Rogers. 2711 Windman Ln - 3 concerns to Concerns about of traffic in the area, six
storeys is too high. Finally, tree protection. Curious about what will happen to the trees?
Question for Watt Consulting. What determines a significant impact on traffic?

P. Frigga. 1010 Graphite PI - Supports the project, that more affordable housing is
needed.

G. Sinclair. 689 Hoffman Ave. - Feels the local residents are not being heard. Would like
to see the traffic assessment. Wants to know why the public doesn't have access to
them. What is the proposal to save trees? The construction will impact the area.

C. Miller 552 Hoffman Ave. - Would like to submit their opposition to the proposal.
Committee ignored the concern to lower the height of the development. The area will
have added traffic. Believes it is unsafe in the area. Did the traffic assessment consider
all the traffic in the area? difficult to turn out of the area. Not enough on street parking.
Neighboring schools are at capacity.

J. Rol, 2779 Winster Ave. - Echoes the previous callers concerns. Believes that a six-
storey building it too much capacity for the area. Is there a loading zone provided?
Actively selling his home after 30 years.

L. Shaw. 2739 Winster Rd - Cornered about the amount of increased traffic to the area.
Street parking is unavailable.

S. Russel, 2593 Millstream Rd - In favour of the project. Is in the downtown core. Will be
adjacent to amentias. Families need access to housing.

M. McKav, 605-784 Hocklev Ave - Commends Council for considering development. The
developer is building nice structures. We need densification in the core.

S. Gearv, 1375 Bear Mountain Pkwv - Echoes local residents concerns. No affordable
housing has been added to the market from Langford. Concerned about outside support
to the area development and local residents not being heard.

A. Churchill. 658 Atkins Ave - Echoes the concerns of the local residents. Has
communicated with City staff about the development. Believes the development is too
big, Traffic will only increase. Why is the traffic assessment not available to the public?
What does significant impact mean? Believes the development is not in the City Centre
Zone. Not enough street parking available.

Scott. 1251 Flint Ave - In full support of this project. Believes in affordable housing.
Believes social, local connections are stronger by attracting new businesses. Likes having
owner owned housing. But City needs more supply for renters. Regarding a dedicated

left turn signal could help with traffic. Sustainable housing will allow more affordable
housing.

R. Cravcroft. 738 Waifred Rd - Supports the projects. Likes all the bicycle parking
available. The upgrades to the area will be welcome. Commended Council for their
work.

N. Duvf, 689 Hoffman Ave - Lives beside the development. The area is busy with traffic.
The infrastructure in area is failing. Parking is unavailable in the area. Possibly build
something with a lower density. Would like details of the traffic assessment. Has
concerns about the trees being removed. There were no changes made from the
Committee recommendations.

Watts Consulting responded - Regarding the traffic assessment, followed industry
standards. Did an a.m. and p.m. assessment of the traffic. Explained the grading system
that is used in traffic assessments.

H. Webber. #405-110 Huxlev PI - Supports the development, as it will help supply a
housing shortage.

M. Wignall. #202-774 Goldstream Ave - Has watched the community grow. Asking
Council that if six storeys too tall for City core? Its going to be the perfect place. Schools
will be built based on the growth of the area. We need to accommodate the demand.

L. Faulkner. 2707 Windman Ln - Is a teacher in the area. Concern is the proximity of
another development. There are not enough exits out of the area. Access to the school
is difficult. Condominiums are not an option for families.

A. Schultz, 552 Hoffman Ave - Echoes the other callers concerns. Does the traffic
assessment consider of the growth to the area? Believes six storeys is too high for the
area.


A. Thompson. 650 Hovlake Ave - Caller is not a resident in the area. But sees the traffic
to the area. Unsure of the affordable phrase, doesn't meant the same to everyone. No
place for rapid transit. Does not support the rezoning.

R. Coutrev, #205-847 Goldstream Ave. - Supports the development. The downtown core
has been designed with thought and time over several years. Wishes Council to stay on
the path to grow the downtown area. There is a huge demand for housing. The Official
City Plan states the demand and where the housing should be. The region is growing,
housing is needed. Road improvements are being done. There is plenty of recreation
based on the contributions from development.

M. Wagner #104-2669 Deville Rd - There is no shortage of people wanting to move here.
But growth should be done in a thoughtful way. Keep up with the amenities available to

S Gearv, 1375 Bear Mountain Pkwv - Can't undo something that has already been done.
Caller supports density. Believes the infrastructure is not available for this development.

      C. Harder, 844 Goldstream Ave. - Echoes the previous callers concerns. The building

      pace of development.

      Mayor Young called a second time for presentations.

      C. Burg. 615 Hoffman Ave. - Caller is not in favour of the development. What time in the

      Mayor Young responded - asked staff a question about the traffic light near the

      Michelle Mahovlich; Director of Engineering and Public Works, responded - We can

      N. Duvf, 689 Hoffman Ave. - Concern about the proposed traffic circle.

      L. Faukner, 2707 Windman Ln - Concern about the roundabout proposal.

     5.1   BYLAW NO. 2098

           "Langford Zoning Bylaw, Amendment No. 692, (2833, 2835, 2837, and 2839 Knotty Pine
           Road) Bylaw No. 2098, 2022."

           The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 2098 at 8:08 p.m.

           Director of Planning Matthew Baldwin adyised that Alex Gannochka of ADEPT
           Engineering Ltd. has applied on behalf of 829 Development Group Ltd. to rezone 2822,
           2835, 2837, and 2839 Knotty Pine Road from the One- and Two-Family Residential (R2)
           Zone to the City Centre 2 (CC2) Zone.

           This is being proposed in order to allow for the development of a townhouse project
           with approximately 26 units.

           Prior to Public Hearing, Council required the following items:

                   1. A technical memo from an engineer that verifies stormwater can be
                   adequately managed on-site for the proposed developments, to the satisfaction
                   of the Director of Engineering;

                   2. A memo prepared by a Landscape Architect that examines existing trees on
                   site and in the frontage and provides comment on the potential for tree
                   retention as part of the development plan, to the satisfaction of the Director of
                   Planning;

                   3.   A revised site plan to the satisfaction of the Director of Planning;

           The above items have all been completed and were considered and accepted by Council
           during their meeting held on February 6th, 2023. The revised site plan allows for three
           existing trees to be maintained and includes a dedication of 5% of the lot to the City.

In further support of this application, the applicant has agifeed to provide the following:

    1. That the applicant will provide the following contributions per unit, prior to the
        issuance of a building permit:

        1.   $1,000 towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund; and

        2. $3,800 towards the General Amenity Reserve|Fund.
    2. That the applicant provides, prior to Bylaw Adoption, a Section 219 covenant,
       registered in priority of all other charges on that title, that agrees:

        a. That the following be implemented to Bylaw No. 1000 standards to the
        satisfaction of the Director of Engineering prior to; the issuance of a building
        permit:

             1. Full frontage improvements, inclusive of sidewalks, bike lanes, road
             edge parking, streetlighting, and boulevard upgrades; and
             2.     A storm water management plan.

        b. That a Construction Park and Traffic Managennent Plan be provided to the
        satisfaction of the Director of Engineering prior to any alteration of land;

        c. That the four subject properties be consolidated prior to the issuance of a
        Development Permit for Form and Character;

        d. That a separate covenant be registered agreeing that the garages and
        carports are to be used for the parking of vehicles and not the storage of items
        preventing the parking of vehicles therein.

        e. That all concrete used on-site will be produced using post-industrial C02
        mineralization technology, or equivalent which offers concrete with lower
        embodied C02 than all other competing bids, and that prior to the issuance of a
        Building Permit the applicant shall provide a prodgct-specific Type III
        Environmental Product Declaration that is 3rd party verified specifying the total
        embodied carbon content of concrete.

        f. That 5% of the lot area be dedicated to the City at the southwest corner of
        the lot, inclusive of the Garry Oak and Bigleaf Maple trees, prior to the issuance
         of a building permit;

         g. That the tree protection measures outlined in the arborist report be
         implemented throughout construction to protectjthe Garry Oak, BigleafMaple,
         and Cypress trees that have retention potential, inclusive of tree protection
         fencing.

This proposal is consistent with the Official Community Plan City Centre designation.

Government Act.

6.   PUBLIC HEARINGS

     6.1   BYLAW NO. 2009

           The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 2009 at 6:13 pm.

           Director of Planning Matthew Baldwin advised that Matthew Moradian has applied on
           behalf of Langford Central Developments Inc. to amend the zoning of 2739 to 2751
           Scafe Road and 2746 Peatt Road from the 'One-and Two-Family Residential' Zone to the
           'City Centre Pedestrian' Zone.

This is being proposed in order to allow for the development of 2 mixed-used buildings
that would be 18 and 24 storeys in height.

As part of this application, a public hearing is required in accordance with the
regulations of the Local Government Act.

In support of this application, the applicant has agreed to the following:

That as a bonus for increased density, the applicant will provide the following
contributions prior to issuance of a building permit:
1.   $750 towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund; and
2.   $2,850 toward the General Amenity Reserve Fund.
subject to reductions depending on use and height in accordance with the Affordable
Housing and Amenity Contribution Policy

The applicant will also provide $10.75 per square metre of commercial space towards
the General Amenity Reserve Fund prior to issuance of a building permit.

That prior to bylaw adoption, the applicant will register a section 219 covenant that
agrees to the following:

1. That full frontage improvements, a storm water management plan, and a
construction parking plan be provided and implemented to Bylaw 1000 standards to the
satisfaction of the Director of Engineering prior to issuance of building permit.
2. That all 6 properties associated with this rezoning be consolidated prior to issuance
of a Development Permit.
3. That onsite parking is allocated to each unit in accordance with the zoning bylaw.
4. That a strata plan is registered for each building prior to issuance of an occupancy
permit.
5. That 100% of the residential parking stalls are capable of providing Level 2 charging
for electric vehicles.

This proposal is consistent with the Official Community Plan 'City Centre' designation.

Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by the Local
Government Act.

The Mayor called a first time for presentations.

•   Matthew Moradian and Rachel Sansom provided a presentation on the proposed
    development on behalf of the applicant. The project would provide housing for 271
    families and commercial space in the centre of Langford, and is not requesting any
    variances. The project will be using carbon reduction technology in its concrete.
    Prices for homes will start under $400K.

•   Liisa Stewart - 2723 Peatt Road - Do not feel this development is reasonable for the
    neighbourhood. Have been negatively impacted by a four-storey development
    nearby and this would be worse. Support development of 4-6 stories.

•   Ryan Craycroft - 738 Walfred Road - Have 100+ employees, many of whom will not
    be able to get into the market without developments like this. Support this
    development, will house young families.

    Michael Biscoe - 2958 Sea Point Drive - Support this project.

    Resident - Willshire Drive - Some people are not able to find housing in Langford
    and have to commute.

    Matthew McKay- 780 Hockley Avenue - Support this development, support the job
    development and economic development created by this development. Many
    rental properties have a zero vacancy. We need more developments like this.
    People who live in dense areas are often able to walk to work and don't negatively
    impact traffic.

    Jacqueline Gintaut -1331 Ravensview Drive - Request that Council vote no to tall
    towers, which will set a negative precedent and compound existing traffic, parking,
    services, and infrastructure issues. There was not sufficient community consultation
    on this development or on the zoning bylaw that allowed developments of this
    height. Prefer a staged approach to development.

    Mary Wagner - 103-2669 Deville Road - Clarified that the carbon sequestering
    technology will be used in the concrete for this development. Do not support zones
    with no height limit, feel that the OCP needs more community input. Request more
    green space, would like the neighbourhood to be walkable.

•   David Fulko, 3035 Dorado Court - In favour of this development. Housing is needed
    right now, and it is better to go up than out, environmentally speaking. It is better
    to have more housing than prioritize traffic. It is appropriate to densify the city core,
    this will add energy, vibrancy, and support arts venues and local businesses. Taller
    buildings often have bigger setbacks and allow more space in the neighbourhood.

•   Anil Karim- Working with the developers to include quality child care within this
    development. The developers strongly support the effort to maximize equitable
    childcare spaces, which serve families who might not have access to quality
    childcare otherwise. Childcare is especially challenging for fast-growing cities, and
    this development is especially appropriate for childcare since it and Langford attract
    young families.

•   Robert Friend, 3024 Glen Lake Road - Employ 50 employees who live and work in
    Langford. Employees are getting pushed out of the city. Taller, dense projects are
    needed to support the growth in the city and families who want to stay in Langford.

•   Resident on 3207 Willshire Drive - Langford is a very fast-growing community. We
    need to house people and labour. People are sharing bedrooms and houses.
    Support this development.

•   Dana Elizabeth - 2850 Aldwynd Road - Support this project and density in the core.
    More homes will help facilitate growth, infrastructure, housing, and walkability.

•   Michael Sikich - 849 Homer Street - Will be marketing this development if it comes
    on the market. Langford is very desirable, which affects affordability. These tall,
    dense developments help address affordability and allow more people to achieve
    home ownership and a sense of pride and community. Taller developments reduce
    urban sprawl and allow more green space around the development.

•   Thai Tran - 2853 Crystal View Drive - Support this project for the affordability that it
    brings. Will set a positive precedent and make the downtown core more livable,
    walkable for young families.

•   Rosemary Turnowski - 837 Brock Avenue - This development would have a huge
    impact. Have worked hard for years to build a sense of community and get to know
    neighbours. Those in favour do not live near the proposed development, and it will
    affect the community. Will affect ability to garden, parking. Feel that this will blow
    up the community.

•   Bryce Wade - 19721 64th Avenue, Langley - Housing crisis requires projects like this.
    Thought he would never be able to afford housing in Vancouver, but working
    remotely will allow this. The only way to provide housing and avoid urban sprawl is
    to build up like this. This project is important for our community and economy.

•   Morgan Petrovic - 309-2717 Peatt Road - Will be impacted by the project since it is
    nearby, but fully support it. Despite potential annoyances, don't think the
    difficulties will be as bad as many believe. Think this will bring jobs for construction,
    local businesses. The centre of communities should grow, and Langford will become
    a bigger city.

•   Jackie Sheridan -1005 Golden Spire Crescent - Concerned about the height of the
    proposal and believe there may be issues with infrastructure for buildings over 6
    stories

              Mayor Young left the meeting at 7:17 pm.

•   Jackie Sheridan -1005 Golden Spire Crescent - believe that these will not allow
    young families to enter the housing market since all housing is unaffordable now.
    These buildings are not eco-friendly.

•   Layne Britton - 3022 Shoreview Drive - Support this project, it is vital for the
    downtown Langford core.

              Mayor Young returned to the meeting at 7:19 pm.

•   Layne Britton continued - Langford has become one of the most desirable places to
    live, and do not think this will negatively impact traffic and parking.

•   Mike, 953 Glen Willow Place - Support this project, this is more environmentally-
    friendly than urban sprawl. High-rise buildings are more energy-efficient than other
    developments. Love the plans.

•   Nicole Simpson - 4111 Mariposa Heights - Support this development. There is a
    housing crisis, and we need the hundreds of homes that would be provided by this
    development. Grew up in Langford and have watched it grow. Support Mayor and
    Council's vision.

•   Yazmin Hernandez - 2634 Sunderland Road - Sunderland Road - Feel the
    conversation about this development should not be about ''projects like these" but
    about this specific development, how it works in the context of the neighbourhood,
    and the merits of the proposal itself. There are not enough amenities like rapid

    transit and bike lanes. The ground floor should be active and dynannic instead of
    multiple levels of parking. Appreciate what Langford is doing to provide housing but
    feel that it is enough without this development.

•   Glen Kakoske -1715 Coronation Avenue - Joined out of interest and have no
    comments tonight.

    Isaac Mann - 2747 Scafe Road - A recent graduate and hoping to enter the market in
    a few years. In full support of this project. These units will be more affordable than
    other markets. Support the sustainable aspects of this development, like building
    vertically. Feel that concerns about traffic, fronting, shading have all been
    addressed by the proponents. Need to bring in and keep younger generations to
    communities in order to develop community amenities.

    Chris Newstead - 2732 Scafe Road - Request that Council not approve this
    development. 271 new units is six times the residences currently on the whole
    street. Traffic and parking are already bad and this will make it far worse. Less traffic
    per residence doesn't matter when overall the traffic will be far worse. Not enough
    parking for the number of units built. There will likely be overflow parking on the
    street. Neighbourhood is currently 1-2 storey homes. A 20+ story building will be
    incredibly out of place. Concerned about negative impacts to lifestyle, noise and
    privacy. Feel Council should prioritize existing residents over development.

•   Susie Hicks -2345 Lake End - Agree with previous callers who have voiced concerns
    with parking and traffic. Traffic to downtown Victoria is terrible. Feel there is not
    enough infrastructure, such as doctors, police, fire and ambulance to support
    current residents. Construction jobs will go away and Langford will be left with low-
    paying jobs. People will continue to have to commute to Victoria.

•   Laurie Plomp - 3592 Whimfield Terrace - Oppose development. This neighbourhood
    is not a good fit for tall towers. Parking ratio is insufficient and will contribute to
    conflict in neighbourhood. Traffic Impact Assessment should be provided to
    residents. More consultation with residents should be required, especially in
    developing greenspace. Request that the public hearing be adjourned until the
    greenspace is better developed.

•   Jordan Goldsmith - 3030 Washington Avenue - Grew up in Langford and have a lot
    of peers who are struggling to find housing. Fully support an opportunity for more
    young people to get into homes.

    Elizabeth Markus - 3262 Zapata Place - Ask Council to vote against this
    development. Council must do more community engagement to understand the
    vision of residents. Residents may not want Langford to become a more urban city.
    Residents have been left out of the process. This will forever change the character
    of Langford. Do not believe this development is environmentally-friendly. Feel high
    density and more environmentally-friendly developments can be achieved in 10-12
    storey buildings.

    Kim Robinson - 960B Paige Avenue - Agree with everyone who opposes this project.
    Do not agree 24 stories is appropriate for this neighbourhood. 10 stories would be
    more appropriate. Feel that residents will have no say once it is built.

      Mayor Young called a second time for presentations.

      None.

      Mayor Young called a third and final time for speakers. There being none, he declared
      the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 2009 closed at 7:51 p.m.

6.2   BYLAW NO. 2008


      The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 2008 at 7:51 pm.

      Director of Planning Matthew Baldwin advised that Matthew Moradian has applied on
      behalf of Langford Gateway Developments to amend the zoning of 2633 to 2647

      In support of this application, the applicant has agreed to the following:

      That as a bonus for increased density, the applicant will provide the following

      1. $750 towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund; and
      2. $2,850 toward the General Amenity Reserve Fund.
      subject to reductions depending on use and height in accordance with the Affordable
      Housing and Amenity Contribution Policy

      The applicant will also provide $10.75 per square metre of commercial space towards
      the General Amenity Reserve Fund prior to issuance of a building permit.

      That prior to bylaw adoption, the applicant will register a section 219 covenant that
      agrees to the following:

      1. That full frontage improvements, recommendations from the associated Traffic
      Impact Assessment, a storm water management plan, and a construction parking plan
      be provided and implemented to Bylaw 1000 standards to the satisfaction of the
      Director of Engineering prior to issuance of building permit.
      2. That all 11 properties associated with this rezoning be consolidated prior to
      issuance of a Development Permit.
      3. That onsite parking is allocated to each unit in accordance with the zoning bylaw.
      4. That a strata plan is registered for each building prior to issuance of an occupancy
      permit.
      5. That 100% of the residential parking stalls are capable of providing Level 2 charging
      for electric vehicles.

      This proposal is consistent with the Official Community Plan 'City Centre' designation.

      Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by the Local
      Government Act.

The Mayor called a first time for presentations.

•   Matthew Moradian and Rachel Sansom on behalf of Langford Gateway
    Developments.

           Councillor Blackwell left the meeting at 7:54 pm.

    Matthew Moradian and Rachel Sansom continued - This project will provide housing
    for 444 families on just over 2 acres of land and will provide 11 500 square feet of
    commercial and daycare space. Will provide approximately $2.6 million in park and
    amenity contributions and is requesting no variances. Housing 444 families in single
    family homes would require 111 acres of land.

           Councillor Blackwell returned to the meeting at 7:58 pm.

    Anais Holdaway -101-827 Arncote Avenue - Oppose this development. There was
    no meaningful engagement with area residents; don't feel residents were heard.
    Planning for people to behave differently (e.g. cycle or use transit) is not
    reasonable. Majority of people who live in this area work in Victoria and traffic is
    already bad. Appreciate that there will be daycare spots but would like to hear how
    many spaces will be available. This number of units may make the childcare
    situation worse. Would like Council to represent its residents.

    Yazmin Hernandez - 2634 Sunderland Road - Traffic Impact Assessments will never
    indicate a development is not appropriate, but this development will increase traffic
    and is inappropriate. 2.5 metre setbacks are minimal for a development of this size.
    Walkability only increases when amenities are provided and pedestrians are
    prioritized over vehicles. Most units will be 1-2 bedrooms, so this will not build the
    neighbourhood.

           Councillor Wade left the meeting at 8:16 pm.

    Tim Revino -101-1663 MacKenzie Ave - Have planning and density, and know
    people who are currently sharing small units with 5+ roommates and bunkbeds in
    each room. We need more density and housing right now. Fully support this project.

           Councillor Wade returned to the meeting at 8:19 pm

•   Matthew McKay - 784 Hockley Avenue - This is an exciting development, could be
    improved by a public plaza and public art. An art walk would be a great addition to
    Langford.

•   Jacqueline Gintaut -1331 Ravensview Drive - Agree with first two callers.

           Councillor Seaton left the meeting at 8:21 pm.

•   Jacqueline Gintaut continued - Request that Council vote no to tall towers, which
    will set a negative precedent and compound existing traffic, parking, services, and
    infrastructure issues. There was not sufficient community consultation on this
    development or on the zoning bylaw that allowed developments of this height.
    Prefer a staged approach to development.

             Councillor Seaton returned to the meeting at 8:24 pm. Mayor Young left the
                 meeting at 8:24 pm.

             Mayor Young returned to the meeting at 8:26 pm.

•   Mary Wagner -103-2669 Deville Road - Suggest having a significant plaza or corner

•   Michael Biscoe - 2958 Seapoint Drive - Support this development. First time

•   Warren Grey -15195 36th Ave Surrey, BC - Would like to move to Langford, support

•   Darlene Oudot - 105-827 Arncote Avenue - Invite Council to come to the

•   Wendy Hobbs - 3442 Luxton Road - Support the callers who are saying that there

•   Andrew Fox - 2634 Sunderland Road - Question the rosy picture that developers are

•   Acting Director of Corporate Services Marie Watmough - there will be

•   Laurie Plomp - 3592 Whimfield Terrace - The density will strongly impact the

      •   Isaac Mann - 2747 Scafe Road - Support this project. A lot of the issues brought up

      •   Ryan Craycroft - 738 Walfred Road - This development will help address

      •   Jason Mackenzie - 996 Cavalcade Terrace - Council should listen to current residents

      •   Acting Director of Corporate Services Marie Watmough - Correction, there is the
          possibility of 300-400 daycare spots.

      the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 2008 closed at 8:52 p.m.

6.3   BYLAW NO. 1992

      The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1992 at 8:52 pm.

      Director of Planning Matthew Baldwin advised that City of Langford staff have applied
      on behalf of City of Langford to amend the Zoning Bylaw No. 300 by updating the
      definitions for ''suites'' and "kitchens", adding a new definition for "public assembly and
      entertainment use", and refining Part 2 for enforceability purposes. These changes were
      initially left out of the spring omnibus (Bylaw 1944) while City Staff collaborated to
      ensure that Council and Departmental desires were incorporated.

      Bylaw 1992 proposes changes to Zoning Bylaw No. 300 Part 1 Definitions and Part 2
      General Provisions to allow for increased usability, education and enforcement of the
      Zoning Bylaw No. 300 for City Staff and the general public.

      As part of this application, a public hearing is required in accordance with the
      regulations of the Local Government Act.

      This proposal is consistent with the Official Community Plan

      Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by the Local
      Government Act.

      None.

      Mayor Young called a second time for presentations.

      None.

      Mayor Young called a third and final time for speakers. There being none, he declared
      the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1992 closed at 8:52 p.m.

6.4   BYLAW NO. 1931


The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1931 at 8:53 pm.

Director of Planning Matthew Baldwin advised that The City of Langford has applied to
annend the zoning of 1365 Goldstreann Avenue from the AM (Amenity) Zone to Area 5 -
Multi-Family of the CDl (Comprehensive Development 1 - Goldstream Meadows) Zone.

This is being proposed in order to allow for the development of a 6-storey multi-family
building.

As part of this application, a public hearing is required in accordance with the
regulations of the Local Government Act.

In support of these/this application, the applicant has agreed to provide the following:

1. That the applicant provides, as a bonus for increased density, the following
contributions per residential unit, prior to the issuance of a building permit:
a) $610 towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund; and
b) $3,660 towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund.
Subject to reductions depending on the use and height in accordance with the
Affordable Housing and Amenity Contribution Policy.

2. That the applicant provides, prior to bylaw adoption, a Section 219 covenant,
registered in priority of all other charges on title, that agrees to the following:
a) That parking stalls are allocated to individual units and visitors as required by the
Zoning Bylaw;
b) That a strata plan of the building is registered prior to occupancy;
c) That residential parking stalls are provided with Level 2 charging capabilities;
d) That the following are provided to Bylaw No. 1000 standards to the satisfaction of
the Director of Engineering prior to the issuance of a Building Permit:
i. Frontage improvements;
ii. A storm water management plan; and
iii. A construction parking and traffic management plan;

The applicant has provided a stormwater management memo, to the satisfaction of the
Director of Engineering, as required by Council.

The applicant has furthermore committed to providing 30% of the units in the proposed
development for sale through the City's new Attainable Home Ownership Program.

This proposal is consistent with the Official Community Plan Mixed Use Employment
Centre designation.

Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by the Local
Government Act

The Mayor called a first time for presentations.

•   Mary Wagner -104-2669 Deville Road - This will negatively impact the nearby trails.
    Any time the City gives up land, it has lost an opportunity to provide an amenity
    that benefits the entire community. This development will affect drainage and
    cause soil erosion. Even dead trees help absorb water. Request that Council make

    The transit for this area is not sufficient for the number of units. There is not
    enough information about the proposed design.

    Director of Planning and Subdivision Matthew Baldwin - Clarified that the public
    hearing is for a rezoning and details about the proposed building are not required at
    this time.

    Jacqueline Gintaut -1331 Ravensview Drive - Concerned that the number of
    buildings is different in the advertisement and the staff report. Concerned about
    traffic, parking and lack of meaningful community consultation. Previous
    correspondence for a previous proposal for this property was not included on the

    attainable. The attainable housing program will only be available to a very small
    number of residents with a relatively high income. This development will not
    benefit Langford residents.

    Suzanne Goudge - 2807 Lakeshore Place - Support green developments and density,

    walkability and has limited bus service, and will require people to drive. Location is
    on a dead-end road. With density, more density and greenspace is needed.

    Cindy Hickson - Lake End Road - Request that Council not approve this rezoning.

    enough parking. Concerned that new multi-use path is not safe. There is run-off

    Teresa Ackroyd, 325 Renart Place - Agree with previous speakers that this property

Mayor Young called a second time for presentations.

•   Karnal Cheema -102-792 Revilo Place - Moved to Langford to be closer to

           and enhanced rather than sold. Residents would like more inclusion in the

           Jacqueline Gintaut -1331 Ravensview Drive - Agree with previous caller, and feel

           greenspace is needed.

           Suzanne Goudge - 2807 Lakeshore Place - It is inappropriate to put a 6-storey
           building next to greenspace. Residents are concerned and ask for Council to listen

           Sienna Geary - 1375 Bear Mountain Parkway - Request that Council listen to the

           Jacqueline Gintaut -1331 Ravensview Drive - Feel that Council is not listening to
