existing_complete_replay.source_motion_text:
WHEREAS on December 5, 2022, Council considered a recommendation to name
        the Kettle Creek Linear Park and Playground after former Councillor Winnie
        Sifert in recognition of her long service to the City of Langford.

        AND WHEREAS Council determined that any decision regarding the naming of
        this park should be deferred until after the adoption of an amended or new park
        naming policy and that adoption has now occurred.

        AND WHEREAS a more suitable park has been identified to be named given its
        proximity to Winnie Sifert's neighbourhood,

        NOW THEREFORE, I move that Council rename Ernhill Park to "Winnie Sifert
        Park" and direct staff to work with former Councillor Sifert's family on a formal
        naming ceremony to be held prior to December 15, 2025.
existing_complete_replay.source_block:
MOVED BY: HARDER
        SECONDED: WAGNER

        WHEREAS on December 5, 2022, Council considered a recommendation to name
        the Kettle Creek Linear Park and Playground after former Councillor Winnie
        Sifert in recognition of her long service to the City of Langford.

        AND WHEREAS Council determined that any decision regarding the naming of
        this park should be deferred until after the adoption of an amended or new park
        naming policy and that adoption has now occurred.

        AND WHEREAS a more suitable park has been identified to be named given its
        proximity to Winnie Sifert's neighbourhood,

        NOW THEREFORE, I move that Council rename Ernhill Park to "Winnie Sifert
        Park" and direct staff to work with former Councillor Sifert's family on a formal
        naming ceremony to be held prior to December 15, 2025.

                                                                                Motion CARRIED.

             PRESENTATIONS



     4.1     Summary of Proposed 2023-2027 Five Year Financial Plan - Director of Finance

5.   PUBLIC PARTICIPATION

     R. Hobbs. Luxton Rd - re: item 6.1 - The speaker inquired about including a youth drop-in centre.
     Inquired about the the grant money being allocated for a youth centre.
     M. Dillabaugh, Director of Finance - responded that a youth centre could be an option for the
     funding.

     W. Hobbs. Luxton Rd - re: item 6.1 - The speaker inquired about the amenities. Inquired about
     the Road DCCs funding.

     M. Dillabaugh, Director of Finance - responded by explaining the Parks DCC's and the Road DCCs
     M. Wignall. Selwvn Rd - re: item 6.1 - The speaker commented on risk management in hiring fire
     fighters through an extended period of time. The speaker inquired why the City needs more
     staff. The speaker was concerned about the purchase of the YMCA.

     S. Hartlieb. Bombardier Cres - re: item 6.1 - The speaker inquired about a fire truck purchase
     being included in the budget. The speaker inquired about the Juan De Fuca recreation centre,
     and to which municipality is responsible for it. The speaker inquired about other municipalities
     contributing to the YMCA costs. The speaker thanked City staff for their presentation.

     S. Sifert. Waifred Rd - re: item 6.1 - The speaker is concern about the increase in tax rate. The
     speaker discussed amenity fees. The speaker would like the sewer connection fees to be
     lowered and amenity fees increased. The speaker is very concerned about a 12% tax increase.

     R. Barrea. Goldstream Ave - re: item 6.1 - The speaker is very concerned about the tax increase,
     and how it will affect the housing market.

     L. Foxall. Plavers Dr - re: item 6.1 - The speaker would like the tax increase 3-5%. The speaker
     would like the hiring of new Citystaff should be done over five years. The speaker believes the
     decrease in investments in the City, has affected the increase to property taxes. The speaker
     inquired about a contract being signed sooner with the YMCA. The speaker agrees with previous
     speakers regarding the fire budget. The speaker is very concerned about the tax increase and
     how it will affect those most vulnerable in the community.

     L. Plomp. Whimfield Terr - re: item 6.1 - The speaker thanked the Mayor, Council and City staff
     for including the public in the budget discussions. The speaker supports the increase in number
     of firefighters hired. The speaker had suggestions regarding budget savings. The speaker made
     suggestions for specific removal of line items being removed from the budget.

     M. Dillabaugh, Director of Finance - responded by explaining that the removal of the items
     would not affect the property tax rate.

     Nicholas Johal. Waifred PI - re: item 6.1 - The speaker inquired about the tax increase. The
     speaker inquired about the increase to City staff. The speaker supports the hiring of 4 new
     firefighters. The speaker is very concerned about the amount of the tax increase.

     M. Dillabaugh, Director of Finance - responded by explaining the budget for building permit
     revenue is the same as 2022.



B. Hutchins, Director of Corporate Services - responded by explaining that the increase staff
does not affect planning, engineering, or building. The added staff are for population growth to
the City.

B. Armstrong. Rodney Rd - re: item 6.1 - The speaker inquired about the road DCC's costs. The
speaker inquired about parks being funded.

M. Dillabaugh, Director of Finance - responded by explaining the borrowing of funds from Parks
DCC's does not mean they won't be paid back. That the money is used upfront then collected
when projects are completed. They explained that Parks DCC's has plenty of funding for it's own
projects.

S. Rossander. Ravensview Dr - re: item 6.1 - The speaker inquired about the revenues. The
speaker inquired about how confident the City is about the amount of non property revenues.
The speaker inquired if the City is on track with the expected revenues. The speaker compared
the revenues to expenditures and inquired where the money is.

M. Dillabaugh, Director of Finance - responded by that the City is confident based on trends.
That the City doesn't overstate revenues. They also responded that the City is on track with
expected revenues. The Director of Finance responded that that the funds are unaudited. If the
numbers are correct, the funds will then get added to the surplus at the end of the year.
W. Hobbs. Luxton Rd - re: item 6.1 - The speaker inquired about legal options of the contract
with YMCA. The speaker inquired about a referendum regarding funding the YMCA. The speaker
inquired about having other municipalities assist with funding the YMCA.

M. Dillabaugh, Director of Finance - responded by explaining the City is legally responsible for
the funding of the YMCA. Purchasing the YMCA is an option.

Nicholas Johal. Walfred PI - The speaker inquired about the proposed staff positions in the
budget.

Darren Kiedyk, CAO - responded that the staff positions descriptions will be made available in
the budget section of the City's website.

Braden Hutchins, Director of Corporate Services - responded by directing the speaker to a staff
report from the Committee of the Whole meeting, February 27, 2023.

M. Wignall. Selwvn Rd - re: item 6.1 - The speaker noted a discrepancy of line items of the
published budget report.

M. Dillabaugh, Director of Finance - responded that the total column does not impact anything.
They assured the speaker they would look into the error.

S. Sifert. Walfred Rd - re: item 6.1 - The speaker spoke to the amount of the increase of
firefighters. The speaker supports increasing the amount of police. The speaker inquired about
the proposed staff positions.

S. Rossander. Ravensview Dr - re item 6.1 - The speaker suggested that maybe there is a middle
ground solution for funding the YMCA.

N. Johal. Walfred PI - re: item 6.1 - The speaker concerned about the tax increase. The speaker
inquired about the YMCA, what is the cost of maintenance of the building. The speaker inquired



        how any developments have been approved since October 2022. The speaker inquired about a
        youth centre supporting the Guides and Scouts.

        Braden Hutchins, Director of Corporate Services - responded that the City is in preliminary
        stages of any decision regarding the YMCA.

6.      REPORTS

        6.1     2023 Budget and Five-Year Financial Plan 2023 - 2027

7.      ADJOURNMENT

existing_complete_replay.source_motion_text:
Council resolves that the City's share of funding for the Bellamy Road Multi-Use Path
             from Treanor Avenue to Bellany Link and Intersection Improvements on Veterans
             Memorial Parkway at Goldstream Avenue and Veterans Memorial Parkway at Peatt Road
             is available and supported, that these projects are a municipal priority, that these

             projects will be complete within the required timeline, that these proposed projects are
             shovel ready according to the criteria in section three of the infrastructure application.

             And therefore, Council direct staff to apply for the 2023 B.C. Active Transportation
             Infrastructure Grant for each of the following projects:

                 1.   Bellamy Road Multi-Use Path from Treanor Ave to Bellamy Link, at a total
                      estimated cost of $1,050,000;

             AND

                 2.   Intersection Improvements on Veterans Memorial Parkway at Goldstream
                      Avenue and Veterans Memorial Parkway at Peatt Road, at a total estimated cost
                      of $500,000.

            4.1    BYLAW NOS. 1989 and 1990

                   The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw Nos. 1989 and 1990 at 5:35 pm.

      Director of Planning Matthew Baldwin advised that Niall Paltiel of Ascend Planning Ltd.
      has applied on behalf of 1103097 BC Ltd. to amend the zoning of 1300 Valemount Court
      from Attached Housing (RM2A) Zone to the Business Park 2A (BP2A) Zone, and 1289,
      1277; 1265; 1253 Valemount Court from Rural Residential (RR5) to Business Park 2A
      (BP2A) to amend the Official Community Plan designation of the subject properties from
      Hillside or Shoreline to Business or Light Industrial to allow for business type uses to be
      developed on the property.

      1. In support of this application; the applicant has agreed to provide a section 219
      covenant, registered in priority of all other charges on title; the following prior to Bylaw
      Adoption:

      a. That the developer will connect and be responsible for any upgrades; connections
      and installation of services and utilities required to support the proposed development;
      to the standards of Bylaw No. 1000 and to the satisfaction of the Director of
      Engineering;

      b. That a formal storm water management plan is submitted and implemented prior to
      issuance of a building permit or subdivision approval, whichever is first; and
      implemented; as per Bylaw 1000, all to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering;

      c. That a construction parking and traffic management plan, prepared to the
      satisfaction of the Director of Engineering, be provided prior to the issuance of a
      building permit.

      This proposal is consistent with the proposed Official Community Plan "Business or Light
      Industrial" designation

      Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by the Local
      Government Act.


      Mayor Young called a first time for presentations.

      N. Paltiel; on behalf of the applicant - presented a Power Point summary of the
      proposed development.

      Mayor Young called a second time for presentations.

      None presented.

      Mayor Young called for a third and final time for presentations.

      L. Plomp, 3592 Whimfield Ter - Concerned that the area is heavily forested. Lack of
      amenities means there will be no money coming into the city. Concerned about
      industrial business in residential setting. Will there be property taxation? Ask Council to
      amend the proposal to address concerns.

      Mayor Young declared the Public Hearing for Bylaw Nos. 1989 and 1990 closed at 5:44
      p.m.

4.2   BYLAW NO. 1999


      The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1999 at 5:44 pm.

Director of Planning Matthew Baldwin advised that Ben Gulbrandsen has applied on
behalf of Jill Moores, Barry Moores, Janis Bayley, Lamar Grube, Patricia Van Buskirk,
Peter Van Buskirk, and Peter Lasell to amend the zoning of 2762, 2768, and 2774
Winster Road from the R2 (One- and Two-Family Residential) Zone to the CCl (City
Centre) Zone.

This is being proposed to allow for the development of a six-storey apartment building.

In support of this application, the applicant has agreed to provide the following as a
bonus for increased density:

a. $750 per unit to the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund; and
b. $2,850 per unit to the General Amenity Reserve Fund.

Subject to reductions depending on the use and height in accordance with the
Affordable Housing and Amenity Contribution Policy.

2. That the applicant also agrees to provide, prior to bylaw adoption, a Section 219
covenant, registered in priority of all other charges on title, that agrees to the following:

a. That frontage improvements, a stormwater management plan and a construction
parking and traffic management plan are provided to Bylaw 1000 standards to the
satisfaction of the Director of Engineering prior to the issuance of a Building Permit:

b. That the developer registers a strata plan, prior to the issuance of an occupancy
permit, that creates individual strata titles for each residential unit;

c. That a separate covenant be registered prior to issuance of a building permit for the
proposed residential building that ensures parking is allocated to each unit and visitors
as required by the zoning bylaw and is not provided in exchange for compensation
separate from that of a residential unit;

d. That 100% of residential parking spaces, excluding visitor parking spaces, shall
feature an energized outlet capable of providing Level 2 charging or higher to the
parking space; and

i. Energized outlets shall be labelled for the use of electric vehicle charging;
ii. Where an electric vehicle energy management system is implemented (load
sharing), a qualified professional may specify a minimum performance standard to
ensure a sufficient rate of electric vehicle charging; and
iii. The owner is required to keep the Electric Vehicle Servicing Equipment (EVSE) in
operation and the Strata Council may not prevent an owner, occupant, or tenant from
installing the EV charging equipment.

Council has also, by resolution, authorized the Director of Planning to issue a variance to
reduce the northern interior side lot line setback from the required 3m to 1.5m for a
stairwell within the Form and Character Development Permit.
This proposal is consistent with the Official Community Plan City Centre designation.

Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by the Local
Government Act.

Mayor Young called a first time for presentations.

B. Gulbrandsen, on behalf of the applicant - Pacific Viking Group has been a family
business since 2003. Projects are based on the OCP. Realizes that Council must weigh
the concerns of the community. An increase of inventory is what's needed in the City of
Langford. Architect Alan Lowe has designed the building.

A. Lowe; Architect, on behalf of the applicant - presented a Power Point summary of the
proposed development.

Councillor Szpak inquired about bicycle storage.

M. Rogers. 2711 Windman Ln - 3 concerns to Concerns about of traffic in the area, six
storeys is too high. Finally, tree protection. Curious about what will happen to the trees?
Question for Watt Consulting. What determines a significant impact on traffic?

P. Frigga. 1010 Graphite PI - Supports the project, that more affordable housing is
needed.

G. Sinclair. 689 Hoffman Ave. - Feels the local residents are not being heard. Would like
to see the traffic assessment. Wants to know why the public doesn't have access to
them. What is the proposal to save trees? The construction will impact the area.

C. Miller 552 Hoffman Ave. - Would like to submit their opposition to the proposal.
Committee ignored the concern to lower the height of the development. The area will
have added traffic. Believes it is unsafe in the area. Did the traffic assessment consider
all the traffic in the area? difficult to turn out of the area. Not enough on street parking.
Neighboring schools are at capacity.

J. Rol, 2779 Winster Ave. - Echoes the previous callers concerns. Believes that a six-
storey building it too much capacity for the area. Is there a loading zone provided?
Actively selling his home after 30 years.

L. Shaw. 2739 Winster Rd - Cornered about the amount of increased traffic to the area.
Street parking is unavailable.

S. Russel, 2593 Millstream Rd - In favour of the project. Is in the downtown core. Will be
adjacent to amentias. Families need access to housing.

M. McKav, 605-784 Hocklev Ave - Commends Council for considering development. The
developer is building nice structures. We need densification in the core.

S. Gearv, 1375 Bear Mountain Pkwv - Echoes local residents concerns. No affordable
housing has been added to the market from Langford. Concerned about outside support
to the area development and local residents not being heard.

A. Churchill. 658 Atkins Ave - Echoes the concerns of the local residents. Has
communicated with City staff about the development. Believes the development is too
big, Traffic will only increase. Why is the traffic assessment not available to the public?
What does significant impact mean? Believes the development is not in the City Centre
Zone. Not enough street parking available.

Scott. 1251 Flint Ave - In full support of this project. Believes in affordable housing.
Believes social, local connections are stronger by attracting new businesses. Likes having
owner owned housing. But City needs more supply for renters. Regarding a dedicated

left turn signal could help with traffic. Sustainable housing will allow more affordable
housing.

R. Cravcroft. 738 Waifred Rd - Supports the projects. Likes all the bicycle parking
available. The upgrades to the area will be welcome. Commended Council for their
work.

N. Duvf, 689 Hoffman Ave - Lives beside the development. The area is busy with traffic.
The infrastructure in area is failing. Parking is unavailable in the area. Possibly build
something with a lower density. Would like details of the traffic assessment. Has
concerns about the trees being removed. There were no changes made from the
Committee recommendations.

Watts Consulting responded - Regarding the traffic assessment, followed industry
standards. Did an a.m. and p.m. assessment of the traffic. Explained the grading system
that is used in traffic assessments.

H. Webber. #405-110 Huxlev PI - Supports the development, as it will help supply a
housing shortage.

M. Wignall. #202-774 Goldstream Ave - Has watched the community grow. Asking
Council that if six storeys too tall for City core? Its going to be the perfect place. Schools
will be built based on the growth of the area. We need to accommodate the demand.

L. Faulkner. 2707 Windman Ln - Is a teacher in the area. Concern is the proximity of
another development. There are not enough exits out of the area. Access to the school
is difficult. Condominiums are not an option for families.

A. Schultz, 552 Hoffman Ave - Echoes the other callers concerns. Does the traffic
assessment consider of the growth to the area? Believes six storeys is too high for the
area.


A. Thompson. 650 Hovlake Ave - Caller is not a resident in the area. But sees the traffic
to the area. Unsure of the affordable phrase, doesn't meant the same to everyone. No
place for rapid transit. Does not support the rezoning.

R. Coutrev, #205-847 Goldstream Ave. - Supports the development. The downtown core
has been designed with thought and time over several years. Wishes Council to stay on
the path to grow the downtown area. There is a huge demand for housing. The Official
City Plan states the demand and where the housing should be. The region is growing,
housing is needed. Road improvements are being done. There is plenty of recreation
based on the contributions from development.

M. Wagner #104-2669 Deville Rd - There is no shortage of people wanting to move here.
But growth should be done in a thoughtful way. Keep up with the amenities available to
those here. Putting too many people in small space. Wants to make sure there is
greenspace available and livable space. Wants more public consultation. Wants
construction times limited.

S Gearv, 1375 Bear Mountain Pkwv - Can't undo something that has already been done.
Caller supports density. Believes the infrastructure is not available for this development.

      C. Harder, 844 Goldstream Ave. - Echoes the previous callers concerns. The building
      density is too large for the area. Pleased about the bike storage. Concerned about the
      pace of development.

      Mayor Young called a second time for presentations.

      C. Burg. 615 Hoffman Ave. - Caller is not in favour of the development. What time in the
      a.m. and p.m. was the traffic assessment done? Concerned about amount of traffic. At
      what time does a traffic assessment affect a development?

      Mayor Young responded - asked staff a question about the traffic light near the
      development.

      Michelle Mahovlich; Director of Engineering and Public Works, responded - We can
      request the traffic timing be changed by the Ministry of Transportation. A traffic
      roundabout will be developed in the area.

      L. Plomp, 3592 Whimfield Ter - Opposes the development. Believes the changes that
      were requested by Planning, Zoning and Affordable Housing Committee, were not
      satisfied. Believes that the Engineering Department's plans will not mitigate traffic
      concerns. Believes that the development is already approved before Public Hearing.

      A. AAron. #401-2745 Veterans Memorial Pkwv. - Traffic is heavy in the area. How many
      cars were counted during the traffic assessment?

      N. Duvf, 689 Hoffman Ave. - Concern about the proposed traffic circle.

      L. Faukner, 2707 Windman Ln - Concern about the roundabout proposal.

      Mayor Young called for a third and final time for presentations. There being none, he
      declared the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1999 closed at 7:23 p.m.

4.3   BYLAW NO. 2017


      The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 2017 at 7:23 pm.

      Director of Planning Matthew Baldwin advised that Dan Robbins has applied on behalf
      of Ramar Langford Holdings to amend the zoning of 791 and 795 Revilo Place and 2931
      Phipps Road from the 'One-and Two-Family Residential' Zone to the 'City Centre 1'

      This is being proposed in order to allow for the development of a residential building
      with approximately 109 units.

      In support of this application, the applicant has agreed to provide the following as a

      1. $750 per unit to the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund; and

      subject to reductions depending on use and height.

building permit.

Plan.

Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by the Local

Mayor Young called a first time for presentations.

K. Cheema, #107-792 Revilo PI - The development will remove a number of mature
trees. Supports densification and increased housing to the City. However, can not
support the application for the development. Due to a decrease in available sunlight,
displace local habitats, parking concerns, increased traffic issues and safety to the area.

Mayor asked staff a question about changing the shape og the building.

Matthew Baldwin; Director of Planning, responded - that the change is possible but not
ideal.

Councillor Szpak asked staff a question regarding natural grass or turf be used in the
courtyard.

Matthew Baldwin; Director of Planning, responded - that the final design has not been
presented as of yet. Also, that the number of trees to be removed has not been
determined as well.

M. Wagner. #104-2669 Deville Rd - Echoes concerns about the removal of trees and the
effects to environment. Would like the developers to save as many trees as possible.

D. Serrao. 792 Revilo PI - Would like the zoning to remain the same. Concerned about
the size of the building, it will remove access to the sunlight. Concerned about the safety
of children on the street due to an increase of traffic. Concerned about the density of
the building. What is the loading zone availability? Would prefer townhomes be built
instead.

C. Harder. 844 Goldstream Ave - Echoes the concerns of the other callers. Would like the
zoning to stay the same. Would like protection of the trees.

K. Cheema. #107-792 Revilo PI - Believes the development should be townhouses.
Would like a lower density building made.

      Mayor Young called a second time for presentations.

      None presented.

      Mayor Young called for a third and final time for presentations. There being none, he
      declared the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 2017 closed at 7:50 p.m.

      The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 2026 at 7:56 pm.

Director of Planning Matthew Baldwin advised that Sherri Davies and Dawn Exiey have
applied to amend the zoning of 661 Hoylake Avenue from the R2 (One- and Two-Family

In support of this application, the applicant has agreed to provide the following as a

1. That the applicant also agrees to provide, prior to Bylaw Adoption, a Section 219

Council has also, by resolution, authorized the Director of Planning to issue the following

Government Act.

Mayor Young called a first time for presentations.

A. Thompson. 650 Hovlake Rd - Lives in the area of the development. Opposed to the
development. Concerned about lack of street parking. Concerns about increase of
traffic. Concerned about school capacity.

W. Peereboom; Development Designer, - on behalf of the applicant presented a Power
Point summary of the proposed development.

      Mayor Young called a second time for presentations.

      A. Thompson, 650 Hoylake Rd - Concerned about the design and landscaping of the
      building. Concern about the street parking available.

      A. Braid. 655A Hovlake Rd - Oppose the development. Concern about the traffic in
      school zone. Concerns about traffic congestion. Would like to see something smaller
      built.

      Mayor Young called for a third and final time for presentations. There being none, he
      declared the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 2026 closed at 8:08 p.m.

4.6   BYLAW NO. 2030


      The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 2030 at 8:08 pm.

      Director of Planning Matthew Baldwin advised that Rachael Sansom of Grayland
      Consulting Ltd. has applied on behalf of Bev and Sherri Befus to amend the zoning of
      902 Walfred from Rural Residential 5 (RR5) Zone to Residential Small Lot 1 (RSI) Zone to
      allow for a bare land strata subdivision of approximately 13 lots.

      1. In support of this application, the applicant has agreed to provide as a bonus for
      increased density, the following contributions prior to subdivision approval:

      a.   $600 per small Lot to the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund;
      b.   $3960 per small lot to the General Amenity Reserve Fund; and
      c.   $1,000 per lot 550 m2 or more in area to the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund;
      d.   $6,000 per lot 550 m2 or more in area to the General Amenity Reserve Fund.
      2. In support of this application, the applicant has agreed to the following, secured by
      a section 219 covenant, registered in priority of all other charges on title prior to bylaw
      adoption:

      a. That full frontage improvements and a stormwater management plan will be
      provided and implemented to Bylaw 1000 Standards and to the satisfaction of the
      Director of Engineering prior to subdivision approval or the issuance of a building
      permit, whichever comes first;

      b. That a Construction Parking and Traffic Management Plan will be provided to the
      satisfaction of the Director of Engineering prior to any alteration of the land;

      c. That vegetation within the road allowance on Walfred Road is to be retained,
      however if any vegetation is removed, the applicant is required to replant the area and
      provide a temporary irrigation system from a private irrigation system to the satisfaction
      of the Manager of Parks.

      d. That a non-disturbance covenant be registered over 31% of the land to be protected
      as open space on strata common property prior to subdivision approval, to the
      satisfaction of the Approving Officer.

      This proposal is consistent with the proposed Official Community Plan "Hillside or
      Shoreline" designation


      Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by the Local
      Government Act.

      Mayor Young called a first time for presentations.

      Rachael Sansom - The applicant presented a Power Point summary of the proposed
      development.

      S. Geary, 1375 Bear Mountain Pkwv - Impressed by the proposal. Concern about
      maintenance of mature trees have been alleviated by the presentation. What is the
      estimate of removal of mature trees?

      M. Wagner. #104-2669 Deville Rd - Appreciated the presentation. Would like a better
      relationship between neighbours and developers.

      Mayor Young called a second time for presentations.

      None presented.

      Mayor Young called for a third

      A. Miller. 906 Walfred Ave - Appreciates the relationship with the applicant. Concern
      about the drainage issues in the area. Will there be a greenspace covenant carried over
      to a new owner?

      Matthew Baldwin; Director of Planning, responded - The covenant will be registered and
      carries along with the property. It will only be changed if presented at a new public
      hearing.

      E. Marcus. 3262 Zapata PI - Concern about changes to the property. Would like more
      information available to the public.

      Mayor Young called a final time for presentations. There being none, he declared the
      Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 2030 closed at 8:29 p.m.

4.7   BYLAW NO. 2032

      The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 2032 at 8:29 pm.

      Director of Planning Matthew Baldwin advised that Rachael Sansom has applied on
      behalf of Richard Hoogendoorn, Cheri Crause, and Lorrine Nygaard to amend the zoning
      of 2822, 2824, and 2828 Jacklin Road from the 'One- and Two-Family Residential' Zone
      to the 'City Centre Pedestrian' Zone.

      This is being proposed in order to allow for the development of a mixed-use building
      with approximately 88 units.

      In support of this application, the applicant has agreed to provide the following as a
      bonus for increased density:

      1.   $750 per unit to the Affordable Housing Fund; and
      2.   $2,850 per unit to the General Amenity Reserve Fund

      subject to reductions depending on use and height; and


3.   $10.75 per square metre of commercial space to the General Amenity Reserve
Fund.

Prior to bylaw adoption, the applicant will register a section 219 covenant that agrees to
the following:

1.   That all three subject properties be consolidated prior to issuance of a Development
Permit;
2. That a separate covenant be registered prior to issuance of a building permit to
ensure parking is allocated to each unit;
3. That a strata plan is registered for the building prior to issuance of an occupancy
permit;
4.   That 100% of residential parking stalls are capable of providing Level 2 charging for
electric vehicles;
5. That full frontage improvements, a storm water management plan; and a
construction parking management plan be provided and implemented to Bylaw 1000
standards to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering prior to issuance of a
building permit.

This proposal is consistent with the 'City Centre' designation of the Official Community
Plan.

Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by the Local
Government Act.

Mayor Young called a first time for presentations.

Rachael Sansom - The applicant presented a Power Point summary of the proposed
development.

V. Smith. 2482 Jacklin Rd - In favour of the proposal. The proximity to Leigh Rd is
beneficial to get to the highway. Walking distance to parks. Contributions to local
amenities will help the community.

M. Reimers, #103-2821 Jacklin Rd - In support of growth in the community that is line
with the area. Concern about

school capacity. Concern about the lack of parking in the area. Would like the height of
the building lowered.

J. Mulleson. 894 Hocklev Rd - Feels there is too much development. Feels Council has
abandoned its current residents. How will this development help the community?

A. Thompson. 650A Hovlake Ave. - Schools are not parks. Area is not walkable.

L. Plomp 3592 Whimfield Ter - Concerned the development could overshadow
neighbouring homes. Would like Council to have a firm restriction to height of the
building.

M. Wagner #104-2669 Deville Rd - Concerns about the amount of development being
done. Concern about lack of greenspace. Would like a firm height of the development.


             R. Cravcroft, 738 Walfred Rd - Supports the development. Needed to prevent urban
             sprawl.

             Mayor Young called a second time for presentations.

             J. Mulleson, 894 Hocklev Ave - Echo comments regarding schools are not parks. Concern
             about a lack of greenspace. Concern about the walkability of the City.

             J. Gordon, 2329 Belair Rd - Supports the development. Believes it ill bring more
             amenities to the area. In order to save greenspace, we have to move up.

             Mayor Young called for a third and final time for presentations. There being none, he
             declared the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 2032 closed at 8:50 p.m.

     L. Plomp, 3592 Whimfield Ter - Item 6.1; Believes the public should have been consulted.

13.   NOTICE OF MOTION

      Notice of Motion from Councillor Guiry

      Whereas Rick Hansen Foundation Accessibility CertificationTM (RHFAC) is a national rating system
      that measures and certifies the level of meaningful access of buildings and sites and the Rick
      Hansen Foundation found that 64% of Canadians have a disability or take care of a person with a
      disability.

      And whereas, one of the key findings of a 2020 Cost Comparison Feasibility Study issued by
      HCMA Architecture + Design was that when meeting the National Building Code there was a cost

      increase of 1% to achieve Rick Hansen Foundation Certified Gold which reinforces that
      "accessibility can be achieved with minimal cost impact through commitment to
      thoughtful/universal design".

      Therefore, Langford Council directs staff to consider Rick Hansen Foundation Accessibility
      CertificationTM (RHFAC) when completing the upcoming review of Langford's Design Guidelines
      and through this process consider a possible timeline for adopting RHFAC as a standard for all
      new buildings in Langford.

                 c. That Section 6.95.05 be varied to allow an accessory building to be located
                    within the rear yard that abuts a golf course.

             Subject to the following terms and conditions:

                 i.   That the variances pertain only to the existing structure;

                 ii. That the applicant shall include screening plantings between the shed and the
                     property line, to the satisfaction of the Director of Development Services; AND

                 iii. That the second accessory shed on the property be removed.

                                                                                         Motion DEFEATED.

                                        Mayor Goodmanson, Councillors Morley and Wagner opposed.

             Councillor Harder returned to the meeting at 9:10 pm.
